articleTitle: Exploring Magnon–Magnon Coupling, Spin Hall Magnetoresistance, and Laser–Driven Spin Textures in 2D van der Waals Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We have demonstrated ultrastrong magnon–magnon coupling in the gigahertz (GHz) band in a two–dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnet, achieving a maximum normalized coupling strength of 0.5. Our investigation revealed that the coupling strength can be tuned by temperature and by magneto–crystalline anisotropy. Additionally, we presented spin Hall magnetoresistance in a 2D vdW antiferromagnetic–based device, illustrating the potential to exfoliate 2D antiferromagnets into thin layers and manipulate their magnetization through spin currents. Finally, we showed that laser excitation can generate different type of spin textures at room temperature and zero–field in a 2D vdW ferromagnet. These findings provide an ideal platform for development of magnonic quantum and spintronics devices based on 2D magnets.

articleTitle: Dimension-Dependent Critical Scaling Analysis and Emergent Competing Interaction Scales in a 2D Van der Waals Magnet Cr2Ge2Te6
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We investigate thickness-dependent phase transition from a paramagnetic to ferromagnetic phase in Cr2Ge2Te6 (CGT) in its bulk and few-layer flake forms. 2D Ising-like critical transition in bulk CGT occurs at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{c}}=\mathbf{67}\ \mathbf{K}$</tex> with out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy. Few-layer CGT on hBN/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si substrate displays the same <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{c}}$</tex> but additionally exhibits a new critical transition at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{c}}^{\prime}=\mathbf{14.2}\ \mathbf{K}$</tex>. Here, scaling analysis reveals that the critical exponents differ significantly from those in bulk and do not align with the known universality classes. Our Density Functional Theory (DFT) and classical calculations indicate competition between magneto-crystalline and dipolar anisotropy emerges with reduced dimensions. The observed behavior is due to minor structural distortions in low dimensional CGT, which modify the balance between spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions and dipolar anisotropy. This triggers a critical crossover at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{c}}^{\prime}$</tex>. Our study shows the emergence of a complex interplay of short- and long-range interactions below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{c}}^{\prime}$</tex> as CGT approaches the 2D limit.

articleTitle: Localization of a Crack in Moving Cylindrical Ferromagnetic Rods by Measuring the Fourier Coefficients of the Leakage Magnetic Flux
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Electromagnetic nondestructive inspection for high-speed moving ferromagnetic materials is necessary for manufacturing efficiency. In this paper, we present a novel leakage magnetic flux (LMF) method to estimate the crack position in a moving cylindrical ferromagnetic rod. The method directly measures the first-order Fourier coefficients of the LMF moving with the crack by using only two coils with DC excitation. The location of a crack is estimated by the proposed method, as demonstrated for an S45C cylindrical rod.

articleTitle: Magnetic Coupling on Multilayer of NdFeB/Dy Films Grown by Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work, we study the influence of Dy through grain boundary diffusion (GBD) on multilayer NdFeB/Dy thin films produced by magnetron sputtering. The Samples were grown with structure Si/Ta/[Dy(t)/NdFeB(t)]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>/Ta, where t represents thicknesses t = 50, 25, 12.5 nm, and N represents the number repetitions of Dy/NdFeB. NdFeB and Dy layers were deposited at 600°C, while the Ta(50nm) layers, were deposited at room temperature. The choice of high-temperature deposition was made to favor the growth of the Nd2Fe14B phase with high uniaxial anisotropy along the c-axis. X-ray diffraction and magnetometry measurements reveal the effects of interdiffusion of Dy at the interfaces and the grain boundaries of NdFeB, resulting in a significant increase in magnetic anisotropy along the C axis compared to a reference sample under the same conditions without Dy. Hysteresis loops demonstrate a magnetic coupling competition between Nd/Fe phases due to the increased interdiffusion of Dy, contributing to a distribution of coercive fields in FORC diagrams. These processes are important for understanding the effect of GBD and for permanent magnet applications.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Extended Landau Theory Method for the Coercivity Analysis of Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The Ginzburg-Landau theory was used to analyze the mechanism that determines magnetic properties from information on the magnetic domain structure of magnetic materials. The Ginzburg-Landau theory enables the analysis of free energy landscape using magnetization as an order parameter. In this study, we extend the Ginzburg-Landau theory to directly link magnetic properties and magnetic domain structure by incorporating data science into the theoretical framework. This enables a data-driven analysis of the coercivity mechanism. The features extracted from the magnetic domain structure were used as new order parameters to connect the data space with the original physical space. Magnetic properties were then derived from the free energy landscape visualized in data space. As a result, we proposed a method in which variables and formulas in the data space are easily interpretable as physical quantities and the theory can be easily generalized.

articleTitle: Hysteresis and Kinetics of the First-Order Phase Transition: Losses in Magnetocaloric Effect Illustrated on the Ni-Mn-Ga-Cu
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The hysteresis that usually accompanies the first-order phase transition and its kinetics causes efficiency losses in any cyclical refrigeration processes. Establishing the correlation between time and hysteresis could provide insight into this issue. This study presents experimental results on the evolution of magneto-induced structures under different thermodynamic conditions and cycling in a magnetic field, and the subsequent effect on the magnetocaloric effect for the NhMno.74Cuo.26Ga Heusler alloy. The study reveals the impact of the evolution of the magneto-induced structural subsystem on the irreversibility of the magnetocaloric effect near the first-order magnetostructural transition. The presence of residual martensite, formed during the initial magnetization of the sample, is identified as the cause of the irreversibility of the magnetocaloric effect. The results demonstrate the difference in the course of the martensitic transition in adiabatic and isothermal conditions. It also highlights the dependence of the nucleation of the martensitic phase and the movement of the boundaries of the new phase on the magnetic field sweep rate.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Transport Properties in Ion-Irradiated $\text{Cr}_{2}\text{AlC}$
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The presence of open-volume defects, such as vacancies, can significantly alter the functional properties of a material, including its structure and electronic transport. This study employs ion irradiation using inert ions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Ar}^{+})$</tex> and transition metal ions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Co}^{+})$</tex> at fluences of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{12}-10^{15}\text{ions}\cdot \text{cm}^{-2}$</tex> to achieve systematic disorder in the multilayer structure of MAX-phase <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cr}_{2}\text{AlC}$</tex>. It is shown that the magnitude of the paramagnetic response of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cr}_{2}\text{AlC}$</tex> increases with ion fluence, regardless of the dopant used. A combination of isolated moments in defect sites with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{J}={1/2}$</tex> and magnetic clusters are used to explain this behavior. Low-temperature (< 30 K) resistivity measurements show local minima and sudden up(down)-turns with decreasing temperature, which, together with unusual MR in this temperature range, suggest the presence of quantum transport effects, such as the Kondo effect.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic Neural Stimulation and Spintronic Neural Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We report our team's recent magnetic biomedical brain-related research work: 1) micromagnetic neural stimulation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{MS})$</tex>; 2) calculation of magnetic field generated by neural cells and tissues and spintronic neural sensing. First, the designing, fabrication, and testing of two micromagnetic implants - the Magnetic Pen (MagPen), a solenoid-shaped single <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{coil}$</tex> prototype, and the Magnetic Patch (MagPatch), a rectangular helix-shaped planar <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{coil}$</tex> array prototype, is discussed. The efficacy of micromagnetic activation using MagPen has been successfully tested over many rodent models. The MagPen prototype had its caveat in terms of mm-size, lack of multidimensional spatial control and activation at the cellular-level. To bridge this research gap, the MagPatch array was designed and fabricated to study <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{MS}$</tex> at the single-cell resolution. Second, we used FEM exemplary models and open-source computational libraries and calculated the magnetic fields generated by individual neurons and neuronal networks at micrometer distances. Our results show that the magnetic field generated by a single-neuron action potential can be detected by ultra-high sensitivity sub-pT magnetic field sensors, which opens the door to future in vivo decoding of neuronal activities through neural networks. Room temperature, high endurance, small volume and low power make spintronic sensors one of the promising candidates for neural sensing. On this aspect, the recent experimental progress for the spintronic sensors for neural sensing has been reviewed, with a specific discussion on our effort on spintronic stack design, device fabrication and detection.

articleTitle: Position Estimation Method of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Moving Horizon Estimation EKF algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Extended Kalman filter (EKF) is widely applied in the position estimation algorithm for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). However, the estimation accuracy will be degraded, when measurement noise is not O-mean white noise. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an EKF algorithm with moving horizon estimation (MHE) to estimate the rotor position of PMSM more accurately. The proposed MHE EKF algorithm uses the concept of a moving time domain window to estimate the motor operating status by integrating the window information of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> moments. By establishing a cost function and adding random noise to replace the measurement error, the prediction problem is transformed into an optimization problem. Simulation and experiment results show that this algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of estimation position.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of High Frequency Air Gap Flux Density Harmonics by Frozen Permeability Method in Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper introduces a fast calculation of high frequency air gap flux density harmonics in electrical machines, using the frozen permeability technique. This approach can rapidly and efficiently evaluate the amplitude of harmonic flux density components due to PWM in electrical machines. This method combines electrical equivalent circuits and the finite element approach, furthermore operating conditions and magnetic saturation can be taken into account. A comparison with transient FEM simulation is performed to validate the reliability of this fast calculation. The findings confirm that the fast calculation method can provide accurate results and truly reduce computation time from a few hours to minutes.

articleTitle: Influence of Leakage Inductance of a Transformer Operating in a DC Resistance Welding Machine on Welding Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The paper is focused on analysis of properties of power electronic transformer operating at resistance welding machine with frequency of 10 kHz and its influence on commutation process in output rectifier. Recently, the most popular resistance welding systems in industrial processes are based on DC welding machines with power electronic inverters. Such systems has numerous advantages for resistance welding, but because of very high welding current, power electronic converters are very sensitive on leakage inductance of the transformer. So, the output transformer, having output current at a level of 10 kA or more, needs special design to minimize the leakage inductance. Analysis in the paper is based on existing resistance welding system and shows in qualitative and quantitative way influence of leakage inductance on the output current of the welding machine. Also some technological aspects are discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of Electromagnetic Stirring During the Solidification on the Structure and Magnetic Properties of 2 % Si Electrical Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The influence of strand electromagnetic stirring (S-EMS) during the solidification in continuous casting process on the structure and magnetic properties of a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>Si non-oriented were analyzed in this study. Hot bands samples were obtained by hot rolling in a Steckel mill with two slabs containing equiaxed grains ratios 15.08% and 45.81 %. In the laboratorial work, the samples were processed without and with hot band annealing at 1000 °C, followed by cold rolling to final thickness of 0.50 mm and final annealing process at temperatures from 860°C to 1100 °C. The results showed that no significant differences were observed on the hot band and final grain sizes with and without use ofS-EMS, except after hot band annealing, where the sample with use ofS-EMS showed abnormal grain growth. Additionally, the use of S-EMS improved the J50, from 1.77 T to 1.79 T at 1100 °C. The hysteretic losses has decreased around 1.1 W/kg and the anomalous losses has increased around 0.6 W/kg as the final grain sizes rises from 50 um to 250 um for both S-EMS conditions. These results suggest that the use of S- EMS improves the final texture due to the presence higher volume of the fibers influencing positively the magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Sensorless Magnetization Current Control for Stable Connection and Separation of Electropermanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: An electropermanent magnet (EPM) can be connected to and separated from ferromagnetic materials by reversing a magnetization state of an AlNiCo magnet. This paper proposes a sensorless magnetization current control for a stable operation of the EPM. Its state of connection and separation is estimated from an induced voltage in the EPM's coil. A current phase control is constructed by detecting a positive-going zero crossing of the induced voltage.

articleTitle: Effect of Binder Content on Structure and Magnetic Properties of Fe-Si Powder Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The structure and magnetic properties of Fe- 3.5 wt.% Si (Fe-Si) powder core with different binder contents were investigated. A similar structure of Fe-Si powder cores with mainly A2 phase was confirmed regardless of the binder content. As the binder content increased, both the saturation magnetization and the initial real part of permeability decreased with the density, which was related by the filling degree of the core. The lowest core loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{P}_{\mathbf{cv}}$</tex> was observed in the powder core with a binder content of 1.0 wt.%. These results suggest that a higher binder content can improve the resistivity of the powder core and insulate the particles, resulting in the lower eddy current loss and, consequently, lower core loss in the high frequency range. Therefore, Fe-Si powder core can be considered for applications in higher frequency range, which were not explored before.

articleTitle: Restoration of Magnetic Order in Heavy Metal Doped Spin Glass
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A systematic evolution of 4d-element triggered restoration of long-range magnetic order in a spin glass compound Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>NiGe, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{M n}_{0.7} \mathbf{Fe}_{0.3-x} \mathbf{Rh}_{x}\mathbf{NiG}$</tex>, will be reported in detail with the help of x-ray diffraction, bulk magnetization and ac-susceptibility measurements. The variation of lattice parameters, Mn-Mn bond lengths in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{ab}$</tex> -plane and along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{c}$</tex> -direction with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> will be determined by analysing the room temperature x-ray diffraction patterns, complying with Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>In-type hexagonal structure. In order to uncover the type of spin-glass behaviour, the frequency-dependent ac-susceptibility cusp and relative shift in the freezing temperature will be analysed. Sherrington-Kirkpatrick criterion will be employed to understand the magnetic correlations with increasing Rh concentration. Origin of ferromagnetism in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{x}=\mathbf{0}.\mathbf{3}$</tex>, possible exhibition of exchange bias (field cooled or zero-field cooled) in spin glass compounds of the series will be examined. Additionally, the effect of hydrostatic pressure on the spin-glass compounds will be investigated with an intent to restore the ferromagnetism by affecting the Mn-Mn distance.

articleTitle: High Frequency Response of Magnetically Coupled Co/Cu/CoFeB Trilayers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Engineering the magnetic behaviour of stacks of ferromagnetic and non-magnetic thin films is mainly controlled by the anisotropy of individual layers plus the interlayer exchange coupling constant. In this context, Co/Cu/CoFeB trilayers with different Cu layer thicknesses were fabricated and the magnetization reversal processes, the interlayer coupling, the FMR frequencies and the damping parameters were studied. Their acoustic and optic modes, combined with their related damping parameters have been analyzed as a function of the Cu layer thickness. Particularly, the resonance frequency of the optic mode is very sensitive to the interlayer coupling constant that allows us to conclude that high resonance frequencies (i.e., above 25 GHz) can be achieved for ferromagnetically coupled bilayers with an interlayer exchange coupling like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${J}_{{eff}}=({2.7}\pm \mathbf{0.8})\ \mathbf{erg}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>.

Author Keywords: FMR acoustic and FMR optic modes

articleTitle: Producing High-Ratio Nanowires by Pressure-Induced Infiltration into Anodized Aluminum Oxide Nanoporous Template
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work aims to optimize the uniformity and filling factor of intermetallic nanowire arrays produced by the metallic flux nanonucleation into anodized aluminum oxide (AAO) templates. This technique allows the growth of a wide range of compositions, yielding a unique tool to achieve promising functional magnetic nanowires of high-quality. Since macroscopic magnetization characterization usually requires high magnetic signal and nanowire alignment, maximizing the template filling factor is crucial. We present a setup with objective of previously infiltrating the flux element into the nanopores, before performing the metallic flux protocol. It is based on an external applied pressure, under vacuum and heated conditions. We achieved throughout infiltration of Ga, a common flux element, in more than 71 % of the nanopores (200 nm diameter and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$80 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> l long) of an AAO template.

articleTitle: An Ultrathin, Rapidly Fabricated, Flexible Giant Magnetoresistive Electronic Skin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in the prevalence of electronic wearables, among which flexible magneto-electronic skin has emerged as a key component, which has opened a new avenue in human perceptual development: magnetic sense. In this paper, a novel type of magneto-electronic touchless interactive electronics that utilizes a flexible giant magnetoresistive sensor array sensitive to weak magnetic fields is demonstrated. The flexible magnetic sensor array has been developed through an electrochemical delamination process. The flexible magnetic sensor is capable of achieving a bending angle of up to 90 degrees, maintaining its performance integrity even after multiple repetitive bending cycles. Our research also encompasses demonstrations of non-contact interaction and pressure sensing, presenting novel findings in these areas.

articleTitle: Using Long Short-Term Memory to Estimate the Two-Dimensional Interference of Bit-Patterned Media Recording Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Recently, to increase the areal density of data storage systems, the bit-patterned media recording (BPMR) is considered the promising candidate for the next generation of stored technologies. In the BPMR, magnetic islands are used to store the user data. Therefore, these magnetic islands are adjusted closer to improve the areal density. However, this leads the bit-error rate performance of BPMR to become worse by two-dimensional (2D) interference. The 2D interference includes inter-symbol interference (ISI) and inter-track interference (ITI) from cross- and down-track directions, respectively. To solve the 2D interference, we can use the ISI/ITI estimator to remove ISI/ITI from the desired signal. Therefore, this study suggests a method to enhance the accuracy of estimating 2D interference using a long short-term memory (LSTM) for BPMR systems. LSTM is developed from the recurrent neural network (RNN) to avoid the vanishing gradient. Simultaneously, LSTM can be used to estimate the relationship between the samples in the training process. Therefore, LSTM can predict the interference from the neighbor bits in BPMR systems. In the proposed model, we used the LSTM to predict the ISI and ITI (like interferences from the neighbor bits) in BPMR channel. Then, ISI and ITI are removed from the desired signal, which is output of the 2D equalizer. Finally, the desired signal only remains the lD interference and easily is detected by the lD Viterbi algorithm. In the simulation, the results show that our proposed model improved the BER performance of the BPMR system compared with the conventional methods.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Thermal Management Efficiency Study of a High-Stability Doubly-Excited Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In response to challenges arising from the large-scale integration of new energy sources into power systems, issues such as frequency and voltage stability, peak shaving capability, transient stability, and dynamic stability of the power grid have garnered considerable attention. The research on key equipment, namely the doubly-excited synchronous generator (DESG), characterized by robust stability and the capability for deep-phase operation, has become a focal point. However, addressing the diverse operational requirements under various conditions, the design of rotor topology and thermal balance of the DESG remain unresolved. This study presents a theoretical derivation of the mathematical model for the synchronous axis system of the DESG. Building upon this, an investigation into rotor topology design is conducted, considering factors such as rotor slot pitch, rotor excitation winding arrangements (symmetric and asymmetric, single-layer and double-layer, orthogonal and non-orthogonal), and air gap length. Additionally, a finite volume method is employed to explore the thermal balance issues and optimize the cooling structure of the DESG under stringent operating conditions. The research outcomes contribute theoretical foundations and technical support for the development of high-power doubly-excited synchronous generators by large-scale power generation equipment manufacturers.

articleTitle: Torque-to-Weight Ratio Improvement and Permanent Magnet Usage Reduction in Large-Scale Magnetic Gears for Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic gears, which can transmit power without mechanical contact, offer lower vibration and acoustic noise compared with conventional mechanical gears. Among the various magnetic gears, a flux-modulated-type magnetic gear has the features of high efficiency and high torque density since all the permanent magnets always contribute to power transmission. This paper discusses an analytical study of flux-modulated-type magnetic gears to improve the torque-to-weight ratio and reduce permanent magnet usage, with the aim of constructing a highly reliable, lightweight, and resource-saving offshore wind power generation system with magnetic gears.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Broadband Magnetic Susceptivity Evaluation of Magnetic Nanoparticle and Protein
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A new broad bandwidth detection of the GDF15 protein (Growth Differentiation Factor-15), which utilizes the broad bandwidth observation up to 67 GHz, has been proposed. We prepared the sandwich-type bound method using a primary and secondary antibody with additional magnetic nanoparticles on an Au film. A DC field application enhanced sharp ferromagnetic resonance, which improved the signal-to-noise ratio of detecting GDF15. The density of GDF15 changed as follows: 0, 0.5, 5, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{50}\ \mu \mathbf{g}/\mathbf{ml}$</tex>. The magnetic susceptivity and FMR intensity increased clearly with the increase of the GDF15 density.

articleTitle: The Effect of CoFeB Electrodes Compositions on Bias Voltage Dependence of Sensitivity in Tunneling Magnetoresistance Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Sensitivity is one of the key characteristics of tunneling magneto resistance sensors. It has been shown that bias voltage has a strong impact on the sensitivity, which typically increases at low bias, peaks at a certain bias, and then reduces at higher bias. However, no studies on the effect of CoFeB active layer on sensitivity have been conducted. We investigated the sensitivity dependence on bias voltage magnitude and polarity in sensors with CO20Fe60B20, CO40Fe40B20 and CO60Fe20B20 active layers. In contrast to the CO40Fe40B20 and CO20Fe60B20 sensors, the CO60Fe20B20 sensors did not exhibit a voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy effect. The sensitivity of CO40Fe40B20 and CO20Fe60B20 sensors increased rapidly and without saturation under positive bias, reaching up to ten times that of negative bias. The bias dependence of the derivative induced by the voltage controlled perpendicular anisotropy modification is responsible for the high increase and asymmetry in sensitivity. The high increase and asymmetry caused by the anisotropy modification are stronger in sensors with weaker perpendicular anisotropy and CO20Fe60B20 electrodes. The results indicate that a higher Fe content in CoFeB alloys enhances the voltage controlled perpendicular anisotropy modification, allowing for a stronger increase in sensitivity by the bias.

articleTitle: Study and Development of a sensor for touchless capacitive computer interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This article describes the initial process to research develop a sensor to be used on a touchless pointer interface to navigate systems. This category has improved in late years, it uses smartphone cameras, Kinect camera from Microsoft, voice commands, but all these examples are a bit difficult to use and have a broad use case. This works than has the objective to reduce the scope and make it more “plug-and-play” type of interface. The scenario would be a simple command like volume up and down of an audio output. The interface will use capacitor like sensors that are already well know and researched by others, they will have small changes to adapt to the specific case. The sensor is made of two metal plates arranged in a planar way that produces fringe capacitance between the two and this electric field is change by the presence of a hand. The importance of the technology is to make it easier to be a product instead of a prototype, and permit people to make small interactions with systems without having to touch it, like in hospitals, industry or at home when the person have the hands contaminated in anyway.

articleTitle: Towards on-Chip Spintronic-Photonic Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work we review our latest work on establishing full on-chip spintronic-photonic integration. We envision a compact photonic memory based on a cross-strip arrangement of a photonic waveguide and a magnetic racetrack. The Pt/Co/Gd materials platform is shown to facilitate all-optical switching by fs laser pulses as well as > 2000 m/s current-induced domain wall velocities. First on-chip demonstrations of magneto-optical readout as well as opto-magnetic writing are presented. Numerical simulations of realistic device designs are used to sketch future potential of this technology, in particular with respect to the use of plasmonics and photonic crystal cavities to more efficiently read and write data in sub-l00 nm bits, and reducing device footprints by wavelength demultiplexing schemes.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of TRL-6 Magnetic Refrigeration Prototypes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Over the last few years, the attention to the carbon footprint of cooling systems has increased substantially, and along with them the demands for the development of more efficient and greener systems. For that, magnetocaloric refrigeration represents a promising solution despite its low technological maturity. This work presents the main finding on the design, commissioning, and performance evaluation of two magnetocaloric prototypes: a wine cooler and an air conditioner. The results demonstrate that the technology still requires improvements regarding the efficiency, cost, and mass of the systems, and the reliability of materials and components. However, investments in technology are expected to soar over the next years due to pressure from society and regulatory agencies.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Magnetoresistance of Epitaxial Grown CoFe Thin Films on Flexible Mica and Rigid MgO Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study investigates the correlation of anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) to the crystal structure, epitaxial relationship, and magnetic properties of CoFe films on both rigid MgO and flexible mica substrates. The AMR ratio is approximately 1.6% for CoFe films on a flexible mica substrate, which is lower than that on MgO substrate of about 2.5% under growth temperature 400°C. The angular dependence of applied magnetic field of AMR ratio to the applied current directions along CoFe[100] and CoFe[110] on MgO and mica substrates are totally different. It could be due to that the epitaxial CoFe film on MgO substrate is in one domain, while three symmetric CoFe domains on mica partly smeared out the in-plane anisotropy with less significant preferred orientation.

articleTitle: Deconvolution of Magnetic Field by Coupling Efficiency Tensor of TMR Sensor Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The relationship between a magnetic field vector and a current density vector is reduced to a tensor to illustrate information transfer between the current density within a volume and the field external to the volume. Forward application of the tensor produces an estimate of the magnetic field by convolution with a current density distribution. Inverse application of the tensor produces an estimate of the state of localized current density vectors by discrete deconvolution using a set of diverse measurements of the field.

articleTitle: Understanding the Influence of Capping Layer on Spin Wave Modes: An In-Depth Investigation with a Custom Time-Resolved Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (TR-MOKE) Setup
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Here, we investigated ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ni thin film (10nm thickness) employing the time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TR-MOKE) with a two-color pump-probe setup in polar geometry. Systematically examining films with and without Hf0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> capping layer of 4nm thickness, we observe the influence of external magnetic fields on magnetic precessional modes. Additionally, our study sheds light on the impact of capping layers on the Gilbert damping parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex> in relation to spin wave frequency. The outcomes provide insights into the recovery and potential improvement of spin mobility in Ni films

articleTitle: Correlation between Strains, Oxygen Vacancies and Magnetotransport Properties of CaMnO3 Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We performed a detailed study of the correlation between structural characteristics of strained CaMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films and its magnetic and magnetotransport properties. The crystalline structure, stacking and strains and stoichiometry of two sets of CaMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> epitaxial thin films grown on SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and LaAlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> single-crystalline (001) substrates were investigated by multiple techniques. Besides, the temperature and magnetic field dependence of magnetization and magnetoresistance ratio of these films were measured in order to determine the magnetic ordering, anisotropies and dominant magnetic interactions in them. The results are correlated in a phenomenological model with the strains and oxygen vacancies present in these thin films

articleTitle: Effect of Different Grain Boundary Diffusion Alloys on Magnetic Properties of Dy-Free Sintered NdFeB Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Dy-free sintered magnets were fabricated by blending Neo powder with different grain boundary diffusion (GBD) alloy powders. Cu, CeAl, and CeAlCu have a negative effect on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cj}}$</tex> of magnets, while PrAlCu and AlCuGa have a positive effect. PrAlCu alloy achieves the best magnetic properties among all of the GBD alloys. With increasing PrAlCu from 0–10 wt.%, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cj}}$</tex> of the magnets gradually increases from the original 14.5 kOe to 19.2 kOe. The magnet with 7.5 wt.% PrAlCu obtains a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cj}}$</tex> of 18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kOe}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{BH})_{\max}$</tex> of 39.1MGOe. It is found that Pr and Cu in PrAlCu alloy are mainly distributed at the grain boundary and triple junctions, leading to a reduced coupling among grains, thus an enhanced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cj}}$</tex>. The grain boundary engineering by adding an appropriate alloy is an effective method to improve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cj}}$</tex> of Dy-free magnets.

articleTitle: Magnetoelastic Resonators Functionalized with Metal Organic Frameworks for Wireless Humidity Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We propose a relative humidity (%RH) sensor based on magnetoelastic resonators functionalized with Metal Organic Framework (MOF) active layers. Different MOF materials were used in the sensor coating: MOF-801, MOF-808, UiO-66-NH2, Al-Fumarate and CAU-23. The capacity of the MOF materials to adsorb water molecules and the sensor response to different levels of humidity were analyzed. The ability of the magnetoelastic sensors to operate contactless, combined with the high adsorption capacity of MOF water harvesters, results in a very promising alliance. Furthermore, magnetoelastic sensors have shown potential as a technique for characterizing the water harvesting capacity of Metal Organic Frameworks.

articleTitle: Cobalt-Iron Nitride Nano-Flake Powders: Synthesis, Analysis Morphological, Structural, Magnetic and Catalytic Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A detailed investigation is presented for the solvent-free mechanochemical synthesis of cobalt-iron nitride nano-flake powders from Fe and Co crystals by high-energy ball milling. To the best of our knowledge, this mechanochemical approach for synthesizing Co-Fe-N from Fe-Co is completely novel. Furthermore, only a few works have ever explored the physic and chemistry properties from Co-Fe-N. The milling process of Co-Fe was done in ambient conditions with a 1:40 powder/ball mass ratio, and it produced uniform Co-Fe-N nano-flake with sizes of 10–200 nm, based on the milling duration. Using these parameters, two different samples were synthesized. The first sample utilized gaseous nitrogen as the nitrogen source (A2), and the second sample employed urea as the nitrogen precursor (A3). The process was carefully monitored and the effect of the milling duration on the powder composition, particle size and aggregate size, magnetic properties, and material activity was examined using XRD, EDS, Raman, TEM, MEV, VSM, and LSV. The mechanism for the transformation of Co-Fe to Co-Fe-N was studied by XPS analysis. The catalyst produced from sample A3 exhibited superior catalytic performance for LSV with an overpotential of -1.12 V at a current density of -1.7 rnA em>, On the other hand, the catalyst derived from sample A2 demonstrated better stability during the catalytic activity test. Co-Fe-N crystals are very easy to obtain, and the milling process is carried out under ambient conditions. Therefore, this work provides a simple, cost-effective, and solvent-free method to produce Co-Fe-N nano-flakes with ferromagnetic behavior and catalytic activity for H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> production.

articleTitle: Calculation of Mutual Inductance Between Trapezoidal and Rectangular Coils with Angular Misalignment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Recently, the need for electric ships has emerged to prevent environmental pollution caused by greenhouse gases, and various studies are being conducted on electric ship wireless power transfer (WPT). Unlike conventional ship WPT systems, which have poor aesthetics and obstruct passengers' passage, this paper considers a system where the transmitting coil is embedded into a dock, and a receiving coil is attached to the lower part of the ship. This system can achieve maximum mutual inductance by using an asymmetrical coil due to the tilted structure of the ship between the transmitting coil and the receiving coil. In this paper, a geometrical calculation method for mutual inductance between a trapezoidal coil and rectangular coils under angular misalignment, based on the Biot-Savart law, is proposed.

articleTitle: Smart Predictions: Machine Learning in Constructing Sm-Fe-V Phase Diagram
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The equilibrium Sm-Fe-V phase diagram is re-investigated by using machine learning algorithms to predict unknown regions and to select the next experiment from the most uncertain region in the predicted data. The least confidence score is applied to the random forest, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), and Neural Network-Multi-Layer Perceptron (NN-MLP) to identify the uncertain region. The uncertainty score of the NN-MLP is high at the potential phase boundaries, while in the random forest, the high uncertainty is in various regions of the phase diagram. Therefore, the first four compositions were selected from the boundary region to synthesize experimentally. The obtained results were incorporated into the dataset, and upon completing the initial iteration, it was revealed that the 1:12 and liquid phase equilibrium can exist in the V-lean region with a composition of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">77</inf>V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>.

articleTitle: Efficient Synthesis and Magneto-Optical Enhancement of Au-Fe3O4 Hetero-dimer Nanoparticles with Triiron Dodecacarbonyl
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study presents a pioneering and efficient method for synthesizing Au-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> hetero-dimer nanoparticles (NPs) with enhanced magneto-optical properties via a thermal decomposition route. Employing triiron dodecacarbonyl (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(CO)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>) as a safer alternative to the commonly used toxic iron pentacarbonyl (Fe(CO)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>), we achieved a near 100% production yield by optimizing the molar ratio of Au seeds to Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(CO)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> (0.6:2.0 mmol) and reflux time (60 min). The resulting hetero-dimer NPs, featuring an Au component of medium diameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{d}_{\mathbf{0}}=\mathbf{6.89}$</tex> nm and a Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> component of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{d}_{\mathbf{0}}=\mathbf{14.51}\ \mathbf{nm}$</tex> (with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{d}_{\mathbf{0}}=\mathbf{4.22}$</tex> nm Au seeds used), exhibited remarkable magneto-optical properties. These included a high magnetization (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{M}\mathbf{s}=\mathbf{72.6}\ \mathbf{emu} /\mathbf{g}-\mathbf{Fe}\mathbf{3}\mathbf{O}_{\mathbf{4}}$</tex> at 300K) and a well-defined plasmon resonance band at 553 nm, showcasing a 42 nm red shift from that observed in pure Au NPs. The use of triiron dodecacarbonyl as a precursor in the synthesis of these high-quality Au-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs highlights their significant potential for magnetic-plasmonic bio-applications.

articleTitle: Magnetocaloric Effect of Uniformly Packed Ferromagnetic Gd Nanoparticle Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We report a theoretical discussion on the magnetocaloric effect (MCE) of ferromagnetic Gd nanoparticles arranged in large eccentricity ellipsoidal clusters. We focus on micrometer-sized clusters of uniformly packed Gd nanoparticles, with the external field parallel to the major axis of the ellipsoidal cluster. We have replicated the bulk results for small nanoparticle spatial density. However, for large nanoparticle density, the MCE is strongly influenced by the nanoparticle's dipolar interaction. At low temperatures, the dipolar field strengths can reach a few Teslas, and there are two distinct regimes. For high external field strengths, the magnetocaloric effect is normal, and the dipolar interaction causes an up-shift of the temperature for the peak of the isothermal entropy change <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta S$</tex>, For low external field strengths, the MCE is normal for temperatures above the cluster Curie temperature. In contrast, we found an inverse MCE for low temperatures due to the nucleation of an antiferromagnetic pattern, where neighboring lines along the ellipsoid major axis are magnetized in opposite directions.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Applications of Glass-coated Ferromagnetic Microwires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The impact of post-processing on soft magnetic properties, giant magnetoimpedance (GMI) effect and domain wall dynamics of Fe-and Co-based glass-coated microwires is evaluated. A remarkable improvement of magnetic softness and GMI effect is observed in both Co -rich and Fe-rich glass-coated microwires subjected to stress annealing. Annealed Co-rich microwires present rectangular hysteresis loop. However, higher GMI ratio and better magnetic softness are observed in Co-based stress-annealed microwires. Single and fast domain wall propagation is observed in as-prepared Fe-rich microwires. Domain wall dynamics of Fe-rich microwires can be substantially improved by annealing. Observed stress-annealing induced anisotropy and related changes of magnetic properties are discussed considering internal stresses relaxation and “back-stresses”.

articleTitle: Comparison of Techniques for the Quantitative Determination of the Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction in Ultrathin Magnetic Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The accurate measurement of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in ultrathin ferromagnetic/heavy metal heterostructures was recently shown to require extreme experimental care. In this presentation the current state-of-the-art of measuring interfacial DMI is reviewed, and two of the most popular techniques - non-reciprocity of thermally activated magnetostatic spin wave dispersion and asymmetric bubble domain expansion - are discussed for their reliability and applicability. Furthermore, the large discrepancies observed recently between the two techniques are analyzed, and possible origins are discussed. The presentation aims to achieve a deeper comprehension of the reasons behind the discrepancies and to assess the applicability of various techniques to different heterostructures.

articleTitle: A Matlab Toolbox for Anhysteretic Magnetization Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We present MagAnalyst, a user-friendly Matlab toolbox that simplifies the fitting process of anhysteretic magnetization curves using the Langevin-Weiss equation of state. This toolbox follows the framework proposed by Silveyra and Conde Garrido, allowing for the characterization of anisotropic materials using a negative Weiss' molecular field constant and the characterization of inhomogeneous materials through multicomponent magnetizations. Our work demonstrates that MagAnalyst can provide reliable and accurate solutions, while also enabling the retrieval of important quantities such as the anisotropy mean field and the induced anisotropy energy constant. By freely distributing this toolbox (https://github.com/matias-gonz/maganalyst/), we aim to offer a valuable resource for studying and understanding the magnetic properties of soft magnets, ultimately contributing to the development of advanced magnetic devices.

articleTitle: Relating Structural Sensitivities and Helical Magnetic Order of MnSi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We relate and complement the structural sensitivities of a non-centrosymmetric B20 cubic chiral magnet MnSi in the vicinity of the magnetic transition using the combined results of temperature-dependent synchrotron x-ray diffraction, dc-magnetization, ac-susceptibility, specific heat and caloric measurements. MnSi is not found to undergo structural transformation down to 18 K. However, the lattice constant exhibits an anomaly at the long-range magnetic ordering temperature. The behavior of lattice constant in the vicinity of long-range ordering temperature is in line with the magnetic changes, indicating the latent heat contribution. The results will be correlated with the magnetic, caloric and transport properties. Our study suggests the vital role of lattice/crystal structure in determining the first order nature of the zero-field magnetic phase transition of MnSi.

articleTitle: Process Development for Synthesizing FeCoN-Based Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To improve the magnetic properties of FeCo alloys, the formation conditions of nitriding phases like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha}^{\prime\prime}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\gamma}^{\prime}$</tex> with excellent magnetic properties were investigated. The conditions of gas nitriding and the grain size of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{100}\ {\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> thick FeCo foil were investigated. Then, by using a material with a small grain size, adjusting the gas nitriding temperature and ammonia gas concentration, and nitriding only the diffusion layer without forming a nitriding layer, a prospect was obtained that nitrogen was uniformly introduced into the entire depth of the foil with only a single phase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\gamma}^{\prime}$</tex> phase. We expect that by quenching this film material above the austenitic transformation temperature, the possibility of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha}^{\prime}$</tex> formation can be investigated in the future.

articleTitle: Design of Magnetic Circuits for Magnetocaloric Refrigeration via Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetocaloric systems are one of the most promising solutions for decarbonizing cooling systems. However, several challenges must be overcome to enable the technology to reach large-scale market adoption, among which the high cost and volume of the systems can be highlighted, mainly caused by the magnetic circuits (MC). Addressing these challenges requires emphasizing the trade-off between augmenting magnetic flux density and reducing the mass and complexity of the MC. This study introduces a topology optimization method focused on crafting an MC that minimizes volume while maximizing magnetic flux density while employing rectangular prismatic permanent magnet segments. The optimized design, exhibits similar volume and magnetic flux density compared to configurations with non-prismatic segments, substantially lowering manufacturing costs and underscoring the potential of topology optimization methods in overcoming key barriers to the large-scale adoption of magnetocaloric systems.

articleTitle: Research on Air-Gap Field Modulation Effect of Torque Enhanced Hybrid Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In order to further enhance the torque and improve the utilization of permanent magnet, this paper proposed a new hybrid PM motor with spoke-type and consequent-pole structure (HPM-SCP). The air-gap field modulation effects (AFME) in the HPM-SCP motor are researched. By quantifying the contributions of the various air-gap flux density harmonics to the torque components and torque fluctuation, the working harmonics and the dominating harmonics that contribute to torque production are analyzed. In addition, a comprehensive comparison of the electromagnetic characteristics of HPM-SCP motor and a traditional HPM machine is conducted. It identifies that in the HPM-SCP motor, the magnetic field modulation effects can be generated significantly thanks to the spoke-type and consequent-pole structure. Then the influences of the key dimension parameters on AFME for torque performance of the HPM-SCP motor are evaluated. Finally, the reliability and effectiveness of theoretical analysis and FE simulation are verified by experiments on an HPM-SCP prototype.

articleTitle: The Critical Behavior of Magnetization near the Curie Temperature in Highly Spin-Polarized Heusler Alloy Co2TiGa0.3Sn0.7
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We present an analysis of the critical behavior of magnetization near the Curie temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{C}}$</tex> in Heusler alloy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Co}_{2}\text{TiGa}_{0.3}\text{Sn}_{0.7}$</tex>, which is a promising candidate for highly spin-polarized materials that exhibit the characteristic properties of magnetic Weyl states. Weyl semimetals have garnered significant interest for their potential applications in spintronics devices, owing to their anomalous magnetoelectronic and magnetothermal properties. The magnetization of the synthesized Heusler alloy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Co}_{2}\text{TiGa}_{0.3}\text{Sn}_{0.7}$</tex> was investigated in the vicinity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{C}}$</tex>. The analysis of magnetic isotherms for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Co}_{2}\text{TiGa}_{0.3}\text{Sn}_{0.7}$</tex> reveals that the critical exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta$</tex> is deduced to be 5.16. The obtained value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta$</tex> deviates from the value of 3.0 expected by the conventional molecular field theory. However, it is in close agreement with the value of 5.0 predicted by the spin fluctuation theory for weak itinerant electron ferromagnets, exhibiting that the spin fluctuation theory is applicable even to highly spin-polarized Heusler alloys.

articleTitle: Analysis of Dual-Airgap Yokeless-Stator Permanent Magnet Motor with Non-Oriented or Grain-Oriented Steels for Aircraft Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this article, a dual-airgap yokeless-stator permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) for aircraft propulsion is analyzed considering the influence of different steel materials. The topologies of the dual-airgap motors without/with stator yoke are illustrated. Due to the unidirectional magnetic flux in the majority of stator, grain-oriented (GO) as well as non-oriented (NO) steels can be used as stator material. The characteristics and electromagnetic performances of motors with NO SiFe, GO SiFe and CoFe steels are analyzed and compared by finite-element method. Furthermore, the dual-airgap PMSMs without/with stator yoke are compared to prove the superiority of the yokeless-stator topology.

articleTitle: How Accurate are Magnetic Loss Measurements?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic steel is utilized in electric motors/generators and transformers, where the cyclic magnetization of the material results in notable energy losses. With the increasing emphasis on boosting energy efficiency, there is a demand for more effective evaluation methods to quantify these losses in challenging operational conditions involving high frequency, elevated temperatures, and also distorted flux conditions. This investigation seeks to assess the accuracy of techniques employed for measuring losses in thin steel sheets, as well as in nanocrystalline and ferrite materials. The evaluation extends beyond the established IEC 60404 standards by broadening the ranges of induction, frequency, and temperature. These measurements play a pivotal role in advancing magnetic materials and power electronics devices, facilitating the development of materials with enhanced energy performance in practical operating scenarios. Consequently, this supports the application of the Ecodesign Directive 2009/125/EC and contributes to the attainment of objectives outlined in the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

articleTitle: Local Temperature Control of Magnon Frequency and Direction of Supercurrents in a Magnon Bose–Einstein Condensate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Spatial variations in the saturation magnetization of magnetic samples, in which the magnon Bose–Einstein condensate is prepared, lead to the appearance of supercurrents and excitation of Bogoliubov waves, which can be exploited for data transfer and processing. Here, we show theoretically and experimentally that demagnetization fields arising in the magnetization landscape strongly influence the dynamics of magnon supercurrents. In our experiment, local laser heating of a tangentially magnetized film of yttrium iron garnet increases the magnetic field in the region of reduced magnetization and, as a result, elevates the bottom of the spin-wave spectrum, where Bose–Einstein condensate is formed. This causes a magnon supercurrent directed outward from the hot region.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Fractionally Magnetized Quantum Ferromagnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We present a theory to realize fractionally magnetized quantum ferromagnet in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{spin}-S \geqq 2$</tex> bilinear-biquadratic spin systems. The origin of the fractionally magnetized state is spin-liquefaction of ferromagnetism which means partly emergent antiferromagnetism. The realization of the spin-liquefaction of ferromagnetism is guaranteed due to a rigorous eigenstate correspondence between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Spin}-S$</tex> model and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{spin} - \frac{1}{2}$</tex> model, i. e., “eigensystem embedding”. This spin-liquefaction theory of ferromagnets can be generalized to any-dimensional lattices. As a typical case, we discuss the two-dimensional models on a square lattice with a numerical exact-diagonalization.

articleTitle: A Novel Counter-rotating Axial-flux Permanent Magnet Memory Machine with Dual-rotor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To meet the operational requirements of the counter rotating propeller (CRP) system under unbalance load conditions, a novel counter-rotating axial-flux permanent magnet memory machine (CR-AFPMM) is proposed, which combines the regulative magnetic field of the memory machine (MM) with the high torque density of the axial-flux permanent magnet machine (AFPMM). Firstly, the machine configurations and operating principle of CR-AFPMMs based on different magnetic circuits are introduced. Subsequently, the electromagnetic performance is compared and analyzed. Furthermore, the anti-demagnetization performance of the low coercive force permanent magnets (LCF PMs) under the impact of load current is comprehensively analyzed. The results indicate that the proposed CR-AFPMM with hybrid magnetic circuits has profound application prospects in the driving device of the CRP.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Orthogonal-Core- Type Variable Inductor with Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Variable inductors, which consist of magnetic cores, primary dc windings, and secondary ac windings, can control the effective inductance of the secondary ac windings by the primary dc current due to the magnetic saturation effect. Therefore, they can be used as reactive power compensators in electric power systems. In a previous paper, a novel orthogonal-core-type variable inductor with permanent magnets. Since it can control the effective reactive power from lead to lag, the line voltage can be increased or decreased without power capacitors. In this paper, a 3 kVA orthogonal-core-type variable inductor with permanent magnets is prototyped and demonstrated to prove its validity and feasibility.

Author Keywords: Orthogonal-core-type variable inductor with permanent magnets

articleTitle: Harnessing Magnetic-Field Driven Actuation for Microscale Motion in MEMS- Inspired Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Precise small-scale control of magnetic actuation necessitates equally precise tuning of the magnetic fields and field gradients that drive the motion. In this study, two control magnets are coupled to create the local magnetic fields required to induce microscale, localized deflections of a shuttle fitted with a soft magnetic element. The magnetization orientation and anisotropy of the magnetic element is optimized to maximize the deflection during the ON state and the difference between it and the OFF state. The effectiveness of the field in exerting actuation force on the magnetic element is demonstrated through the creation of a double folded beam MEMS structure that is integrated with the control magnets. Analytical models considering the field strength and gradient from the control magnets are used to optimize the material and shape of the soft magnetic element, and the design of the beam structure. Additional magneto-mechanical simulations are performed to support the analytical deflection estimates predicted from this innovative integrated actuator design.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculations of Electron's Phase Shift Due to Interactions with Magnetized Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Differential phase contrast, through the use of transmission electron microscopes, allows accessing information on magnetic configurations or textures with resolutions smaller than nanometers and even close to angstroms depending on the characteristics of the microscope. This phenomenon is due to the Aharonov-Bohm effect, that predicts a shift in the relative phase (of the electron wave) between two beams traveling through different regions of the material, with electric or magnetic potentials. This shift can be used to make insights into the local magnetic configuration- contained in the region bounded by the beam paths. Here, we show how Toroidal Harmonics functions can be used to compute the phase shift generated by the magnetic vector potential for different geometries and magnetization textures with cylindrical symmetric geometries.

articleTitle: Spin and Orbital Moments of Magnetic Topological Insulator MnBi2Te4 Epitaxial Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Intrinsic magnetic topological insulators (MTIs) have proven to be an important material system for the study of quantum effects and the development of novel electronic devices. Unlike the magnetically doped topological insulators (TIs)., intrinsic MTIs well preserve the crystalline ordering and homogeneity of the pristine TIs, leading to enhanced quantum coherency in many cases. Here, we report a detailed study of the atomic scale spin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m_{\mathrm{s}})$</tex> and orbital <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m1)$</tex> moments of an epitaxial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MnBi}_{2}\text{Te}\triangleleft$</tex> thin film. The synchrotron-based x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) measurements were performed to investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of the thin film at 3 K and up to 14 T. The 16.3 nm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MnBi}_{2}\text{Te}4/\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}$</tex> shows reduced moments of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_{\mathrm{s}}= (1.64\pm 0.2)\mu_{\mathrm{B}}/\text{Mn}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m1=(0.16\pm 0.02)\mu_{\mathrm{B}}/\text{Mn}$</tex> at 14 T compared to their bulk counterparts. The reduced magnetic moments may be attributed to the weakened intralayer or interlayer exchange interaction and the intrinsic structural defects of the materials. Future work to understand the correlations between the structural defects, intralayer or interlayer exchange interactions, and magnetic properties will have strong implications for both fundamental physics and practical applications of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MnBi}_{2}\text{Te}_{4}$</tex> materials.

articleTitle: Use of a Ferrofluid in a Magnetic Brake for a Wind Energy Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A magnetic brake is developed by using ferrofluids. An aluminum disk coaxial with the rotation axis is immersed in a ferrofluid composed of iron oxide nanoparticles. This work presents the initial stages in the development of a device to reduce the impact of wind gusts on the operation of a wind turbine. The study focuses on the quantification of the variation of the magnetic field generated by coils in the Helmholtz configuration when they are immersed or not in the ferrofluid. The results obtained both by a finite element simulation and by direct measurement show a variation of 3 kA/m and 6 kA/m respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of New Beveling Consequent Pole Hybrid Magnet Dual Stator Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes new beveling consequent pole hybrid magnet dual stator machines (BCP-HMDSMs). The proposed BCP-HMDSMs employ two layers of consequent-pole modulation rings, in which the PMs all are dual-beveling topologies. The hybrid N dFeB-Ferrite magnets are employed to achieve low cost and avoid demagnetization, which N dFeB magnets on inner stator and Ferrite magnets on rotor. The rotor teeth act the role of modulation pole to modulate the magnetic field excited by N dFeB magnets. The configuration and design consideration of the proposed BCP-HMDSMs are described, respectively. In addition, the electromagnetic performances of the proposed BCP-HMDSM are evaluated using finite element analysis (FEA) and compared with the conventional dual stator machine (DSM). The FEA-predicted results show that the proposed BCP-HMDSM has the merits of high steady torque, low torque ripple, low cogging torque and high power factor.

articleTitle: The Impact of Fe2+ and Fe3+ Segregation on the Structural and Magnetic Properties of ZnO/Fe Multilayers Deposited via Sputtering: A Study Using EELS and EDS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Ferromagnetic (FM)-metal/oxide multilayers play a central role in achieving highly efficient spin injection, crucial for determining the performance of spintronic devices. In this study, we investigate the microstructural and magnetic properties of [ZnO(5nm)/Fe(t)]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> multilayers (t = 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 nm) deposited on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si substrates using magnetron sputtering. Characterization of the multilayers was conducted through transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM). XRD, XRR, and TEM analyses reveal the presence of multiple crystallographic defects and macroscopic periodicity. Consistent chemical profiles across the ZnO/Fe multilayers were identified through EELS and EDS methods. The saturation magnetization of the multilayer with t = 0.3 nm is approximately five times lower than that of the multilayer with t = 1 nm, and this discrepancy is attributed to indirect coupling between isolated Fe ions rather than the presence of clusters. These findings contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the microstructure and magnetic properties of the investigated ZnO/Fe multilayers, offering insights for their potential applications in spintronics.

articleTitle: Itinerant SDW Phases, Contributions from the CrNb Dilute Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The magnetic phases diagram of antiferromagnetic Cr alloys is very rich with many magnetic phases that are associated to an itinerant antiferromagnetism due to spin-density waves state. In this work we present a systematic study around spin-flip transition of CrNb alloys, in the compositional range represented by Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0}\leq \mathbf{x}$</tex> at% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq \mathbf{3.5}$</tex>. This study revealed a remarkable agreement between the predicted values for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{N}}/\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{SF}}$</tex> by Varelogiannis model [3] and our experimental results, supporting the applicability of this model to itinerant antiferromagnetic SDW systems in general and Cr alloys in particular.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study Between Permanent-Magnet-Free Reluctance Machines for Heavy-Duty Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper introduces permanent-magnet-free electrical drive solutions designed for the traction of a heavy-duty vehicle. The vehicle features a maximum continuous torque of 200 Nm and a nominal speed of 1600 rpm. The torque production, efficiency, and thermal characteristics of the designed variable flux reluctance machine are presented. Furthermore, two additional frequently utilized reluctance machine configurations, namely switched reluctance and synchronous reluctance machines, are explored for potential application in the same heavy-duty context. A comprehensive comparison is undertaken for three electrical drive options, assessing factors including torque generation, efficiency, power factor, and thermal characteristics. The examination covers both constant-torque and flux-weakening operations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Dual-Stator Permanent Magnet Machines with Inner Stator Teeth Designed in Hypotenuse for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The paper designs and analyzes new dual-stator permanent magnet machines with inner stator teeth designed in hypotenuse (ISTH-DSPMM), which can be applied in electric vehicle requiring high torque quality. The IST with hypotenuse can function as modulator to regulate the airgap flux density, which can effectively suppress the harmonic distortion to achieve low harmonic distortion and low torque ripple. The designed IST are combined of rectangle and triangle, which can be formed as trapezoid- and parallelogram-shaped stator teeth. Three representative ISTH-DSPMM and the conventional DSPMM with rectangle inner stator teeth are comparatively analyzed using method of finite element analysis (FEA). The investigated four machines have identical key parameters except the shape of IST for a fair comparison.
