The FEA-calculated results including back electromotive force, steady torque at rated state and torque ripple verify the merits of designed ISTH-DSPMMs.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy Control Through Mechanical Deformations: Study of Magnetoelastic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The present work aims to study the magnetoelastic coupling between Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles (NPs) in order to control the magnetic anisotropy of flexible nanocomposites through their deformation. In this sense, firstly, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs were synthesized using the solvothermal methodology as described by Zu et al. [1] and fully characterized using powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and vibrating sample magnetometer. The results of PXRD and TEM pointed out a nanoprism morphology with a spinel structure. No secondary phases were found, which evidences no oxidation of the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs. The VSM measurements displayed superparamagnetic NPs at room temperature. Afterward, the flexible nanocomposites were prepared using the characterized NPs and Mold Max™ 14NV silicone rubber. Up to date, the flexible nanocomposites were characterized by atomic force microscopy and a smooth surface with no Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs aggregates was observed. Finally, tension measurements will be performed under a magnetic field by using the NanoRack Sample stretching stage, coupled with Jupiter AFM equipment.

articleTitle: Advancing Kerr-Microscopy Imaging of Three-Dimensional Magnetic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work systematically investigates the magnetization reversal of pyramidal thin film magnets by magneto-optical Kerr-microscopy. Pyramids with different wall angles have been fabricated by two-photon polymerization lithography, covered by either a ferromagnetic or an exchange biased thin film system. In this contribution, the influence of the different wall angles and angles of light incidence on the magneto-optic Kerr-microscope signal is systematically studied, as an initial step towards Kerr-microscopy investigations of bent surfaces.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of a Novel Flux-Switching Arc Permanent Magnet Machine with Flux-Reversal Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel flux-switching arc permanent magnet (PM) machine (FSAPMM) with flux-reversal effect to improve the electromagnetic performances of conventional arc permanent magnet (APM) machine. The ending effect of APM is reduced by adopting a cross and concentrated winding connection. The electromagnetic performance of the proposed FSAPMM was analyzed and compared with the conventional FSAPMM and flux-reversal APM machine (FRAPM) by using finite element analysis (FEA) method after optimization. The results show the proposed FSAPMM has the highest back-electromotive force (EMF) amplitude, average torque and the lowest cogging torque.

articleTitle: PM-Free Axial-Flux Motors for Transport Electrification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Axial-flux machines offer advantages such as high power density, compact design, and potentially higher efficiency so that they have gained popularity in electric vehicles (EVs), wind turbines, robotics, etc. While axial-flux permanent-magnet (PM) machines have been studied widely, the PM-free axial-flux machines have received limited research attention. This paper discusses the performance of PM-free axial-flux machines and compares them to axial-flux PM machines and PM-free radial-flux machines. It shows where PM-free axial-flux machines show potential performance advantages for transport electrification.

articleTitle: Characterisation of Magnetic Sensors for Space Applications – an NMI Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Accurate characterisation of magnetic sensors is required across a range of industrial applications. The National Physical Laboratory (NPL), as the UK's National Metrology Institute (NMI), maintains and disseminates measurement standards, with traceability to SI units, that provides characterisation of advanced magnetic sensors from nT-level to several T. Space missions can benefit from the increasing sensitivity and accuracy of magnetic sensors. To calibrate such sensors, a low magnetic noise environment and traceable measurement systems must be established. Both spacecraft design and in-flight operation must rigorously incorporate magnetic cleanliness and compensate for field fluctuations. To reduce measurement uncertainties and dependent sensor error budgets, a greater understanding of the magnetic environment becomes crucial. This presentation will describe the development of traceable measurements systems at NPL that enable the characterisation of these sensors at the nT level for space applications. These systems allow key parameters, such as gain, linearity, offset and noise to be determined, with specific attention given to the measurement of the temperature dependance of these key parameters, and recent developments for the orthogonality of small magnetometers in a fast and cost-efficient way.

articleTitle: Investigating Unusual Dynamics: Time and Frequency-Dependent Variations in Specific Power Absorption of Magnetite Nanoparticles in Magnetic Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic hyperthermia is a mechanism that allows the conversion of electromagnetic field energy into heat by utilizing magnetic nanoparticles. To this, an external ac magnetic field, typically in the radiofrequency range, is applied to magnetic colloids containing magnetic monodomain nanoparticles resulting in the dissipation of heat energy into the surrounding medium. This work focuses on investigating iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles (IONPs), specifically Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (magnetite), with diameters of 17 nm and 25 nm. Magnetic hyperthermia experiments, conducted at frequencies between 150 kHz and 488 kHz with magnetic field amplitudes up to 550 Oe, revealed notable values of specific absorption rate (SAR), reaching 405 W/g for the 25 nm sample and 642 W/g for the 17 nm sample. Intriguingly, a reproducible increase in SAR was observed over time when applying the magnetic field, peaking at 768 W/g for the 17 nm sample, prompting ongoing investigation into its origin.

articleTitle: Comparison of Torque Generated by In-Plane and Out-of-Plane Anisotropic Magnetorheological Elastomers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study aims to optimize torque generation in Magnetorheological Elastomers (MREs) containing high remanent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Nd}_{2}\text{Fe}_{14}\mathrm{B}$</tex> particles. We explored two approaches to enhancing the overall remanent magnetic moment of the MREs: in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OOP) anisotropic arrangements of the magnetic filler particles. While the IP MREs have a slightly higher remanent moment resulting from shape anisotropy, the difference in particle arrangement established different effective bending moduli such that the IP MREs exhibit a lower net actuation in a magnetic field compared to OOP MREs. This surprising behavior indicates the importance of a synergism between both the magnetic and mechanical properties for maximizing torque production.

articleTitle: Differential Model based Parameter Estimation of IPMSMs from Multi-state Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Accurate parameter estimations are essential for efficient operation and high performance of interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs). A differential model is proposed to estimate three-phase IPMSM parameters, including permanent magnet (PM) flux linkage, winding resistance, and machine inductances. A three-phase IPMSM model considering voltage source inverter (VSI) nonlinearity and magnetic saturation is investigated, then the model is decoupled based on the proposed differential approach to reduce cross affection and observational error. With multi-state measurements, each parameter is estimated separately with high efficiency and accuracy. Least square (LS) algorithm is employed to improve the computational efficiency. The proposed approach is especially suitable for identifying parameters over an extensive speed range under various load conditions without requirement for any signal injection.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution in Computed Tomography Images: An Integrated Approach of Artificial Intelligence and LapSRN Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study aims to develop and apply advanced super-resolution methods in computed tomography images, which can also be applied to X-ray images, using Python and its libraries. The proposed project seeks to improve the quality of enlarged images, with the help of artificial intelligence and the LapSRN algorithm, an advanced super-resolution approach that involves deep learning and Laplacian pyramids. The methodology employed ranges from obtaining a database of X-ray images to the application of the super- resolution process and the evaluation of the results. The research seeks to generate results for better diagnostic accuracy and the acceleration of prognoses. In addition, it is intended that this study assists other similar studies for the greater application of these technologies in medical areas. The results indicate that artificial intelligence-based super-resolution is a promising approach to enhance X-ray tomography images, with potential to benefit various areas of medicine and image diagnostics, such as radiology and oncology. The research also highlights the significant differences between traditional resolution enhancement methods and super-resolution.

articleTitle: Surface Spin Wave Resonance in NiFe/Zr Multilayers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work reports a room temperature study on the excitation of surface spin wave resonance (SWR) modes in magnetron sputtered NiFe/Zr multilayers. The surface anisotropy constants and the variations of the magnetization close to the surface of the ferromagnetic (FM) layers are deduced from ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) and SWR measurements at X-Band (9–10 GHz) microwave frequency. The results confirm the inverse dependence of the anisotropy constant and the variation of the magnetization on the thickness of the NiFe layer.

articleTitle: Research on the Performance of Bidirectional Field Modulation Machine with Separated Type PM Excitation with Different Slot-Pole Combinations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper studies the bidirectional field modulation machine with separated type PM excitation (STPM-BFMM) with 90mm frame size. First, STPM-BFMM with different slot-pole combinations is designed, including 12-slot/l0-pole, 9-slot/8-pole, 15-slot/14-pole and 18-slot/22-pole. Secondly, the electromagnetic performances of the proposed STPM-BFMM are optimized by the multi-objective optimization method. Finally, using finite element simulation to compare the electromagnetic performance under different slot-pole combinations, including back electromotive force, cogging torque and steady torque, the advantages and disadvantages of different machines are obtained. The FEA-predicted results show that the 12-slot/l0-pole machine has merits of high quality output torque and high power density.

articleTitle: Thin Films of Heusler Alloy – Ni2(MnCu)(GaAl): Estructural and Magnetic Properties, a Spin Glass Behavior-Like Appears
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Heusler alloys are ternary metallic alloys with intriguing magnetic properties, such as shape transition and appreciable magnetocaloric effects, among others. This study investigates thin films of Heusler alloy with an approximate concentration of Ni2Mn0.7Cu0.3Ga0.8Al0.2, focusing on their structural and magnetic properties. The films, produced by sputter deposition, ranged in thickness from 32 nm to 300 nm on a Si (100) substrate with a 30 nm Ta adhesion layer. The structural transition (at 260 K) was observed only in the 300 nm thick film, with a Curie temperature around 300 K. Additionally, a spin glass behavior was noted in these samples and corroborated using the Vogel-Fulcher model.

articleTitle: Novel Self-Excited Brushless Topology for Wound Field Vernier Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel self-excited topology for the brushless operation of wound field vernier machines (WFVMs). The proposed topology involves a new armature winding configuration that develops fundamental and sub-harmonic magnetomotive force (MMF) components in air gap once the armature winding of the machine is supplied current from the inverter. The rotor of the machine is equipped with a harmonic winding which is used to induce current from the sub-harmonic MMF component of the air gap flux. The induced power is rectified to energize the main rotor field winding to the main rotor field. The electromagnetic interaction of stator and rotor fields along with the existence of the gearing effect develop torque. 2-D finite element analysis (FEA) was carried out to validate the theory for an outer rotor wound field vernier machine model.

articleTitle: Study of the Magnetoelectric Effect in PVDF/Ni Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The magnetoelectric (ME) effect consists in the generation of voltages by magnetic fields. In this work, we focus on ME composites, combining a piezoelectric polymer (PVDF) and a magnetostrictive material (Ni). In this case the ME coupling occurs indirectly via strain induced between the two layers. The deep study and understanding of this strain-mediated ME effect might serve for new magnetic field detecting technologies, e.g. for flexible ME transducers, with better performances. Our goal is to evaluate, through simulations and experimental procedures, the voltage outputs generated by magnetic fields and demonstrate the ME coupling in PVDF/Ni composites.

articleTitle: Extremophilic Microorganisms: An Alternative as Synthesizers of Ferromagnetic Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The development of new alternatives for the synthesis of nanoparticles (NPs) has been of great interest. Chemical synthesis has traditionally been employed, however chemical methods for the synthesis of NPs require the use of numerous highly toxic reagents, resulting in the production of environmentally harmful residues. Recently biological synthesis of nanoparticles has emerged as a promising and eco-friendly alternative, where extremophilic microorganisms and their enzymes play a key role. In this work the primary objective is to demonstrate the capability of two extremophilic microorganisms, isolated both from low temperature extreme environments, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Geobacillus sp. ID17 for the biosynthesis of ferromagnetic NPs, specifically iron oxide NPs generated both intra and extracellularly.

articleTitle: Voltage-Controlled Anisotropic Magnetoresistance in Ferromagnetic-Piezoelectric Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The utilization of voltage control within piezoelectric-ferromagnetic heterostructures presents a compelling strategy to enhance the performance of magnetoresistive sensors. In this study, we employed voltage control in a FeGaB/AlN piezoelectric-ferromagnetic heterostructure to regulate the anisotropic magnetoresistance of the FeGaB layer. Specifically, the applied voltage was used to modulate the magnetic field response characteristics of the FeGaB film, thereby influencing its sensitivity to the orientation of the magnetic field. The application of a voltage ranges from 0 to 60V led to nearly linear improvements in the magnetoresistance of the FeGaB film.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Flaw Detection using Eddy-Current Probe Array Based on Giant Magnetoresistance Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work presents a flaw detection system consisting of an array of eddy-current (EC) probes based on giant-magnetoresistance (GMR) sensors for mapping the defects on a metal sheet. Prior to measurement, a spatially-dependent calibration process was done to compensate the inter-channel inconsistency in responsivity and positioning. The calibrated 8-channel probe array exhibits high-sensitivity, which enables the detection of tiny feature with superior spatial resolution. The proposed system allows for the visualization of the geometric characteristics of the flaws with an inter-spacing of more than 2 mm on a copper sample. The suggested approach has great potential in nondestructive testing of metallic sheets for the characterization of small and intricate shape flaws.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Calorimetric Properties in EuSe and EuSe0.93S0.07 Compounds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work, we present the experimental results of the magnetic and calorimetric properties of the EuSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> compounds with x = 0 and 0.07. We observe antiferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and ferromagnetic behavior for low temperatures between 4.6K and 5.22K. The results indicated that these compounds are good candidates for gas liquefaction in cryogenics temperatures.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation Model for Inductance of Brushless DC Motor Under Bearing Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In a brushless DC motor (BLDCM), bearings are crucial components. During motor operation, when rolling bearings fail, the periodic variation of the air gap between the stator and rotor occurs, leading to changes in the air-gap permeance and subsequently altering the electromagnetic parameters of the motor. The winding inductance directly affects the parameters of the BLDCM control system. This paper presents the analytical equations for inductance under bearing faults, considering faults in the outer race, inner race, rolling elements, and cage. The validity of these equations is verified through numerical calculations. The results provide assistance for the motor control system.

articleTitle: Precision and Quantum Measurement Using Photons Phonons and Spins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work we will present our latest results on using novel cavity designs that couple photons, phonons and spins in solids, including magnon collective spins, paramagnetic spins including rare earths and techniques to generate and measure low loss phonons. We look at the photon-spin and photon-phonon couplings, and how some of the systems can be used to test fundamental physics.

Author Keywords: About four key words or phrases in alphabetical order, separated by commas

articleTitle: Micromagnetic Aspects of the Magneto-Impedance Response of the FM-I-NM-I-FM Multilayer Film Driven by a High-Frequency Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Currently, the technology of thin-film magnetoresistive elements based on amorphous ferromagnetic (FM) structures that use the giant magnetic impedance (GMI) effect to detect ultra-low magnetic fields is being actively developed. In order to select a promising design for a thin-film GMI sensor of arbitrary geometry with high sensitivity to the field, a complex model has been developed that combines the calculation of time maps of the magnetic field distribution from by alternating current from nonmagnetic metal (NM) conductor and micro magnetic analysis of the dynamics of localized spin moments in a thin-film FM shell sensitive element under the influence of a given field at each moment of time. Within the framework of the micromagnetic model, an increase in the output signal of the film FM-NM-I (insulator)-NM-FM structure with increasing current and transition to a nonlinear operating mode was demonstrated. The results obtained will be useful in developing the technology for manufacturing sensor elements based on the GMI effect in amorphous thin-film FM nanostructures.

articleTitle: Dynamics of the Shape of Magnetic Fluid Droplets Under the Influence of a Magnetic Field: Experiment and Lattice Boltzmann Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The results of the study of the influence of the magnitude of the magnetic field strength and the concentration of the magnetic phase of the magnetic fluid (MF) on the elongation coefficient and the shape of the drop of MF floating in glycerin are presented. The dependences of the elongation coefficient of the MF droplet on the parameters of the magnetic fluids used and the strength of the magnetic field intensity are obtained.

articleTitle: Effect of Sheet Thickness on the Excess Loss of Non-oriented Electrical Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This article shows a detailed study of the effects of thickness, frequency, silicon content and grain size on excess loss and statistical parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{0}}$</tex>. For this, 126 samples were used in the research. Therefore, the grain normalization method was adopted on sheets with the same silicon content and different thicknesses. Thus, it was found that the larger the grain size, the greater the effect of thickness on the excess loss.

articleTitle: First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) Features of Ferrimagnetic and Antiferromagnetic Coupled Skyrmions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work aims to experimentally investigate probing coupled skyrmions in perpendicular magnetic anisotropy multilayers. The first-order reversal curve (FORC) method is a powerful technique to unveil hidden states or subtle behaviors in complex magnetic systems. We focus on two multilayer stacks aiming to antiferromagnetically coupled skyrmions to cancel the skyrmion Hall effect. In the first case, using a ferrimagnetic layer (CoGd/Pt), the skyrmions still present a non-null net magnetization. Helped by magnetic force microscopy, we found that with both high or low Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, skyrmions tend to merge with magnetic stripes. On the other hand, skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnetic systems are fully compensated. By varying the spacer thickness in a Co/Pt/Ru multilayer, FORC results exhibit different features depending on the Co/Pt coupling, revealing a complex behavior.

articleTitle: A Quasi-3-D Finite Element Modeling of An Axial Flux Magnetic Resonant Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Due to inherent the 3-D magnetic structure of axial flux machines (AFM), 3-D finite element analysis (FEA) is the most commonly utilized approach for simulation in the design and analysis. However, these simulations are exceedingly time-demanding, particularly during the early phases of the design. This challenge has not been properly addressed in the design of an axial flux magnetic resonant motor (AFMRM). This in turn has limited the level of optimization that has been achieved in the design of AFMRM motor. In this paper, we present a method to quasi-3-D conduct FEA modeling analysis of an AFMRM motor. It is achieved by slicing the 3-D geometries of the AFMRM machine with cylindrical planes of different radii to form equivalent 2-D linear machine (2DLM) models. The magnetic problem is then solved in each slice with a 2-D finite element method (FEM). As a result, the generated mesh required for computation is faster and many designs analysis can therefore be implemented for optimization.

articleTitle: Recycling Nd-Fe-B End-of-Life Magnets with Different Levels of Oxidation Using the Magnet-to-Magnet Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The recycling of Nd-Fe-B end-of-life magnets through powder metallurgy can aid in reducing the usage of primary raw minerals, decreasing environmental damage, and redirecting otherwise discarded materials towards high-tech applications. This work assesses the process of recycling discarded Nd-Fe-B magnets at various stages of oxidation. It uses a magnet-to-magnet approach, starting with the hydrogen decrepitation method and ending with the sintering of the recycled magnets. The research findings suggest that the properties of recycled magnets largely depend on the oxidation content of the raw material. Recycled magnets with the highest oxidation content (27400 ppm) demonstrated poor properties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{EoL} (\rho=5.35\mathrm{g}/\text{cm}^{3}$</tex>, Br <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.11\mathrm{T}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cJ}}=15\text{kA}/\mathrm{m})$</tex>. However, starting with magnets that have a low oxidation content (4900 ppm) resulted in notable properties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\rho=7.35\mathrm{g}/\text{cm}^{3}$</tex>, Br <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=1.16\mathrm{T}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\text{cJ}}=900\text{kA}/\mathrm{m})$</tex>. This resulted in a 100% remanence recovery of the end-of-life magnet and 78% coercivity recovery. In summary, the feasibility of recycling these magnets is directly associated to the oxygen content of the original end-of-life magnet.

articleTitle: An Improved Analytical Model for the Novel Counter-Rotating Axial-Flux Hybrid-Excitation Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In order to accurately predict the magnetic field distribution of the counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation permanent magnet machine (CR-AFHEPMM), an improved subdomain model is proposed in this paper, which combines the Ampere's loop law with the Kirchhoff's law of magnetic circuits. Firstly, a simplified subdomain model is established in the Cartesian coordinate system, and the constraint equation considering the excitation circuit is derived by combining the excitation winding and the end of the armature winding. Then, considering the influence of SMC material saturation, the vector magnetic potential and magnetic density of each subdomain are iteratively calculated, effectively reducing the error of the magnetic field distribution. Finally, accurate prediction is made on the magnetic field distribution and magnetic regulation characteristics of the CR-AFHEPMM, and eddy current losses of the permanent magnet are calculated. This model is proven to have significant accuracy in the CR-AFHEPMM, providing a novel and convenient method for magnetic field analysis and permanent magnet loss calculation of such machines.

articleTitle: Design of a New Consequent-Pole Hybrid Excited Machine with Segmented Stator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this paper, a new consequent-pole hybrid excited (HE) machine with segmented stator (CHE-SS machine) is proposed, which can be applied in some variable speed applications. To decrease the torque ripple, the segmented structure is adopted in the stator. The stator tooth can be divided into two types: the primary tooth and the secondary tooth. The field winding is placed on the primary tooth. The armature winding is placed on the secondary tooth. The U-typed permanent magnets (PMs) are placed in the rotor to improve the torque density and the rigidity. To validate the superiority of the proposed machine, some electromagnetic properties, such as the back electromotive force (back-EMF), the output torque and the cogging torque are simulated and analyzed by the finite element (FE) method. The FE-predicted results show that this proposed machine can exhibit excellent performances.

articleTitle: Complex Permeability of Noise Suppression Sheets up to 40 GHz Evaluated with the Improved Shielded Loop Coil Type Permeameter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Measurable frequency range of the popular shielded-loop coil type permeameter is extended from 9 GHz to 40 GHz by means of the new quarter-size design, new RF calibration techniques and the introduction of superconducting magnet to saturate magnetic sample sufficiently during the background measurements.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis of Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor Considering Force-Magnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic vibration characteristics of permanent magnet linear synchronous motor considering the force-magnetic coupling are studied. In order to obtain more accurate vibration characteristics of the motor, the electromagnetic force is regarded as the applied stress, and the influence of the applied stress on the magnetostrictive effect and the magnetic permeability is introduced to construct the force-magnetic coupling relationship. Finally, the finite element software is used to analyze and verify the effect of considering the force-magnetic coupling relationship on the vibration characteristics of the motor.

articleTitle: Short-time annealing enhancing the magnetic properties and microstructure uniformity of melt-spun (Nd, Pr)-Fe-B ribbons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work, to solve the problem of poor uniformity of the melt-spun (Nd, Pr)-Fe-B ribbons obtained by direct rapid quenching, appropriate short-time annealing had been implemented. The microstructure and magnetic properties of the melt-spun (Nd, Pr)-Fe-B ribbons before and after annealing showed a significant improvement in the uniformity. The improvement of uniformity was beneficial for the application of melt-spun powders in bonded magnets and hot-deformed magnets, enhancing the magnetic properties of related products.

articleTitle: A Novel Speed Estimation Algorithm for a Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor Using Extended Kalman Filter with Multiple Fading Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A Suboptimal Multiple Fading Extended Kalman Filter (SMFEKF) for the permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM) is proposed to achieve accurate speed estimation and high reliability of the PMLSM sensorless drive system, which is under parameter mismatch and sudden load disturbance. Firstly, the dynamic mathematical model of the PMLSM is established. Secondly, an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is designed to estimate the speed and position of the PMLSM, and a SMFEKF is introduced to improve the estimation performance of the proposed algorithm under the parameter mismatch and sudden change of load conditions. Finally, the EKF and SMFEKF-based PMLSM systems are simulated and experimentally compared. The results show that the proposed algorithm can realize the accurate estimation of the speed and position of PMLSM under different conditions, and it is verified that the introduction of multiple fading factors can improve the estimation effect of the algorithm significantly.

articleTitle: Load Operations Analysis of a Hybrid Excited Flux Switching Vernier Alternator for Renewable Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This contribution presents the analysis under load conditions of the operation of an original hybrid excited flux switching Vernier machine designed to operate as a renewable energy generator. This machine can be used in renewable energy conversion applications, as wind turbine generator, or tidal turbine generator. The operations under different load conditions are analyzed both theoretically, using finite element models (FEM), and experimentally. The finite element models were developed during the design of this machine, prior to its construction. The comparison of the experimental study results with those obtained from the FEM will help assess the accuracy of developed models. The experimental study will also help assess the performance of the studied machine.

articleTitle: Exchange Bias Effects in Bismuth Ferrite Nanostructures Produced by Pulsed Laser Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Exchange bias properties in bismuth ferrite nanostructures produced by pulsed laser deposition with different mophologies are reported. Distinct bismuth ferrite nanostructures were obtained, driven by the background pressure in the deposition chamber: vacuum (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> Torr) and high pressures (0.25 and 4.0 Torr) of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and submitting them to a thermal treatment after deposition at 500°C. The bismuth ferrites nanostructures range from very compact thin-film (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>Torr), to clustered nanoparticles (0.25 Torr), to an arregement of nanoparticles contacting with fewer neighbours (4.0 Torr). The field-cooled magnetization curves of the nanostructures display a horizontal shift (exchange bias), and for clustered nanoparticles, the exchange bias coexists with a vertical shift. The magnetic properties are discussed considering the morphologies of the nanostructures and their role in the magnetic anisotropy and interaction between nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Design of LS-SynRM Rotor for Efficiency Improvement and Torque Ripple Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The motor is one of the most power-consuming electrical devices worldwide. Therefore, improving the efficiency of motors is a crucial factor in reducing power consumption and carbon emissions. The international standard IEC 60034–30 classifies the efficiency grades of motors and promotes efficiency improvement through regulations. Current research is underway to upgrade efficiency grades from IE3 to IE4. The induction motor, which is the most widely used industrial motor, has the drawback of inevitable eddy current flow in the rotor due to its operating principle, resulting in associated losses. On the other hand, LS-SynRM, based on the same principle, simplifies motor control during startup and incurs eddy current losses only during operation initiation, leading to improved efficiency. This paper focuses on the optimal design of the rotor to achieve efficiency grades of IE4 or higher for industrial LS-SynRM while minimizing torque ripple.

articleTitle: Innovative SynRM Rotor Design for Simplified Construction and Enhanced Mechanical Reliability in High-Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents a novel rotor geometry for high-speed synchronous reluctance motors (SynRM), where the rotor is drawn using a cosine function of the airgap length. This geometry can improve mechanical reliability in high-speed applications, such as in electric vehicles, by eliminating the need for flux barriers and making prototype construction easier. Initially, we present a brief review of the literature on high-speed SynRM, investigating the mechanical issues that might negatively affect their electromagnetic characteristics. After that, we discuss the proposed rotor design methodology. Then, electromagnetic results obtained through the numerical simulation of a 114 kW motor at 12000 rpm are shown, highlighting good torque and power density outcomes.

articleTitle: IMU-Based Robotic Finger Force Sensing with Modular Soft Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study introduces a novel force sensing method for soft robotic fingers using an array of inertial measurement units (IMU s) and modular soft actuators (MSAs). It overcomes the limitations of traditional methods like rotary encoders by transforming soft actuator components into virtual linkages. This simplification allows for direct application of Jacobian matrix to precisely calculate forces exerted by soft robotic fingers. When compared to traditional soft robots, the proposed method enables force control for the finger in both X and Y directions, which is thought to be significant for its enhanced accuracy and applicability in scenarios where conventional methods fail, broadening the scope of soft robotics in various applications.

articleTitle: A Study of Iterative Signal Processing Schemes for Double-Layered Bit-Patterned Recording
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To enhance the areal recording density of the alternated magnetic recording technologies, we have investigated the performances of the iterative recording schemes based on a double-layered bit-patterned magnetic recording (BPMR). We developed a read/write channel model that ideally integrates the signals from both upper and lower layers. In this study, we considered a two-layer recording that uses a single reader to retrieve a single readback signal through a signal combination produced from the upper and lower layers. For signal processing, we initially recover the upper layer signal and subsequently recover the lower layer signal using partial equalization and readback reconstruction schemes where the reproduced readback signals were generated under the iterative system. Based on the results, the proposed iterative signal processing schemes have been certified to deliver better bit error rate performance compared to single-layer BPMR systems, when they were considered at the total areal density of 4 Tb/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Simple PM Eddy Current Loss Model for Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a new simple model for fast calculating the PM eddy-current loss in axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) machine with considering the radial segmentation. Firstly, the PM eddy-current loss generation mechanism is revealed for AFPM with concentrated winding based on 3-D finite element analysis (FEA). Then, the relationship between PM eddy-current loss and magnet segmentation is derived by using the proposed model, and the segmentation loss coefficient is introduced to compare the error between the proposed method and 3-D FEA. Besides, the PM eddy-current loss is calculated and optimized under different conditions. Finally, a 60kW prototype with segmented PM is manufactured and tested to validate the proposed model.

articleTitle: The Harmonic-Balanced Finite Element Method with Laplace Transform for Transient State Nonlinear Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A harmonic-balanced finite element method (FEM) with the Laplace transform is proposed for transient state nonlinear problems. Different from the conventional harmonic-balanced method applying the Fourier transform, the implementation of the Laplace transform can make sure the simulation is accurate and more efficient for the convergence of transient state nonlinear problems. The strategies of taking the damping factor of the Laplace transform and the fixed-point reluctivity are investigated for the algorithm. To validate the method on problems with saturated magnetization, the simulation results are compared to the results of the conventional harmonic-balanced FEM with the Fourier transform in a 3D eddy current model under different exciting sources.

articleTitle: Effect of Tension and Compression Stress on the Magnetic Losses in a Low-Carbon Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: An experimental study of the evolution of magnetic losses in DC-04 steel under static mechanical stress was conducted. The material was subjected to uniaxial stress at levels from -90 MPa to 90 MPa, and the evolution of magnetic losses, from quasi-static regime to 300 Hz, was monitored. Remanent induction and coercive field were also recorded. All measurements were performed with controlled magnetic induction in a sinusoidal form. The analysis of these experimental results demonstrates the high non-linearity of the stress-loss relationship.

articleTitle: Optimization of Layer Thicknesses for Dual-Layer Bit-Patterned Media Recording (BPMR) Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To increase the areal recording density of magnetic recording, we have investigated the effect of the thicknesses of the individual layers in dual-layer bit-patterned magnetic recording (BPMR) systems. The recording media consisted of two, discrete recording layers, separated by a non-magnetic spacer layer. The bottom recording layer thickness and head-medium spacing (HMS) were fixed, while the top recording layer thickness was varied to adjust the spacing between the reader and the bottom layer. By varying the layer thicknesses, the readback signal strengths from the top and bottom layers can be adjusted and balanced. To determine the bit-errorrate improvement needed to reach a target areal density of 4.0 Tbits/in2, i.e. 2.0 Tbits/in2 per layer, the readback signal was processed using an iterative method. The results showed that the proposed design could outperform a single-layer BPMR system.

articleTitle: The Vibration Calculation Method for Gapped Cores Based on the Electric-Magnetic-Mechanical Coupling Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A new vibration calculation method for gapped cores is proposed to study the calculation of electromagnetic equipment containing cores. The magnetic circuit model is investigated by analyzing the air gap structures and magnetic flow direction. The vibration equivalent circuit model, based on the method of electromechanical analogy, is used to calculate the vibration displacement of transformer and reactor cores. Comparing the calculated results with the experimental data shows accuracy. The calculation time of this method is 5 seconds, which is much faster than 643s of finite element method, the calculation efficiency is greatly improved. This investigation provides a new scheme for the vibration and noise calculation of electromagnetic equipment.

articleTitle: A Novel Axial-Field Juxtaposed Magnetic Circuit Variable Flux Memory Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To achieve the goal of coexisting wide regulative speed range and high efficiency in high-speed operation, a novel axial-field juxtaposed magnetic circuit variable flux memory machine (AF-JMCVFMM) is proposed, which combines the high power density of axial-field permanent magnet machine (AFPMM) and wide speed regulation range of variable flux memory machine (VFMM). Firstly, the topology and variable flux principle are introduced. Subsequently, the main parameters are designed and optimized based on the equivalent magnetic circuit (EMC) and finite element method (FEM). Then, the electromagnetic performance of the proposed machines is compared and analyzed. The results indicate that the wide regulative speed range and the expansion of high efficiency region can be achieved by the proposed machines, which have profound prospects in the field of variable speed traction applications.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Experimental System for Thermomagnetic Coefficient Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The thermomagnetic coefficients play a pivotal role in converting heat to electricity in ferromagnetic systems. Specifically, the Anomalous Nernst Effect and Longitudinal Spin-Seebeck Effect show promise for energy conversion. However, traditionally, calculating thermomagnetic coefficients relies on a limited value of thermal gradient measurements due to experimental constraints. In this study, we introduce a novel experimental setup aimed at generating thermomagnetic curves with a significantly higher density of data points, enhancing the reliability of coefficient calculations. Our proposed setup enables the attainment of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> T values of up to 40 K without the thermal annealing on the films, due to the highly efficient thermal dissipation.

articleTitle: Design of a Linear Motor: An Optimization Approach Considering Motor and Inverter Losses with Different Voltage Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents the design and testing of a brushless permanent magnet linear motor to be used in a compressor application. Usually in the literature, optimization process focuses in the motor or the inverter optimization. However, voltage waveform generated by the inverter has direct influences in the motor and inverter losses. Here it was used a methodology that optimizes the motor taking into account motor and inverter losses models. In this sense, the process optimizes the efficiency of the motor and inverter set, resulting in a global optimum scenario. A two-step optimization process using a 3D analytical MEC routine and a 3D Finite Element software was used to simulate the linear motor. The optimization was carried out with two supply voltage waveforms. The first is the single pulse voltage and the second is the sinusoidal PWM waveform. The designed motor was assembled and tested in a dynamometer to evaluate the motor, inverter and set efficiency, supplied with both waveforms of voltage.

articleTitle: Investigation of High Torque Density Yokeless-Rotor PMSM with Large Diameter to Axial Length Ratio for Aircraft Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: High torque density is an important metric in the design of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) for aircraft electric propulsion. The yokeless-rotor PMSM is designed by multi-objective optimization and compared with the motor with rotor yoke to further improve the torque density. The influence of outer diameter in yokeless-rotor PMSMs is analyzed, revealing that excessively large diameter to axial length ratio will lead to the reduction of torque density. Furthermore, the 3D optimization is performed to analyze the end leakage flux effect, which realizes more precise optimization compared to the 2D multi-objective optimization.

articleTitle: Maximizing Competing Spin Current of the W/Pt/ferromagnet Devices with Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Using spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR), we investigated the spin-orbit torque (SOT) arising from the competing spin current (CSC) effect within a W/Pt/ferromagnet heterostructure. We maximized the CSC with an optimized W/Pt thickness ratio by separating the damping- and field-like torques with the ST-FMR. The stack design, with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, was subjected to current-induced SOT switching testing. It fully supports the conclusion obtained from the ST-FMR results.

articleTitle: Controlling Spin-Waves by Spin-Polarized Current for Logic and Neuromorphic Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Spin-waves (magnons) are among the prime candidates for building fast yet energy-efficient platforms for information transport and computing. We here demonstrate theoretically and in state-of-the-art micromagnetic simulation the effects that strategically-injected spin-polarized current can have on controlling magnonic transport. We reveal analytically that the Zhang-Li spin-transfer-torque induced by applied current is analogous to the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction for scattering the magnons in the linear regime, to then provide a generalized Snell's law that describes the spin-wave propagation across regions with different current densities. We validate the latter in numerical simulations of realistic systems, and exemplify how these findings may help advance the design of spin-wave logic and neuromorphic computing devices.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction of New Dual-Stator Machines Using Squirrel Stator Teeth in Uneven Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents two new dual-stator machines using squirrel teeth in uneven distribution (STUDDSMs), which have the merits of low cogging torque and low torque ripple. The proposed STUD can be designed by changed width (CW) and shifted position (SP) of squirrel stator teeth, which keeps the volume of squirrel stator equal. The airgap flux density can be modulated based on flux modulation effect and regulated according to the proposed STUD for high torque density and low total harmonic distortion, respectively. Then, the geometrical configurations of CW-STUDDSM and SP-STUDDSM are presented, in which they share the same key parameters for a fair comparison. The design consideration of these two STUDDSMs are provided, together with the cogging torque and steady torque are analyzed by finite element analysis. The analyzed results validate the employment of STUD can effectively decrease cogging torque and torque ripple.

articleTitle: Advanced Lumped Parameter Thermal Network for Modeling of Cooling Solutions in Electric Vehicle Motor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Electric motors utilized in electric vehicles are robust, efficient machines capable of delivering a wide spectrum of torque across their drive cycle. Throughout their operation, inevitable losses are incurred within the power system, primarily in the form of heat energy, which is directly proportional to the square of the current. Managing this heat energy necessitates suitable cooling methods to effectively counteract the generated heat during operation. Thermal analysis serves as a predictive tool to anticipate and address these thermal challenges and is often executed through finite element analysis (FEA). However, the utilization of FEA comes with extended computation times, prompting the exploration of alternative thermal analysis methods like the lumped parameter thermal network (LPTN). Unlike FE A, LPTN s do not face significant reconstruction time issues during the design stage, presenting an advantage in the development of potential motors. Presented is an enhancement to the conventional LPTN design while broadening the scope of the motor design process by introducing an LPTN cooling model. The objective is to implement this model in the early stages of electromagnetic design, particularly focusing on cooled housing development. Additionally, a case study involving a 13-kW induction motor was conducted through experimental testing to validate the proposed LPTN.

Index Terms: Energy In The Form Of Heat

articleTitle: Predicting Magnetic Losses in HGO Steel Sheets Under Distorted Induction Waveform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We show that the magnetic losses of thin high-permeability grain-oriented Fe-Si sheets can be coherently assessed under sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal induction waveform by the analytical formulations provided by the Statistical Theory of Losses. Results are provided regarding the energy loss measured in 0,18 mm thick commercial sheets under sinusoidal induction and its change, for given peak polarization value Jp, with the distortion introduced by a third harmonic of defined amplitude Jp3 and phase <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi_{3}$</tex> relationships with respect to the fundamental component. It is shown that accurate prediction of the 50 Hz losses at Jp = 1.7 T for distortion generated by third harmonic peak polarization ratio Jp3/Jp1 = 0.1, 0.2, and φ3 ranging between 0°and 180° can be made by the sole knowledge of the sinusoidal losses.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a New Consequent-Pole Hybrid Excited Permanent Magnet Machine with DC-biased Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A new consequent-pole hybrid-excited permanent magnet machine with DC-biased current (CPHEPM-DC machine) is proposed in this paper. The tooth located in the stator can be divided into two types: the main tooth and the auxiliary tooth. The five-phase multifunctional winding is adopted, which can be regarded as both the armature winding and the excitation winding. There are nine U-typed permanent magnets (PMs) placed in the rotor to improve the power density. In order to verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis, some electromagnetic properties, including the back electromotive force (back-EMF), the average output torque and the cogging torque are analyzed by the finite element (FE) method.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing of Nanoscale Displacements Through Detection of Magnetic Field Gradients with Magnetic Tunnel Junction Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: An array of magnetic tunnel junctions, connected in a Wheatstone bridge is characterized as a positioning sensor to detect spatial displacement of a magnetized object. In order to perform the experiment, the sensor was mounted at a fixed frame, and a micro-magnet was installed on top of nano-positioning stage. The movement of the stage was controlled by stepper motor and piezo-actuator in closed-loop feedback. The sensor signal was recorded in real time, to detect displacement of the magnet, defined by commands to the stage. The positioning transfer curves were obtained for different magnetization orientations of the magnet with respect to the field sensing direction of the MT J s and positioning direction of the magnet displacement. For the optimal configuration, giving linear transfer curve between positioning displacements and the sensor voltage, the effects of magnet size, sensor size and vertical distance between the sensor and magnet positioning trajectories, are characterized. In the optimized configuration, 10 nm steps resolution is obtained.

articleTitle: Research on High Performance TMR-Superconducting Composite Magnetic Sensor and Performance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR)-superconducting composite magnetic sensor, characterized by its high sensitivity, compact size, and low power consumption, exhibits significant potential for applications in weak magnetic field detection. Magnetic field resolution is a pivotal parameter in assessing the performance of the TMR-superconducting composite sensor in detecting weak magnetic fields. This study optimized the bonding process, leading to the successful fabrication of a TMR-superconducting composite sensor with an enhanced magnetic field resolution of 5.23pT/√Hz@1Hz. Expanding on this achievement, several strategies were employed to further enhance the sensor's magnetic field resolution, such as transitioning from bonding to coating techniques, implementing a constriction- folded structure for the superconducting loop, and refining the TMR film layer.

articleTitle: Fe-Cr-Nb-B Magnetic Particles for Cancer Cell Destruction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Fe-Cr-Nb-B type magnetic particles have shown great potential in applications related to cancer therapy. Their characteristics, such as size, shape and surface chemistry along with their magnetic properties make them suitable for applications such as magnetic hyperthermia, magneto mechanical actuation and chemotherapeutic drug loading and release, as well as the possibility of being transported using stem cells loaded with these particles. Furthermore, Fe-Cr-Nb-B type magnetic particles can be used to associate magnetomechanical effect on cancer cells with the effect of adsorbed and controlled release of anticancer drugs through magneto-mechanical actuation.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Voltage-Controlled Magnetic Anisotropy in Orthogonally-Magnetized CoFeB/MgO/CoFeB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) is crucial for advancing high-speed, low-power magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM). Here, we report the optimization of the VCMA coefficient in an orthogonally-magnetized CoFeB/MgO(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>)/CoFeB structure. By optimizing the MgO thickness, the VCMA value reaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{53}\ \mathbf{fJ}/\mathbf{V}\cdot \mathbf{m}$</tex> in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{t}=\mathbf{2.6}$</tex> nm sample, which has a 108.7% enhancement compared to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{t}=\mathbf{2}$</tex> nm counterpart. Moreover, by analyzing the MTJ capacitance with equivalent MTJ circuit model, we demonstrate that the improved VCMA coefficient is mainly attributed to the enlarged interfacial capacitance. Therefore, our work not only reveal the profound influence of barrier thickness on VCMA but also provide insights for the design of future VCMA-MRAM.

articleTitle: Systematic Optimization of Electromagnet Hardware for Electromagnetic Suspension: A Fusion of Simulation and Multi-Objective Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-objective optimization (MOO) framework for the design of electromagnets in electromagnetic suspension systems. Traditionally focused on mechanical properties, electromagnet design often necessitates subsequent control system adjustments. Our approach aims to streamline this process by integrating mechanical design with controller performance from the outset. The paper highlights the inefficiencies of iterative design due to long production lead times and presents a solution through our proposed MOO framework. Key contributions include the development of the framework and its application in the simulation of an electromagnet, demonstrating a more efficient and balanced design approach.

articleTitle: Spin-Orbit torque in α-W-Based Magnetic Tunnel Junction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Spin orbit torque (SOT) provides an efficient way to induce magnetization dynamics and switching of nanomagnets using electrical currents. In this study we present a SOT-induced magnetization switching in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\mathbf{W}$</tex>-based magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) with an effective in-plane magnetic anisotropy. 6-nm thick W is characterized by a relatively low resistivity and the spin-Hall angle of 0.1. In the MTJ nanopillars with an easy-axis oriented perpendicular to the current direction we observed a magnetization reversal with the current density approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7 \times 10^{11}\mathbf{A}/\mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex>

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of CeO2/g-C3N4 Nanocomposites: Structural, Morphological, Optical, and Magnetic Properties Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study investigates CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/g-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanocomposites synthesized hydrothermally, focusing on their structural, morphological, optical, and magnetic properties. CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, synthesized under varying conditions, exhibit high crystalline purity. Distinct morphologies are observed based on the molar ratio, impacting magnetization. Thermal treatment of g-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> enhances saturation magnetization, while unexpected variations in CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> /C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanocomposites suggest potential interfacial interactions. The study underscores the influence of the molar ratio on magnetic properties, contributing insights into multifunctional materials for potential applications and guiding future research.

articleTitle: A Tubular Flux-Reversal Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Linear Generator Used in Direct Drive Wave Energy Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Direct-drive wave energy converter (DDWEC) is more widely used due to its simple structure and high conversion efficiency. Different kinds of linear machines are used in DDWEC to improve the power density. Among them, transverse flux linear machine uses perpendicular magnetic flux path and axial stacked silicon steel sheets to reduce iron loss and enhance power density. In this paper, a flux-reversal transverse flux permanent magnet linear generator is proposed. The winding connection type of this configuration is elaborated. Circumferential three-phase type, axial three-phase type and the proposed one are compared to obtain higher power density and lower thrust ripple. The proposed three-phase winding configuration has the lowest thrust ripple (0.76%) and decent average thrust (247.01N).

articleTitle: Stress-Induced Magnetization Process in Shifted Grain-Oriented Steel Ring Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Electrical steel's magnetic properties in industrial applications often differ from theoretical predictions due to assembly-induced mechanical stresses. In this study, we evaluate the impact of compressive stress applied perpendicular to the core on the magnetic behavior of structures crafted with an innovative approach. Utilizing shifted grain-oriented Fe-Si steel rings, the strategy effectively alleviates magnetic losses and mitigates magnetostriction-related vibrations. Insights into complex magnetization processes are revealed through the analysis of first-order reversal curves (FORC), demonstrating stress-induced alterations in hysteresis loops and FORC diagrams. Under the applied stress, an additional magnetization process emerges at low magnetic fields, resulting from domain reorganization and interacting with the effects introduced by shifting the layers within the core.

articleTitle: Halbach Array Collaborative Robot End Effector for Advanced Handling of Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Handling of magnetic materials using robots is currently limited to end effectors that grasp using only compressive force, which can be problematic for unusually shaped objects, low energy conditions, or sensitive materials. An end effector designed for a ubiquitous collaborative robot, capable of handling them with magnetic force rather than compressive force, would prove to be intrinsic in the development of enhanced magnetic capabilities, especially for additive manufacturing. This work details the design of an actuatable pair of linear Halbach arrays on a parallel end effector of a collaborative robot as well as integrated coils and torque sensors to determine the magnetic moment of a material.

articleTitle: A Novel Winding Design for EV Traction Electric Motors: Hybrid Hairpin Winding Layout Containing Both Copper and Aluminum Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Emerging design considerations for future electric vehicle traction machines prioritize innovative hairpin winding designs that deliver superior electro-magnetic performance across a wider speed range while maintaining lightweight construction and cost-effectiveness. To address this challenge, incorporating aluminum as the winding material presents a viable solution due to its lightweight and cost-effective nature however, overcoming its higher ohmic losses, while meeting the higher performance targets remains a main critical obstacle to be addressed. In this respect, utilizing the analytical models: winding function-based model, and winding's AC loss estimation model, this paper proposed a novel hybrid hairpin winding design layout that combined the integer slot distributed windings (ISDW) and variable pitch concentric winding layouts for a commercially available traction machine. The hybrid winding layout incorporates both copper and aluminum windings, resulting in a reduction of 36.1% in winding weight and 46.6% in cost compared to the conventional ISDW design windings with only copper. Additionally, the hybrid winding layout exhibits higher electromagnetic performance including output power, torque, and efficiency, over wider speed range, encompassing both the maximum torque per ampere and field weakening regions

articleTitle: Magnetic Measurement System and Environmental Magnetic Field Compensation at CEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper describes the CEM's magnetic measurements laboratory roadmap, identifying the main objective and the essential steps to achieve it, aligned with the stakeholder's requirements. It details the establishment of a magnetic measurements laboratory to address the lack of national standards in Spain and ensure the traceability of magnetic measurements. The paper also outlines the measurement standards and field generation techniques depending on the measurement range, with particular emphasis on the active environmental magnetic field compensation.

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Computing with the Ferromagnetic/Antiferromagnetic SOT Systems: The Role of Emerging Antiferromagnetic Phase
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Field-free switching is pivotal for ushering in the era of high-density memory expansion. Field-free spin-orbit torque (SOT) switching is achieved by the W/Pt/Co/NiO/Pt device through perpendicular exchange bias under a minimal current density. A SOT-based memristor and current-induced gradual switching behavior are realized to construct spin-based artificial synapses and sigmoidal neurons for neuromorphic computing. An artificial neural network (ANN) is implemented to recognize MNIST handwritten digits and characters, achieving impressive accuracy rates of91~95%, depending on the robustness of the NiO antiferromagnetic ordering. Our finding opens promising pathways for advancing field-free spintronic devices and revolutionizing the landscape of neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of the Magnetoimpedance effect from Micromagnetism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A new self-consistent (fully coupled) numerical method is proposed for modeling the magnetoimpedance effect directly from fundamental magnetic properties. It accounts for the dependence of the permeability on both the applied magnetic field and the amplitude of the alternating field produced by the current. This is particularly challenging because the local value of the ac field in the sample is, in turn, governed by the permeability due to the skin effect. First, using a micromagnetic code, the permeability is calculated for all combinations of the applied external field and amplitude of the ac field. The results are then transferred to a finite element program to solve the Maxwell equations, which self-consistently determines the appronriate permeability and the amplitude of the ac field in each point of the sample. Results are presented for a strip of Permalloy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> long, 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> wide and 200 nm thick, confirming the effectiveness of the method to calculate the magnetoimpedance response from first principles.

articleTitle: Spin-Triplet Supercurrent Optimization in Ferromagnetic Josephson Junctions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Spin-triplet supercurrent with long-range propagation through ferromagnetic layers has been well established in theory and experiment [1] and the use of magnetic layers for switching the ground state phase across Josephson junctions between 0 and π has been experimentally demonstrated [2]. Combining the two effects to observe <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0-\pi$</tex> switching in a Josephson junction containing three noncolinear magnetic layers [3] has also been experimentally demonstrated [4]. Expanding on this idea, with careful control of magnetic layers in a noncoplanar configuration, it has been theoretically proposed that a device can be created which imparts an arbitrary phase difference across the junction [5], [6]. This demonstration of the Anomalous Josephson effect, a so-called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi_{0}$</tex> junction’, however, has yet to be realized in a system of conventional ferromagnets. We present two notable stepping stones toward this goal in the form of characterization of candidate patterned thin magnetic materials and transport measurements of candidate Josephson junction device structures.

articleTitle: Bright Envelope Solitons in the Double Negative Media Based on Thin Films of Nonlinear Ferromagnetic Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The paper presents the theoretical results that demonstrate the bright envelope soliton formation on a backward electromagnetic wave existing in a double negative medium based on a magnetized thin film of ferromagnetic semiconductor (FM SC). An analytical model of a magnetized ferromagnet containing magnetized cold and collisionless electron plasma is constructed based on the use of Maxwell's equations and material expressions including tensor functions of dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability. The nonlinearity of the FM SC is due to the dependence of magnetization on the amplitude of the high-frequency magnetic field. It is shown that one of the solutions of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation with coefficients depending on the electromagnetic properties of the BEMW has a form of a bright envelope soliton. The duration of such nonlinear pulses is controlled by the change of thickness of a FM SC film, strength of a magnetic bias field and electron concentration in plasma.

articleTitle: Unveiling a Bulk Antiferromagnetic Order via the Polarity of Spin-Orbit Torque Ratchet at Ferromagnet/Antiferromagnet Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Resolving the bulk order in an antiferromagnet (AFM) is technically difficult because of the absence of net magnetization in nature. Exchange-coupling, an AFM with a ferromagnet (FM) serves as an alternative approach to study the order of AFM via the exchange bias effect, however, it has been considered only revealing the order at the FM/AFM interface. This study reports an approach to unveil the bulk order of an AFM via the ratchet effect in an FM (Co)/AFM (IrMn)-based SOT device, which is associated with a hidden effect behind the exchange bias. It has been shown the ratchet polarity could be determined only when the exchange bias was completely facilitated, in which an analog (digital) switching was observed while the SOT switching was driven to be against (following) the direction of exchange bias. Although the exchange bias can be reversibly switched accompanying with SOT, but the built-in asymmetry via the ratchet polarity may reveal the hidden bulk order of IrMn. Finally, the plasticity on the SOT switching was observed with a tailorable threshold and the remarkable sensitivity in response to the various pulse-current modules. It suggests the Co/IrMn-based SOT device may be an ideal hardware system to be applied to the artificial neuron network for the advanced memory applications.

articleTitle: Determination Method of Nonlinear Reluctance Matrix Considering Saturation Differences for Three-Phase Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The transformer model and its parameters derived from the magnetic circuit have more physical significance, and it is also easier to converge in numerical calculations. The United Magnetic Equivalent Circuit (UMEC) model can well describe the coupling between phases of the three-phase transformer. The UMEC model considers the nonlinear characteristics of the port reluctance when determining the reluctance matrix, but it does not consider the differences of the nonlinear characteristics for each reluctance. This article proposes a nonlinear reluctance iterative method that considers phase differences. At each time step, the nonlinear characteristics of ferromagnetic materials are used to iteratively calculate the reluctance and the magnetic flux flowing through it to obtain a more accurate reluctance matrix. The new method can more accurately describe the saturation differences between phases. The parameters in the nonlinear reluctance matrix can be deduced from the transformer nameplate data, it is beneficial for the practical application of this transient model. A calculation program for the proposed three-phase transformer model was written in C++ language, and compared with the method that ignores the nonlinear differences in each reluctance.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Computing with p-Bits: Optimization, Machine Learning and Quantum Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The increasing computational demands of the modern AI has been in steady conflict with the slowing down of Moore's Law driven era of electronics.
