To meet the demands of AI in the new era, augmenting existing complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology with emerging technologies has become a promising new direction. One research thread along this line is the notion of physical computing, where a set of computational tasks are mapped onto a programmable “computer” whose natural physics leads to desired outcomes for computational problems. What is different from traditional computers in this approach is a shift from the focus of general-purpose to domain-specific computing. One example is probabilistic computing with fluctuating probabilistic bits (p-bit) that are conceptually in between bits and qubits. Among many possible implementations, p-bits that use the inherent stochasticity of magnetic tunnel junctions is emerging as one of the most scalable, energy-efficient and manufacture-ready option and their scaled implementation could be of particular use in a variety of applications in combinatorial optimization, machine learning and quantum simulation. Below, I discuss the rapid pace of progress of this field from device, architecture and algorithmic perspectives.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Co2FeGa Heusler Alloy Films grown by Sputtering Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The influence of growth conditions on the structural and magnetic properties of polycrystalline Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeGa Heusler alloy thin films prepared by sputtering deposition on Si substrate is investigated by XRD, VSM and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">57</sup>Fe conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy (CEMS). The CEMS and VSM results suggest that the films grown and annealed for a short time (1 h) at 873 K are highly ordered, with L21 structure, potentially favoring a high spin polarization. The formation of D03 ordering in the thin films is ruled out.

articleTitle: Frequency Sensitivity Analysis of Magnetoquasistatic System with Voltage or Current Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study proposed a higher-order frequency sensitivity analysis (FSA) of magneto-quasistatic (MQS) system driven by either voltage or current intensity excitation. Variational formulations for the FSA were derived from the voltage- or current-driven MQS system by differentiation with respect to angular frequency. Instead of a discrete approach, this study employed a continuum one, which results in the frequency sensitivity of an analytical form. The frequency sensitivity was expressed in terms of a magnetic vector potential (MVP), an electric scalar potential (ESP), and a source ESP. The higher-order frequency sensitivity was sequentially derived from the lower-order one by repeating differentiation. Due to the continuum approach, the frequency sensitivity was evaluated before the discretization process of the finite element method, and its numerical analysis could be easily implemented by using commercial finite element software. Two numerical examples were presented to demonstrate theoretical validity and numerical applicability of the FSA.

articleTitle: The Potential of SmCo4B-Based Compounds as a Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The SmCo4B-based magnets are of interest as they exhibit extremely high anisotropic field (~65 T), thus having a significant potential for high coercivity (~up to 20 T). However, their use in practical applications is limited due to low saturation. To tackle this, we substitute Sm and Co with N d and Fe, respectively. In this work, the intrinsic magnetic properties of SmCo4B, SmCo3.sFeo.2B, and Smo.7Ndo.3Co3.sFeo.2B are investigated by using PPMS up to 14 T, vertical single coil turn up to 100 T, and non-destructive pulse coil up to 60 T to understand their potential in permanent magnet applications. The magnetization increases from 0.35 T for SmCo4B to 0.55 T for SmN dCoFeB, with a decrement in the anisotropy field to 35 T at 300 K. These results demonstrate a potential as permanent magnets for substituted SmCo4B-based magnets.

articleTitle: Shape Optimization of Electric Motors Using 2.5-D Continuum Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents a new shape optimization method of the electric motor which efficiently reflect the 3D properties. 2.5-D Continuum sensitivity is formulated by using the concept of material derivative for the objective function. When the variables are numerically analyzed in the 3D design problem, the average value on the design boundary variable is calculated and applied to the 2D design velocity. Optimization proceeds by transforming the updated motor shape to the 3D shape. To perform this proposed method, the shape design for the 4-pole synchronous reluctance motor was conducted.

articleTitle: Flux-driven Nonlinear Transient Model for Single Phase Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: When transformers experience transient processes such as over voltage and switching, its port current exhibits significant nonlinear distortion. The magnetic flux distribution inside the transformer also changes when the current distorts. This means that the topology of the transformer's magnetic circuit and its parameters are also changing. To accurately reflect this change, this article proposes a topology selection method driven by magnetic flux. In time-domain simulation, the magnetic flux of the port is taken as the characteristic value, and different topologies are called based on the characteristic value. The nonlinear parameters in the topology can be derived from easily obtained nameplate data. Finally, the transient model was implemented in C++ and compared with the simulation results of PSCAD to verify its feasibility and accuracy.

articleTitle: Towards the Development of Coercivity by Low Temperature Densification of Nd(Fe,Mo)12N Intermetallic Compounds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: REFe12 intermetallics (RE being a rare earth) are considered as the strongest candidates for alternative high-performance permanent magnet material, thanks to the combination of high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, high Curie temperature and moderate saturation magnetization. However, the development of a well-adapted microstructure, including a paramagnetic/non-magnetic intergranular phase with low melting point, as in the case of NdFeB magnets, is necessary in order to develop the coercivity and remanent magnetization. In the case of Nd-based 1:12 compounds, the densification may prove to be difficult due to the necessity of nitrinding the compounds, which conducts to a strong reduction of the stability of the 1:12 phase, as the decomposition temperature of the nitride is strongly reduced. In this work we present a study on the low temperature densification of the Nd(Fe,Mo)12N compound promoted by a low melting intergranular phase, as is the case of Nd-Cu or La-Cu.

articleTitle: Structural and Magnetic Characterization of a Ferrofluid Obtained Through an Economical Way of Chemical Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The structural and magnetic characterization of several batches of ferrofluids produced by an economical co-precipitation production method that allows obtaining the material in a relevant quantity for use in technological applications was carried out. These ferrofluids are composed of magnetite nanoparticles stabilized with citrate in aqueous suspension. Structural characterization was done by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), Small-Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS), and Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS). The results indicate the presence of iron oxides like magnetite (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>04). The average crystallite diameter is 8 nm (XRD), 6.0 nm (TEM) and 6.9 nm (SAXS). Magnetization vs temperature measurements are consistent with a wide distribution of small sized particles and superparamagnetic behavior, also corroborated in the magnetization vs magnetic field measurements. Saturation magnetization Ms is around 90 Am<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Ikg. Repeatability of the process was ascertained.

articleTitle: First-Principles Study of Saturation Magnetization Flux Density in Nitrogen Defective ɑ'-Fe8Nx
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Saturation magnetization flux density (Bs) in nitrogen defective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_{8}\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> was investigated by means of the first-principles density functional theory. Total 443 quasi-disordered structures consisting randomly distributed interstitial nitrogen in bcc iron were constructed and the corresponding magnetization and cell volume were calculated. The value of Bs was derived by using the magnetization and the cell volume as a function of the nitrogen concentration. It was found that the nitrogen defective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> is more stable than disordered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_{8}\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> in all nitrogen concentration, indicating that the increase of Bs in nitrogen defective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> occur by annealing process. Our calculation also reproduced an increase of magnetization of the stoichiometric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_{8}\mathrm{N}$</tex> due to the ordering of interstitial nitrogen.

articleTitle: Synthetic Antiferromagnetic/Ferromagnetic Spin-Orbit Torque Devices with an Oxide Spacer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We obtained an oscillatory RKKY nature within the Pt/Co/NiO/Co/Pt stack by changing NiO thickness. This allowed us to develop spin-orbit torque (SOT) devices featuring synthetic antiferromagnetic (AFM) and ferromagnetic (FM) couplings. Field-free switching with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was achievable in AFM- and FM-coupled devices. Nevertheless, a lower switching current density but a larger switching percentage were obtained in the AFM compared to the FM case. The interlayer exchange coupling strength of the NiO was estimated to be close to that of metallic Wand Ta as a spacer material.

articleTitle: Deflection Patterns on Strontium Ferrite/Iron Oxide/Ecoflex 00-30 Flexible Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work we have demonstrated a novel methodology on improving magnetic properties of flexible magnetic actuators. This was done by taking advantage of the exchange spring technique in which hard magnetic materials are enhanced by the addition of soft magnetic ones. Here we have combined iron oxide (Fe3O4) particles with strontium ferrite ones in a flexible matrix (Ecoflex 00–30) with the goal of increasing the bending capacity of samples when exposed to the same magnetic field. Results showed that, although a higher concentration of particles leads to higher stiffness, the addition of iron oxide particles to these composites has increased the bending capabilities. This technique offers another degree of freedom in the design of hard magnetic flexible materials, and can be used as a tool to manufacture soft magnetic robots with more complex capabilities.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Structural Scale of Hollow Particles and Core-Shell Particles on the Properties of Magnetorheological Fluids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Sedimentation resistance is undoubtedly the most relevant rheological property of magnetorheological fluids. Typically, researchers use hollowing or coating of magnetic particles to reduce the density difference between the particles and the carrier liquids, thereby improving the anti-sedimentation properties of magnetorheological fluids. However, the treated particles lose their magnetic properties, which in turn reduces the yield stress of magnetorheological fluids. In order to study the effects of coating thickness and hollow radius on yield stress and settlement velocity, the expressions of relative shear stress and relative settlement velocity of particles under the two structures were established based on the two-particle configuration, and the mechanical properties and anti-settlement properties of the two particle structures were compared. It is found that there is a scale range, and when the hollowness and coating thickness of the particles are within this range, the hollow structure not only exhibits better anti-sedimentation but also has less loss of yield stress. In other words, within this scale range, hollow structures are better than coating structures. This research has a theoretical guide for the preparation of high-performance magnetorheological fluids.

articleTitle: Computational Speed Improvement of Reluctance Network Analysis Combined with Play Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve the solution convergence of the reluctance network analysis model incorporating the play model by decomposing the DC hysteresis characteristics into linear and nonlinear terms and applying the play model only to the latter. In this way, it is possible to increase the width of a time step by converging the solution in nonlinear iterative calculation and, as a result, to shorten calculation time by reducing the number of time steps.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Dynamic Magnetic Properties in RuO2/Co-Fe-B Stack Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We present the research on the fabrication of RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and the change in dynamic magnetic properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{RuO}_{2}/\text{Co-Fe-B}$</tex> stack films with various Co-Fe-B thicknesses <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(t_{\text{CFB}})$</tex>. The damping constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex> and effective magnetization <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(4\pi M_{\text{s,eff}})$</tex> in these stacking films were evaluated by using the broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurement technique. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\pi M_{\text{s,eff}}$</tex> decreases with the decrease of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\text{CFB}$</tex>, which might be attributed to the increase of the interfacial anisotropy energy. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> increases with the decrease of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\text{CFB}$</tex> which might be attributed to contribution of the spin pumping, and/or the magnetic inhomogeneity in the stacking films.

articleTitle: Magnetically Actuated Compliant Soft Robotic Gripper for Grasping Delicate Food Items
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study focuses on the development and assessment of an innovative soft robotic gripper, activated by an electromagnet (specifically, a solenoid), designed for the delicate handling of unpackaged vegetables and fruits within the food industry. The study introduces a soft gripper, configured as two flexible opposing fingers capable of gently gripping fragile food products. The primary objectives of this design include achieving compactness, lightness, simplicity, and a reduction in overall system complexity. The flexible two-finger appendages were fabricated through 3D printing using a fused filament fabrication (FFF) method with soft elastic thermoplastic polyurethane filament material. To evaluate the gripper's performance across diverse rigid object characteristics, including different sizes, surface asperities, and shapes, holding forces were empirically measured using an Instron testing machine. The study concludes by demonstrating the practical feasibility of the soft electromagnetic gripper, showcasing its ability to successfully grasp a variety of delicate natural food items with differing sizes, shapes, and weights.

Author Keywords: Fragile and delicate food products handling

articleTitle: Coercive Force as an Indicator of Structural Changes in the Heat Treatment of Amorphous and Nanocrystalline Alloys on the Example of Fast-Quenched Fe-Cu-Nb-Si-B Tapes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The potential of coercive force as a structurally sensitive characteristic for amorphous and nanocrystalline alloys has not been sufficiently disclosed, partly because the physical mechanisms of the occurrence of magnetic hysteresis in such alloys are under active study. The paper shows that the behavior of the coercive force during heat treatment of Fe-Cu-Nb-Si-B alloys in both the amorphous and nanocrystalline states reflects more subtle processes in changing their structure than those that can be observed by traditional methods, for example, scanning calorimetry.

Author Keywords: dependence of soft magnetic properties on annealing temperature

articleTitle: A Novel Characterization Method for Transformer Interturn Short-Circuit Faults Based on Arc-Induced Transients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This digest proposes a novel characterization method for transformer interturn short-circuit faults using the transients in the change of winding magnetomotive force (MMF) caused by the zero-off effect of the fault arc. To enhance the clarity and regularity of these transient features, the signals of winding MMF variations are analyzed using variational mode decomposition (VMD), with the optimized VMD parameters selected by particle swarm optimization (PSO). To validate this characterization method, calculations and experiments for interturn short-circuit faults are carried out on a specifically designed transformer. The results confirm that the arc resistance as a load induces transients in the change of winding MMF as the short-circuit circulating current passes through zero, affirming the viability of this characterization method for actual interturn fault identification applications.

articleTitle: Self-Generation of Spatiotemporal Parametric Patterns in Active Ring Resonators Based on Single- and Bicomponent Magnonic Quasicrystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The paper presents the experimental results that demonstrate the formation of spatiotemporal parametric patterns in active ring resonators based on one-dimensional single- and bicomponent magnonic quasicrystals (MQCs). Such patterns are formed through the nonlinear parametric three-wave decay of a magnetostatic surface spin wave (MSSW). It is shown that in the active ring resonator based on the single-component MQC made from a ferrite film, the spatial patterns of magnetization are localized in the grooves at a MSSW frequency and in the crests at a frequency of parametrically excited spin waves (SWs). In the active ring resonator based on the bicomponent MQC (the ferromagnetic permalloy strips located on a ferrite film surface), the magnetization localization is observed in free parts of the ferrite film both at the MSSW frequency and at the frequency of parametrically excited SWs.

articleTitle: Suppressing the Three-Phase Flux Linkage Asymmetry of Modular Flux-Switching Permanent-Magnet Linear Machine by Rearranging Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This article proposes a winding rearrangement method to address the asymmetric flux linkage of the modular flux-switching permanent-magnet linear machine (FSPMLM). Due to the end effect, the two-end winding flux linkages respectively shift in a positive and a negative direction, with respect to the middle winding. In the proposed method, the two ends of the windings are connected to the same phase, while the rest are rearranged and the module spacing is adjusted. Ultimately, the three-phase superposition flux linkages are almost symmetric. The finite element analysis is used to verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Drag Force Analysis of Superconducting EDS Type Hyperloop System According to Changes in Tube Material Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a study on the electromagnetic drag force analysis of a hyperloop system for traveling up to 1200 km/h by installing superconducting electromagnets (SCMs) in the vehicle's bogie and mounting coreless linear synchronous motors (LSMs) in a vacuum tube with an electrodynamic suspension (EDS) system. The tube of the hyperloop system is made of steel to withstand the sub-vacuum condition about 0.001 atm, but when a superconducting coreless LSM is used as a propulsion system, there is no magnetic material that can shield the strong magnetic field caused by the SCM, and then eddy currents caused by the magnetic field may occur in the tube steel. The eddy currents generated in the tube steel generate drag forces that impede the driving of the vehicle, which in turn becomes the driving resistance of the hyperloop system. In order to explore the drag force characteristics, this paper studied the theoretical causes of electromagnetic drag, and based on the theoretical background, studied the drag force variation depending on the material properties of the tube steel.

articleTitle: Sound as an Additional Tool for Spin-Wave Dynamics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Analysis of complex data such as spin wave behavior requires the use of sophisticated visualization techniques, which might not always be enough. An approach to combining data sonification with interactive visualization of a spin-wave transient response in confined Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8o</inf>Fe2o microstrips of different shapes on uniform MW field excitation is discussed in this work. Developed prototype has been successfully presented in the science-communication framework at a digital art exhibition.

articleTitle: Analysis of the High-Frequency Magnetization Process Through Machine Learning and Topological Data Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The study of the high-frequency magnetization process is crucial for advancing technologies like electric vehicles and 6G communication systems. We employ Topological Data Analysis (TDA) and machine learning to explore the magnetization process in materials at frequencies up to 100 KHz. Our approach involves analyzing the microstructures affecting magnetization dynamics, aiming to enhance power device efficiency. Utilizing a high-resolution magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) microscope, we visualize magnetic domains at varying frequencies. Persistent homology, a TDA method, is used to convert topological features into vectors, which are then processed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to capture the significant information. This study also addresses the challenge of machine learning explainability in material science, correlating algorithm outputs with physical phenomena.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Inductance Matrix Modeling Method for Multi-Winding Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: There is often a negative inductance in the equivalent circuit model of a multi-winding transformer, which may cause oscillations in the system's solution. This paper proposes a method for establishing a nonlinear matrix model for multi-winding transformers. The number of parameters to be solved in the matrix model matches the port experimental results, and its nonlinear characteristics can be determined by the transformer nameplate data provided by the manufacturer without additional measurements, which is highly reliable and accurate. The proposed matrix model helps to improve the efficiency of power system solving and greatly reduces measurement costs, it is a simple, accurate and highly worthy of application in system simulation.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Models of Nonlinear Magnetic Behavior Laws for Finite Element Modeling of Iron Losses in a Toroidal Core
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper explores the implications of nonlinear anisotropic behavior models on the simulation of magnetic losses in a toroidal core made of a conventional Grain-Oriented Electrical Steel (GOES) within a finite element method (FEM) simulation environment. GO laminations are commonly used to improve the efficiency of electrical machines, but their complex behavior requires accurate modeling. Nonlinear resolutions for different anisotropy models were implemented and compared with a measurement-based model. Then, an anisotropic iron loss model from Appino et al. has been applied to evaluate the iron losses. This method provides a decisive way to qualitatively assess various models directly, relying on measurable quantities of interest.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electrical Modelling of Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Tunnel Junctions with Temperature Dependent Magnetic Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A magnetic tunnel junction, or an MTJ, is a spintronic device of nanoscale dimensions. It is a magneto-electric device that can hold two definite resistance states according to its magnetization states. MTJs can be used as memory elements due to their non-volatile nature. They can be fabricated into chips using VLSI techniques. The main applications of MTJs include computer memory, logic, and neuromorphic computing. This work focuses on the modelling of Spin Transfer Torque and Voltage-Controlled Magnetic Anisotropy Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (STT-VCMA MTJs) using a SPICE-based simulation approach. The study incorporates thermal effects, such as temperature-dependent variations in key parameters like saturation magnetization, spin polarization, uniaxial anisotropy, and VCMA coefficient. Simulations reveal the impact of these temperature-dependent parameters on the switching behavior of MTJs. The results demonstrate that incorporating thermal effects is crucial for accurately capturing the dynamic behavior of MTJs, shedding light on the temperature-sensitive aspects of their operation. This work contributes to the understanding and development of robust SPICE models for STT-VCMA MTJs, facilitating their integration into larger electronic systems and supporting the exploration of novel memory technologies.

articleTitle: Simulations of Experimentally Detected Ambient Skyrmions in Symmetric Synthetic Antiferromagnetic Multilayers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topological solitons consisting of non-collinear spin textures that display promising properties for spintronic information storage and logic devices. A type of system that has been proposed to host 2D skyrmions in room-temperature and zero magnetic field conditions, is the synthetic antiferromagnetic multilayer, composed of ferromagnetic layers that exhibit antiparallel RKKY coupling mediated by a non-magnetic spacer. In this work, we performed micromagnetic simulations to complement an experimental investigation about ambient skyrmions in Pt/Co/Ru/Co/Pt multilayers, assessing their magnetization reversal properties and coupled skyrmion stability.

articleTitle: Effect of Curie Temperature Distributions on the Areal Density Capability of Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The effect of Curie temperature distributions and average grain size on the areal density capability of heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) media was calculated. For a target areal density of 2 Tbit/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>the average grain size should be less than 5.3 nm and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma T_{c}$</tex> should be less than 25 K.

articleTitle: Development of Interdented Devices for Surface Acoustic Waves (SAW) Applied to Magnonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Advances in the field of spintronics in the last decades have instigated new approaches to overcome the limit on the propagation length of spin waves (SW). This makes the use of SW a promising prospect for applications in electronic devices in the process of transmitting digital information. So, this work aimed to develop a surface acoustic wave (SAW) device to excite spin waves through their interaction with elastic waves that arise from excitations of the crystalline structure, which are quantized as phonons. These elastic waves are generated by interdigital transducers (IDT) placed over a piezoeletric material.

articleTitle: Effect of Magnetostriction on the Vibrations of Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this article, a vibration coupling model of PMLSM considering magnetostriction is established based on the relationship between magnetic field and magnetostriction strain. The influence of tooth flux density saturation on vibration caused by magnetostriction under overload condition are analyzed by finite element model. The frequency characteristics of PMLSM vibration caused by magnetostriction are verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Structural and Magnetic Properties of Ultrathin Films Calculated from First-Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Ultra-thin magnetic films, ranging in thickness from a single atomic monolayer to several dozen atomic layers, show a variety of structural and magnetic properties that distinguish them from thicker films and bulk materials. In this work, we summarize the results obtained for the following ultrathin magnetic layers: Fe (001), Fe (111), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{L}\mathbf{1}_{0}$</tex> FeNi (001, 100, 111), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{L}\mathbf{1}_{0}$</tex> FePt (100, and 111), FeCo-(B,C,N), transition-metal monolayers in Fe matrix, and heterostructures: MgO/Fe, Ru/FeO, and Au/Fe. Using the density functional theory-based full-potential local-orbital (FPLO) code, we obtained a range of structural, electronic and magnetic properties for the above structures. The obtained results correlate well with experimental studies and have potential for application in most cases.

articleTitle: Effect of Ge Doping on the Martensitic Transformation and Magnetoelectric Behavior of Ni42Co8Mn39Sn11-xGex Melt-Spun Ribbons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work we study the effect of Ge substitution for Sn on the martensitic transformation, Curie temperature in the austenite phase, and magneto-electric behavior of the Heusler type alloy ribbons Ni42Co8Mn39Sn11-xGex with x = 0, 1, 2, 3 (at. %) prepared by the so-called continuous rapid quenching method. These samples were labeled as Sn11Ge0, Sn10Ge1, Sn9Ge2, and Sn8Ge3 for x = 0, 1, 2, 3, respectively. The Curie temperature and martensitic transformation were determined using a thermogravimetry analyzer (TGA-Q500 TA Instruments) and a differential scanning calorimeter (DSC-Q100 TA Instruments). The thermogravimetry measurements were conducted in presence of small dc magnetic field, H ∼ 2 Oe, to determine the Curie temperature in the austenite phase of the samples. The magneto-electric behavior was investigated using Hall effect measurements at room temperature. A comparison between magnetic thermograms, their temperature derivatives and DSC curves reveal that the samples suffer a martensitic transformation followed of a magnetic phase transition. The enthalpy values involved in the martensitic transformation (0.404 J/g, 4.39 J/g, 8.31 J/g, 11.55 J/g), respectively. The Curie temperature values in the austenite phase for Sn11Ge0, Sn10Ge1, Sn9Ge2, and Sn8Ge3 are 146.1 ± 0.1 °C, 137.2 ± 0.1 °C, 124.3 ± 0.1 °C, and 104.8 ± 0.1 °C, respectively. This result indicates that the exchange interaction weakens with increasing Ge content. The Hall effect experiments reveal an ordinary and extraordinary contribution to the Hall effect and a positive Hall coefficient.

articleTitle: Magnetization Reversal and Direct Observation of Magnetic Domains on FePt Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In ferromagnetic thin films, the presence of an out-of-plane component of the magnetic anisotropy may induce a transition from planar to stripe-like magnetic domains above a critical thickness, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{t}_{\mathbf{c}}$</tex>. Because of the changes in the domain structure, important changes in the magnetization reversal mechanisms are observed. We present the analysis of the magnetization reversal in FePt thin films, where this phenomenon is observed, through the experimental observation of magnetic domains by magneto-optic Kerr effect microscopy. The observed reversal mechanisms are strongly dependent on the thickness of the sample. For t<tc, the reversal process is a combination of domain wall movement and rotation of domains. Meanwhile, for t>tc, the stripe-domain structure determines the magnetization reversal.

articleTitle: Unsaturated Modes of Ferromagnetic Resonance in Maghemite Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this study, we present an investigation of Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) at various microwave frequencies (1.1 GHz, 3.5 GHz, 9.4 GHz, and 33.9 GHz) for maghemite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\gamma}-\mathbf{Fe}_{\mathbf{2}}\mathbf{O}_{\mathbf{3}})$</tex> nanoparticle samples in both powder and aqueous ferrofluid forms. Their structure was confirmed through X-ray Diffraction (XRD), revealing an average diameter of 12.1 nm. Analysis of the FMR spectra obtained at room temperature (RT) suggests that the samples are in a non-saturated state for microwave frequencies below 10 GHz.

articleTitle: The Scalable Analytical Model for Predicting the Performance of SPM Machine with Arbitrary Magnet Shape
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper develops the scalable analytical model (SAM) for predicting the performance of the surface-mounted permanent-magnet (SPM) machine with the arbitrary magnet shape and magnetization direction. The magnets are finitely divided into rectangles based on the magnetization direction and then they are replaced by the equivalent magnet currents along the surface of the magnets. Based on the SAM, the air-gap field of the SPM machine can be obtained considering the iron nonlinearity. The proposed method is useful for accelerating the optimization process of the torque ripple reduction in the servo motor application. The finite-element method (FEM) is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Maximum-Torque-Per-Watt Control Framework for Variable Flux Reluctance Machines with Magnetic Saturation and Cross-Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper suggests a maximum-torque-per-watt (MTPW) control approach for a variable flux reluctance machine (VFRM), considering factors like the machine's magnetic saturation and cross-coupling between field and armature windings, which are both located in the stator of the VFRM. The VFRM's torque production, which can be highly affected by saturation, relies on the cross-coupling between field and armature windings, and on the varying field and armature currents. The operating points on the torque-speed locus are determined by different combinations of these currents. The paper presents a strategy to obtain the optimum combination of reference field and armature currents based on a saturation-dependent model with a focus on minimizing the total copper loss. The proposed method is to be validated on a VFRM drive simulation, and experimentally.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Modeling AE-Effect Magnetic Field Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In recent years, magnetoelectric ΔE-effect sensors have been investigated to detect small amplitude and low-frequency magnetic fields. Much progress has been made in understanding the complex interplay of magnetic, mechanical, and electrical properties and their influence on the signal and noise of the sensor system. This holds for different designs of magnetoelectric resonators but also for surface acoustic wave devices. Experimental and theoretical advancements will be reviewed and presented, including the first steps toward applications and arrays with many miniaturized sensor elements. Limitations and prospects will be discussed critically, such as performance variations and strategies to improve signal and noise. A novel origin of magnetic noise owing to the nonlinearity of magnetostriction will be revealed, which applies to all sensor devices incorporating magnetic materials. The results contribute significantly to understanding the limitations of magnetic sensors and provide essential guidelines for optimizing future ΔE-effect sensors.

articleTitle: Vortex-state in Iron Nanodisks: Formation and Response in Water Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The magnetic vortex state has been widely studied in soft magnetic alloys such as Permalloy (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>). However, the morphological conditions for this unique spin configuration in single-element Fe nanodisks are not defined yet. Fe is an interesting material for magnetic-based biomedical applications due to its biocompatibility and high magnetization. This work investigates the spin structure of Fe nanodisks as a function of thickness and diameter. Nanodisks were fabricated with thicknesses of 20 - 150 nm and diameters of 300 - 1000 nm. Magnetometry measurements allowed us to determine the geometrical conditions for the formation of a spin-vortex configuration. Furthermore, the magnetic response of Fe-nanodisks in water solutions was analyzed at low frequency magnetic fields. The results bound the dynamic limits of these nanostructures in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Influence of Interactions in the Behavior of Magnetic Nanoparticle Agglomerates: Experiments and Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This presentation discusses the effects of magnetic nanoparticle (MNP) aggregation on a series of experimental measurements related to magnetic fluid hyperthermia (MFH). The investigation focuses on different agglomerate structures, especially those with elongated shapes. We analyze the influence of interparticle interactions through a combination of theoretical and experimental approaches. First, a novel perspective on magnetic behaviour is provided through the comparison of numerical simulations of non-interacting MNPs and chain systems, with magnetic anisotropy as a key parameter for the determination of the specific power absorption in MFH experiments. This view provides consistency to conflicting reports regarding interaction effects on the heating response. Second, we study cytosol phantoms with dispersed and oriented MNPs, extending our understanding beyond the initially simulated ideal chains. A novel method is employed to produce spatiotemporal 2D maps during MFH experiments which facilitates the identification of spatial MNP arrangements and their effect on the heating response. Finally, we were able to reproduce ac hysteresis loop measurements for these phantoms through the modeling of interactions in an effective way. This is achieved using input from previous simulations and experiments such as cryo FIB-SEM images of the phantoms.

articleTitle: Magnetoelastic Constraint on Sensor-Intrinsic Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Intrinsic magnetic noise limits the functionality of most magnetic field sensors. This study investigates the impact of intrinsic magnetic noise on the performance of magnetoelectric magnetic field sensors, at the example of two sensor concepts based on the ΔE effect and the converse magneto electric effect, respectively. Our analysis shows that they exhibit comparable behavior in terms of noise and operational limitations. In both cases, the magnetic properties of the magnetostrictive layer determine the theoretical minimum of the equivalent magnetic noise density. The range of operational parameters with which this minimum can be achieved is constrained by the magnetic noise source linked to the nonlinearity of the magnetostrictive properties. This previously unidentified noise source significantly degrades sensor performance and imposes a strict limit on the acceptable noise level of the nonmagnetic noise sources in the sensor system. Although this noise source is particularly evident in highly magnetostrictive materials, it can be relevant to a wide range of devices incorporating magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Enhancing Noise and Vibration Performance for a Traction Squirrel Cage Induction Machine Through Rotor Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The squirrel cage induction machines (SCIMs) are widely employed in electric vehicles (EVs) owing to their rugged construction and cost-effectiveness in maintenance. However, the efficient performance of the SCIM largely depends on the electromagnetic design of its rotor, while also taking into account the critical aspects of noise and vibration (NV). This paper focuses on the concurrent modification of the rotor slot and bar shapes of one traction SCIM to meet the dual objectives of optimizing traction performance and fulfilling NV requirements.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Spin-Transfer Torque assist Spin-Orbit Torque Magneti-zation Switching under In-plane External Field Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The 3-Dimensional Domain Wall Magnetic Memory (3D-DWMM) is regarded as the next generation magnetic memory with incredible storage density exceeding 30 Tb/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is unattainable for today's MRAM. For the writing process, implementing spin-transfer torque (STT) and spin-orbit torque (SOT) simultaneously is a suitable approach for 3D-DWMM. In previous research, we fabricated a GMR device, and studied the STT assist SOT switching experimentally, discovered the STT assist efficiency was dependent on external field. In this study, we employed micromagnetic simulation to analyze how external field affect the STT-SOT switching as well as the switching efficiency. The experimental STT-SOT switching was successfully reproduced by the simulation, and it was found that STT torque deviates the memory layer magnetization from the initial direction, which contributes the reduction of SOT switching current density.

articleTitle: Defect Evaluation in Mild Steel Plate Using Harmonic Ratio Induced by Square Wave Excitation Field and Nonlinear Magnetization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Multi-frequency Eddy Current (EC) techniques such as Pulse Eddy Current (PEC) and rectangular EC techniques have gained widespread adoption for non-destructive tests of conductive materials. However, in the case of mild steel, the harmonics induced by a square wave excitation field can be affected by the nonlinear frequency-dependant magnetization. In this work, we study the harmonic magnetic responses induced by artificial slits on a mild steel plate upon a square wave excitation field. The result reveals that the harmonics' percentage increment is increased slightly, suggesting the effect of the mild steel's B-H characteristic. The harmonic ratio of the real and imaginary components can be used to evaluate the slit depth in the mild steel plate with improved sensitivity and immunity to the lift-off effect.

articleTitle: The Study the Characteristics the Magnetic Response of Microspirals Made of an Amorphous Magnetic Alloy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In recent years, more and more attention has been paid to the study of various amorphous materials. This is due to the fact that these materials have unique sets and combinations of properties, which is why they are widely used in microelectronics, instrumentation, and medicine. The present work is aimed to study the characteristics of the magnetic response of microspirals made of an amorphous magnetic alloy.

articleTitle: Quantum Thermal Expectation Values from an Effective Atomistic Spin Dynamics Model Using Path Integrals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In previous work, we have developed a method to approximate quantum thermal expectation values of a spin system using a path integral approach in the framework of atomistic spin dynamics. In the present work, we extend this model from a single spin coupled to a constant magnetic field, to the more general case of a system of spins coupled by isotropic Heisenberg interaction, in a potentially time-dependent magnetic field. In a first approximation, the classical atomistic model is extended by an effective field which for every interaction pair, depends only on the two interacting spins. This implies that we have a straightforward generalisation from 2 to N interacting spins. We compare our results to exactly solvable cases using exact diagonalisation for two-spins.

articleTitle: Effective Magnetic Anisotropy of NixCo1-xFe2O4 Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The study of nanoparticles has generated great interest in recent years in several areas of research. For example, multiferroic magnetoelectrical composite materials. In this way, the combination of ferroeletric materials and ferrites, in special CoFe204 and NiFe204, as magnetic is interesting since these materials are isolating oxides with high transition temperatures and high saturation magnetization. In this work, the effective magnetic anisotropy was studied as a function of the temperature for nanocristaline nickel doped cobalt ferrite samples NixCox-1Fe204., x = 0,0; 0,25; 0,50 and 1).

articleTitle: Frequency Spectrum Analysis of Magnetic Field Strength for Effective Condition Monitoring of Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for Inter-laminar Fault (ILF) analysis and condition monitoring of magnetic cores with Grain-Oriented Electrical Steels (GOES). The proposed technique relies on interpreting frequency spectrum of the magnetic field strength over one cycle of magnetisation. Experimental work was undertaken on stacks of four standard Epstein size laminations subjected to artificial ILFs of different severity. Impacts of each fault scenario on the magnetic field strength in time and frequency domains were studied. This approach can effectively increase accuracy of fault diagnosis, and improve detectability of weak fault signatures in magnetic cores.

articleTitle: Enhanced SOT Efficiency in Pt/Co Systems with a NiO Interlayer for SOT-MRAM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To enable spin-orbit torque (SOT) magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) a decrease in the switching current is needed. One method to achieve this is by improving the SOT efficiency. In this work, the interface of Pt/Co systems are modified with NiO in order to study its effect on the damping-like SOT efficiency. The NiO thickness was varied to study its impact on the Pt/Co structure and Co magnetization as well as the antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering of the interlayer. The results show Co magnetization direction dependence on the NiO thickness. Additionally, annealing was found to not only enhance the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) and SOT efficiency, but also to increase intermixing, as evidenced by X-ray diffraction (XRD), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Furthermore, after annealing, an increased thermal stability of the antiferromagnetic ordering of NiO was observed. This prompted considerations about its impact on spin current transport. Despite the observed intermixing, the exact relationship between intermixing and SOT efficiency enhancement remains unclear.

articleTitle: Magnetic Skyrmions in Synthetic Ferri- and Antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions have generated a lot of interest due to their distinct physical properties derived from their unique topology, which can be characterized by their winding number or topological charge. At the same time synthetic ferri- and antiferromagnets provide an opportunity for coupling two magnetic skyrmions with opposite topological charges resulting in novel behaviors. This presentation will discuss two possible physical representations of these systems. One is given by multilayers where the antiferromagnetic coupling comes from interlayer exchange coupling through a non-magnetic layer. Micromagnetic simulations showed how the dynamics of these systems depends sensitively on the interplay between exchange and dipolar coupling. Another system are inversion-broken multilayers of rare earth and transition metal systems. Here temperature allows to control the magnetization of the individual skyrmions, and in fact temperature can result also in a change from out-of-plane to in-plane anisotropy and a concomitant spin-reorientation transition. Repeated cycling through this transition shows that the topology of the spin textures is preserved during this continuous deformation.

articleTitle: Critical Transitions in Rare-Earths Magnets of (R,R‘)2Fe14B Type
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We demonstrate the peculiarities of the magnetization process in the ferrimagnetic intermetallic compounds of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{R,R}^{\prime})_{2}\text{Fe}_{14}\mathrm{B}$</tex>-type, their hydrides, as well as complex modified rare earth compounds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{R,R}^{\prime})_{2}\text{Fe}_{14}\mathrm{B}$</tex> (R = Nd, Gd, Dy, Ho). They have been studied theoretically and experimentally in ultrahigh magnetic fields. We observe phase transition induced by external ultrahigh magnetic fields (up to 200 T) and also describe the magnetization process analytically (in terms of critical transition fields) and numerically. In this work, the first and second critical fields of the field-induced magnetic transitions, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}2}$</tex>, were estimated. Critical field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}2}$</tex> predicting the place of transition to the forced-ferromagnetic state was estimated for the first time for various intermetallic compounds.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties Stability from 5 K to 800 K in Metastable γ-Fe85Pd15 Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</inf>Pd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf> cylindrical nanowires were electrodeposited into alumina templates of 52 nm pore diameter, crystallizing in the metastable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma-fcc$</tex> phase. After a thermal treatment up to 1000 K, some rearrangement and ordering in the structure is observed, while maintaining the same crystalline structure. The magnetic properties of the nanowire array are determined in a wide temperature range (from 5 K to 800 K), noticing a spin-glass-like behavior below 100 K superimposed to a modified Bloch law. It is remarkable that the magnetic properties of the as-deposited metastable phase display a continuity with respect to those observed in the high-temperature annealed one. Surface effects appear as a result of the nanosized crystallites and the small diameter of the NW, which lead to a spin-glass-like behavior. Strong inter- and intra-wire magneto static interactions are likely to influence the overall magnetic behavior of the system.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Brushless Exciter for Aircraft Wound Rotor Synchronous Machine Based on Magnetic Slot Wedge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Brushless excitation system makes aircraft Wound Rotor Synchronous Machine(WRSM) obtain good reliability and maintainability, but it also suffers from the disadvantages of slow dynamic response and relatively low excitation efficiency. This paper proposes a low-cost method to improve dynamic response speed and efficiency of brushless excitation system by adding magnetic slot wedges(MSW) between the stator poles of Main Exciter(ME) without changing the structure of ME. By Finite Element Analysis(FEA) simulation, MSW will increase the commutation reactance of ME, which is beneficial to improving dynamic performance. Moreover, MSW weakens the air gap flux density harmonics, leading to significant reduce in core loss of ME. A 12kVA generator prototype is manufactured and tested. The test results are consistent with FEA simulation results, which proves the accuracy of FEA model and confirms the performance improvement of ME by MSW.

articleTitle: Quaternary Neural Network Equalization for Three-Dimentional Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: One approach considered promising for advancing the development of magnetic data storage systems is three-dimensional magnetic recording. But when the recording density rises, media noise becomes a bigger problem for magnetic recording technology. Machine learning algorithms have been proven to outperform traditional numerical techniques in solving the magnetic recording signal quality issue. We compared the detection bit error rate (BER) performance of a per-layer shallow neural network equalizer and a quaternary neural network equalizer for two recording layers. For a two-layer recording density of 4 Tb/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the results show that the combined quaternary neural network equalization and detection scheme outperforms the per-layer shallow neural network equalization and one-dimensional Viterbi detection and outperforms the conventional two-dimensional generalized partial response equalizer combined with a quaternary Viterbi detector, especially for the bottom layer.

articleTitle: Polarity Influence of Poles on Positional Accuracy in Absolute Encoders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: With a particular focus on potential impact of pole transitions on localization precision, the aim of this study is placed on the study of significance of magnetic pole and magnetic flux variation in positional accuracy in absolute encoders. By constructing a magnetic model, an in-depth analysis of the interplay between magnetic poles and flux variations is conducted to evaluate practical effects of field shape variations on absolute encoders in positioning applications. The findings reveal the advantages of adjusting magnetic pole positions to enhance the positional accuracy of absolute encoding. This research not only deepens the understanding of absolute encoding but also provides valuable insights for optimizing magnetic field in precision positioning systems. The conclusions of this study hold practical value for improving existing positioning technologies and the development of future more accurate absolute encoding systems.

articleTitle: Strain-Induced Oxygen Vacancies and Ferromagnetic Order Near the Interface in CaMnO3 Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work we have studied the structural and magnetic properties of CaMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films grown over SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (100) substrates and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{BaTiO}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> underlayers. These films are subject to a biaxial tensile strain due to a lattice mismatch of 4.8% or 7.2% between the CaMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and the respective underlayer. We have performed a systematic study of the manganese valence state throughout the thickness of the films and found correlations with their magnetic properties. Specifically, we have established that there is a concentration of Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sup> ions near the interface with the substrate that leads to an enhancement of a ferromagnetic order. We conclude that oxygen vacancies generate in this interface as a mechanism to release stress. According to the amount of oxygen vacancies, other magnetic phases may dominate the ground state.

articleTitle: Spin-Orbit Torque Switching of Mn3Sn in Configuration II
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Previous research has demonstrated the spin-orbit torque (SOT) switching of Mn3Sn in configuration I. However, this configuration has yielded several unexpected outcomes, giving rise to debates concerning the fundamental physics governing the switching process. Alternatively, in configuration II, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\sigma}$</tex> is perpendicular to the kagome plane, which bears greater resemblance to the ferromagnetic (FM) system. In this study, we show successful SOT switching of Mn3Sn in configuration II, demonstrating behaviors more akin to FM, e.g., the critical switching current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(J_{\text{crit}})$</tex> and external field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(H_{\text{ext}})$</tex> are in the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{10}\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> and tens of Oersted, respectively. The switching result is also independent of the initial state. We further show that the distinctive spin structure of Mn3Sn leads to unique switching characteristics, including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{\text{crit}}$</tex> increasing linearly with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\text{ext}}$</tex> and the opposite switching polarity to FM. A switching phase diagram is further provided as a guideline for experimental demonstrations, offering a clear physical picture for the observed phenomena.

articleTitle: The Effect of Thermal Fields on Spin Hall Switching in Devices Stabilized by In-Plane Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work, we examine the effect of random thermal noise on spin-orbit-torque magnetic random-access-memory (SOT-MRAM) devices stabilized by in-plane uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy. We model these thermal fluctuations using a nondimensionalized random-field model, then quantify the effect of model parameters. We then examine the effect of the thermal background on the SOT-MRAM switching process, and observe a “smearing out” of switching stochasticity, as well as changes in switching thresholds and dependences on polarization angle and anisotropy strength. Finally, we decouple randomness arising from thermal noise and randomness associated with system nonlinearity to get a fuller picture of the transient dynamics of magnetization trajectories.

articleTitle: Thickness Dependence of Unidirectional Magnetoresistance in Co2MnGa Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: With intrinsic giant anomalous Hall and Nernst effects, Weyl ferromagnet C02MnGa stands as an ideal candidate for exploring efficient charge-to-spin conversions. In this work, by utilizing the high-quality epitaxial C02MnGa single films, we observed a sizable unidirectional magnetoresistance. Surprisingly, the isotropic crystallographic axis dependence of unidirectional magnetoresistance, together with its linear scaling to the C02MnGa thickness, neither can be explained by the conventional spin current drift-diffusion process. By employing heat equation, we analytically derived the current induced vertical temperature gradient, and unambiguously show the thickness dependence of unidirectional magnetoresistance induced by anomalous Nernst effects. Our work provides direct evidences of thermoelectric voltages in the nonlinear transport that may be extended to other material systems as well.

articleTitle: Analysis of Air-Gap Field Modulation in Asymmetric Stator Tooth Bilateral-Excitation Flux Modulation Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In view of the complexity of the flux density harmonic components of bilateral-excitation flux modulation (BFM) machines, it is not easy to analyze the role of air-gap flux density harmonics on the electromagnetic torque of BFM machines. In this digest, Taking the novel asymmetric stator tooth (AST) BFM machine as the research object, the flux modulation phenomena of the PM magneto motive-force (MMF) and armature winding MMF are analyzed in detail. Meanwhile, based on the air-gap field modulation theory and Maxwell stress tensor equation, the contribution of air-gap flux density harmonics to the electromagnetic torque of the BFM machine is obtained.

articleTitle: An Accurate Multi-Objective Optimization Strategy for Surface-Mounted Permanent-Magnet Machines Based on Nonlinear Finite-Permeability Subdomain Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This digest presents an accurate multi-objective optimization strategy for surface-mounted permanent-magnet machines (SMPMMs) by combining a nonlinear finite-permeability sub domain model (FPSM) with an optimization algorithm. First, the nonlinear FPSM is developed by introducing a nonlinear iterative algorithm to consider the magnetic saturation of soft magnetic materials and applied to the SMPMMs. Then, the average torque and the torque ripple are computed by this analytical model. Next, this nonlinear FPSM is combined with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to find the optimal designs for the studied SMPMM. Finally, the electromagnetic performances of one optimal case are validated by the finite-element model to demonstrate the effectiveness of the presented optimization strategy.

articleTitle: Magnetic Hardness of Fe3C-Based Alloys: A First-Principles Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The demand for hard magnetic materials is exponentially growing, while at the same time prices of rare earth elements can not be considered as stable. Therefore, rare-earth free permanent magnets are intensively sought after. In this work we have performed a systematic study of magnetic properties of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C with hexagonal and orthorhombic structures using full-potential local-orbital electronic structure code FPLO. Employing virtual crystal approximation (VCA), we also performed calculations for the composition range (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C. In addition, also using VCA, we determined the dependence of magnetocrystalline anisotropy on the number of electrons in the C site, considering a range of alloys from B, through C, to N (atomic numbers 5, 6 and 7). The results obtained suggest new candidates for hard magnetic materials.

articleTitle: MMF Harmonic Analysis of $\mathbf{Multi}-\boldsymbol{M}-\mathbf{Phase}$ Fractional-Slot Permanent-Magnet Machines with Partial Operating Winding Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the magnetomotive force (MMF) harmonics in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{multi}-\boldsymbol{m}-\mathbf{phase}$</tex> fractional-slot machines when one or more <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{m}- \mathbf{phase}$</tex> channels are disconnected due to faults. Employing a universal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Q}-\mathbf{set}\ \boldsymbol{m}-\mathbf{phase}$</tex> winding arrangement, this study reveals the intrinsic relationships between MMF harmonics generated by different winding sets. Through analytical derivation, results show that harmonics of the same order from different winding sets share the same amplitude but differ in phase shifts. For harmonics of different orders, certain symmetries and similarities are found in their phasors. Based on the discovered rules, all composite MMF harmonics can be classified into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{Q}/\mathbf{2}+\mathbf{1})$</tex> groups when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Q}$</tex> is even and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{Q}+\mathbf{1})/\mathbf{2}$</tex> groups when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Q}$</tex> is odd. The MMF harmonics within the same group vary synchronously as the faulty condition changes. The findings are validated by the finite-element method, which will be provided in detail in the full paper.

articleTitle: Biomimetic Magnetic Nanocarriers for Cancer Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Biomimetic nanocarriers, also named cell-membrane coated nanoparticles, are promising multifunctional materials for cancer therapy. The nanostructures are designed to improve drug delivery, thermal and immunotherapy. It combines the property of the nanoparticle core with the cell membrane, enhancing blood circulation, cancer targeting and immune stimulation. Here we report the development of distinct biomimetic magnetic nanocarriers containing Mn-ferrite nanoparticles encapsulated into the vesicles and IR-780 near-infrared dyes incorporated in the membranes. The biomedical applications of several systems are compared with a focus on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), magnetic hyperthermia and photothermal therapy (PTT) applications. Non-invasive MRI thermometry data during PTT is also reported, indicating a great potential of biomimetic magnetic nanocarriers for cancer therapy.

articleTitle: Laser-Enhanced Domain Wall Motion in GdFeCo and GdFe Nanowires for Racetrack Memory Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of the laser-annealing (LA) process on domain wall (DW) motion in GdFeCo and GdFe nanowires. Current-induced DW motion measurements revealed a substantial enhancement in velocity after a 3 ns pulse duration, with remarkable increases from 760 m/s to 1470 m/s for GdFeCo and 770 m/s to 1430 m/s for GdFe at 4.3×1011 A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 5.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. Notably, LA reduced the threshold current density for DW motion in GdFe wire to 0.8×1011 A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Additional experiments demonstrated stable DW motion, showcasing uniform DW motion for the front and rear edges of DWs without applying external magnetic fields or complex lithography processes. LA process emerges as a valuable technique by overcoming pinning effects and modifying the magnetic properties of nanowires for racetrack memory applications.

articleTitle: Dependence of the cut region on the magnetic losses of a non-grain-oriented Fe-Si steel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The final cutting process of electrical steel sheets is well-known to negatively impact their magnetic properties. Specifically, mechanical cutting introduces structural changes in the cutting region that adversely affect the steel's performance by increasing its overall magnetic loss. In this work, a non-grain oriented electrical steel was studied, and the effects of cutting clearance and the number of cuts in the material sheets (zero cut or single strip, cut in half and separated into 3 parts) on the relative permeability and different loss components (hysteresis, classical, and excess) were evaluated across a wide range of frequencies (10 to 400 Hz) and maximum polarization values (0.1 to 1.5 T). Our observations indicate that hysteresis loss is the most prominent among all the loss components, regardless of the magnetic polarization and throughout the frequency range up to 400 Hz for all cutting conditions. Above this value, the classical loss begins to dominate. However, interestingly, for samples with the greatest number of cuts (3 parts), Pe becomes greater than Pc and no inversion is observed in the entire range of polarizations studied. These findings demonstrate that each physical mechanism has a dominant role within a specific frequency range of a device's operation. Additionally, we noticed that increasing the cutting clearance from 0.01 mm to 0.03 mm resulted in a roughly 14% increase in total loss. This increase can be attributed to the impacts on the microstructure caused by the larger cutting clearance.

articleTitle: Online Permanent Magnet Demagnetization Monitoring Using Model Reference Adaptive System Considering VSI Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Permanent Magnet (PM) demagnetization could lead to performance degradation and failures in permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) making it less reliable. This paper presents an online technique for detecting PM demagnetization (PMD) in PMSMs by estimating the value of the PM flux linkage. The proposed method employs a Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) to provide a robust and adaptive estimation of the PM flux linkage. Additionally, the nonlinearity introduced by the voltage source inverter (VSI) is considered to enhance the accuracy of the estimation process. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in PMD monitoring.

articleTitle: Parametric Sensitivity Analysis and Efficiency Improvement of Electromagnetic Repulsion Mechanism Based on Orthogonal Experiment Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: As a linear actuator, the electromagnetic repulsion mechanism (ERM) has the advantages of simple structure and fast driving speed and is widely used as the circuit breaker, the bypass and the grounding switch in flexible DC transmission systems. However, the low efficiency of ERM is a significant drawback. There are many parameters that affect the dynamic characteristics and efficiency of ERM, but the importance of each parameter still needs to be further explored. This article establishes a two-dimensional ERM finite element model, and verifies the accuracy of the model through preliminary experiments. Next, the efficiency of ERM at different parameter levels were calculated by the orthogonal experimental method, and the main parameters affecting performance were determined through range analysis and variance analysis. The results show that the main parameters affecting efficiency are the coil outer diameter, capacitance value, pre-charging voltage of capacitance, and mass of moving parts. The coil outer diameter is the most important parameter affecting efficiency, and the capacitance and pre-charging voltage are both important parameters. When designing ERM, different parameters should be considered based on the required performance.

articleTitle: On the Behavior of the Magnetocaloric Quantities $\Delta S_{iso}$ and $\Delta T_{ad}$
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work, we theoretically discuss the behavior of the magnetocaloric quantities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta S_{iso}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta T_{ad}$</tex> in physical systems of local interacting magnetic moments. For this purpose, we use a Heisenberg-like model Hamiltonian with non-equivalent sites and extra terms to account for anisotropy. Our systematic analysis in terms of the model parameters shows that for isotropic ferromagnets, the curves of the magnetocaloric quantities exhibit the usual behavior with a peak around the critical temperature; a change of sign in these curves takes place in compounds with antiferromagnetic coupling, and in presence of anisotropy. Moreover, in compounds with canted magnetic moments, a profile with two peaks occurs in these curves.

articleTitle: Angle-Dependent In-Plane Magnetic Field Detection by MEMS Resonant Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
