abstract: Miniaturized piezoelectric/magnetostrictive contour-mode resonators have been demonstrated to be effective magnetometers through the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\Delta} \mathbf{E}$</tex> effect. A magnetic field sensor based AlN/FeGaB micro electromechanical system magnetic resonant is proposed. The angle dependence is characterized by its normalized Kerr intensity curve and resonance frequency shift. Magnetic domain reversal at 0° is related to stress distribution, which follows the region of IDT. The resonant frequency of the resonator is 378.48 MHz without external magnetic field. When the magnetic field is applied and the angle to easy axis is 0°, the resonant frequency shift is minimized and close to zero. As the magnetic field rotates, the maximum resonance frequency shift occurs when the magnetic field is at a 90° to the easy axis, reaching up to 90 kHz. Meanwhile, its magnetic field detection sensitivity is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{25}\ \mathbf{Hz}/\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{T}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between Split Stator Permanent Magnet Machine and Flux Reverse Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a new split stator-permanent magnet machine (SSPMM) based on the field modulation effect, which is evolved from the traditional flux reversal machine (FRM). Compared to FRM, SSPMM has higher quality torque. The topologies of SSPMM and FRM are presented. In addition, the analytical modeling for the proposed SSPMM is established. The electromagnetic performances including the airgap flux density distributions, back-electromotive force, cogging torque, and steady torque are analyzed comparatively. The FEA-predicted results show that the proposed SSPMM exhibits the merits of high steady torque, high quality torque, and low cogging torque.

articleTitle: A Blinking Detection System Based on Magnetic Sensor and Magnetic Hair Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Blinking detection is a technology that detects whether the eyes are opened and closed in a short period of time, which can realize the control of external devices or communication with the outside world. It is suitable for occasions where it is inconvenient to use hands and voice. Existing technologies such as optical detection and electroencephalography detection are difficult to be widely applied due to their inconvenience or limitations. Magnetic sensors with advantages of small size, high sensitivity, and non-contact measurement are expected to become one of the integrated modules of smart glasses. In this study, magnetic sensors are integrated into a pair of smart glasses, and flexible magnetic hairs are adhered to human eyelashes. The blinking action of human is analyzed by detecting the output changes of magnetic sensors during blinking. According to different blinking actions, functions such as barrier-free human-computer interaction and covert communication is obtained. This technology can be applied in environments such as cycling and driving, and also can be used to help disabled people control external devices or communicate with the outside world more conveniently. Therefore, this technology has great application potential in the field of wearable devices and covert communication.

articleTitle: Test Bench for Characterization of HTS Tapes at Low Magnetic Fields Based on Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The paper focuses on the description, design, construction of a prototype and examination of the test bench for characterization of superconducting tapes operating at low magnetic fields. The test bench is based on a rotating cylinder containing permanent magnets and producing homogeneous magnetic field in the center, where a superconducting tape is located. The 3D printing additive manufacturing technology is used for construction of the test bench. Designed measuring device allows for fast and easy characterization of angular dependence of the critical current density on external magnetic field of examined tape. The test bench is dedicated to examination mostly for HTS tapes (1G tapes made as silver matrix with filaments and 2G tapes made as coated conductors), which is leading superconducting tapes technology. The description presented in the paper contain description of the idea of tool supported by FEM analysis, description of manufacturing and selected results of tests. Problem of scalability of results is also discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: RTD Fluxgate Sensors based on Twisted Glass-Coated Microwires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A new type of residence time difference (RTD) fluxgate sensor is proposed. The sensor consists of a soft magnetic glass-coated microwire surrounded by a pick-up coil, and an electronic system with multiple roles: the generation of the excitation signal, the processing of the pick-up signal and the display of the measurement result. The periodical switching of the magnetic core magnetization is performed by applying a sinusoidal electrical current directly through the magnetic material. The sensor operation and its behavior for 3 representative categories of glass coated microwires - Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">77.5</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</inf> B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73.5</inf> Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13.5</inf> B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">68.18</inf> Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4.32</inf> Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12.5</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>- used as sensitive elements are described in detail.

articleTitle: Graphical Root Cause Analysis of Magnetically Induced Vibrations in Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Structural vibrations caused by magnetic forces in synchronous machines constitute a multi-domain problem involving both electromagnetic and mechanical phenomena. Recent years have seen an increasing effort in the scientific community to improve the capabilities of the calculation models used to assess this problem. On the one hand, this trend contributes to increasing the accuracy of the calculated results obtained. But on the other hand, the increased complexity of the models tends to make the identification of cause-effect relationships more difficult. In this context, this work proposes a new graphical tool for the comprehensive analysis of stator core vibrations in synchronous machines. The development of a holistic diagram for the root cause analysis of the electromagnetic and mechanical phenomena, called the vibration cause diagram (VCD), is presented and applied to two example machines of different sizes. The analysis method obtained is particularly useful during the design phase of a new machine or for the troubleshooting evaluation of existing machines.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a High-Speed Slotless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Considering Air-Gap Airflow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The air-gap airflow will affect the performance of the high-speed slotless permanent magnet synchronous motor (HSSPMSM). However, the influence of airflow is often neglected in motor design, leading to discrepancies between the designed and actual performance. This paper conducts the design and analysis of the HSSPMSM considering the influence of air-gap airflow. The coupling relationships among airflow, electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical are established. The dimensions design and performance analysis of the HSSPMSM are performed. Based on the designed dimensions, a lOkW/40krpm HSSPMSM prototype is developed. The experimental results indicate that the developed HSSPMSM matches the design requirements.

Author Keywords: high-speed slotless permanent magnet synchronous motor (HSSPMSM)

articleTitle: Magnetic Particle Spectroscopy (MPS)-Based Bioassays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic Particle Spectroscopy (MPS) originates from Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) and was initially designed to assess the suitability of magnetic nanoparticle tracers for MPI applications. Since 2006, MPS has found application in bioassays. It relies on detecting the magnetic dynamics of magnetic nanoparticles in bioassay contexts. When exposed to an external sinusoidal magnetic drive field, magnetic nanoparticles exhibit magnetization relaxation, aligning their magnetic moments with the field direction through Brownian and Néel relaxations. Their nonlinear magnetization responses induce higher harmonics of the drive field frequency, revealing information about the nanoparticles' biological environment. Throughout its development, various MPS designs have been reported. Herein, I will cover the dynamic magnetization models of magnetic nanoparticles and the surface functionalization of these nanoparticles for MPS-based bioassays. In addition, different MPS platforms will be explored, including single- and dual-driving field designs and MPS assay mechanisms such as volumetric- and surface-based bioassays. The integration of MPS with lateral flow assays and microfluidic channels will also be discussed. Various examples of MPS-based bioassays for detecting viruses (e.g., influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2) and foodborne pathogens/toxins will be showcased.

articleTitle: Melanoma Cell Internalization of Spin-Vortex Nanodisks for Cancer Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In the last decades, the study of magnetic nanoparticles for biomedical applications has increased due to their great potential to develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. In particular, disk-shaped particles has recently emerged in this field by their unique properties. In this work, we investigate the cell-particle interaction between magnetic nanodisks in a spin-vortex configuration and skin cancer cells in-vitro cultures. The quantification and the internalization intervals of nanodisks was evaluated by magnetometry measurements. Furthermore, this study confirmed the interaction of MNDs of different sizes with tumor cells in-vitro assays and observed that magnetic nanodisks could induce up to 50% cell death in melanoma cells upon external magnetic field application.

Index Terms: Application Of An External Magnetic Field

articleTitle: The Influence of SiO2 Layer on the Temperature Stability of SMC Based on Iron and Mn-Zn Ferrite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Soft magnetic composites Fe/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Mn-Zn ferrite with low energy losses and high magnetic permeability are studied. The electromagnetic properties in composites with (a) 0 wt%, (b) 1 wt %, (c) 2 wt %, (d) 3 wt %, (e) 4 wt %, and (f) 10 wt % of ferrite are investigated. Further, loss separation as a function of ferrite content and temperature was studied. An increase in temperature in working conditions affects the magnetic properties of the SMCs, which requires consideration of the temperature effect in the process of predicting magnetic properties. The content of ferrite plays a significant role in modulating the magnetic properties of Fe/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ferrite soft magnetic composites. The effect of the presence of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer can play the positive role after the thermal cycles to keep the unchanged structure.

articleTitle: Development of Open-structure Rotary Magnetic Encoder for Underwater Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents development of an open-structure rotary magnetic encoder and validation of signal integrity without additional waterproof protection, demonstrating excellent performance for potential underwater applications. The encoder utilizes two sets of Hall sensors to generate orthogonal signals and incorporates nonlinear curve fitting to adjust the measured data under various flying height, which can be used to adapt to interferences from surrounding media. Through experimental validation, it is found that the proposed system offers positioning accuracy and repeatability in water comparable to and even better than those achieved in air, while enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio and enabling accurate detection of small angular fluctuations. Furthermore, the compact size of this rotary magnetic encoder makes it suitable for installation in mechanical arm joints to compensate for minor angular deviations that may result in misalignment of the end-point's target position.

articleTitle: 2-Axis Planar Hall Magnetic Field Sensors with Sub NanoTesla Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic sensors based on the planar Hall effect (PHE) are attractive for applications where sub nano-Tesla field resolution is required. Here we present detailed noise study of PHE sensors made of two crossing masnetic ellipses that measure two axes of the magnetic field in the sensor plane with equivalent magnetic noise level better than 350 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pT} / \sqrt{}\text{Hz}$</tex> at 10 Hz in exactly the same region while keeping the size and noise level of a single axis sensor.

articleTitle: Transport Model for Magnetic Particles in Aqueous Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Despite the recent advances in the theoretical modeling and experimental development of magnetic separation systems for micrometer and sub-micrometer size particles, the separation of metal ions in aqueous is poorly understood. In this presentation, we develop a mathematical model based on the fluid dynamics of aqueous solutions (described in terms of the Navier-Stokes equations), drift-diffusion of magnetic particles, and the interaction between the magnetic particles and the fluid to understand the magnetic separation process. Then, we use this model to study the limitation of metal ion separation in high gradient magnetic separation systems. Simulation results and predictions will be provided in the full presentation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties Dependence on Geometrical Parameters of Electroless-Plated Ni-Based Rhombohedral Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Recent research that has brought huge scientific attention on ferromagnetic nanotubes as building blocks for nanoarchitectures and magnetic devices for technological applications are usually focused on cylindrical shape nanotubes, while only a few have been addressed with alternative three-dimensional geometries. Here, we present rhombohedral magnetic nanotubes obtained by a novel synthesis method based on electroless-plating deposition into the pores of ion-track etched muscovite mica templates, providing a precise control over nanotubes geometry. Both, pure nanocrystalline Ni and amorphous Ni-B nanotubes were fabricated and their magneto-structural properties were characterized as function of their geometrical parameters. Their magnetic properties dependence on increased deposition time were discussed which, in combination to micromagnetic simulations, allow to understand their intriguing magnetic behavior.

articleTitle: Air-Cored Linear Motor: Design and Operating Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Long-stator linear synchronous motors have been proven to operate efficiently at high speeds, making them suitable for ground-based high-speed transportation technologies such as Maglev trains or Hyperloop. The need for laminated steel along the track makes this type of motor cost-prohibitive which argues in favor of an ironless design. Air-cored synchronous motors are more difficult to control, especially at low speeds at the beginning of acceleration phases. Here, we report the design and low-speed performance of a long-stator air-cored linear synchronous motor. This study is based on a 4.8 m long test track with a rail-bound vehicle. Successfull motor operation with a conventional variable frequency drive system demonstrates sufficient magnetic flux linkage between an optimized multi-turn stator and a permanent magnet excitation system. We infer information from measurements for different driving profiles and air gaps from 5 mm to 25 mm. Depending on whether position and speed feedback are integrated, we observe a major difference in vibrations, leading to different levels of potential passenger comfort.

articleTitle: Evidence of Spin-Polarized Current in Fe-Rich NbFe2 Compound
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The effects of slight changes in the ideal stoichiometry on the structural, magnetic properties, and electrical transport of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Nb}_1-x\text{Fe}_{2+x}(x>0)$</tex> compounds have been investigated. Excess Fe in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Nb}_1-x\text{Fe}_{2+x}$</tex> leads to an anisotropic contraction of the unit cell: the initial growth along the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> and b-axis achieves a maximum for sample A2 while c-axis increase continously. The magnetotransport results in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{NbFe}_{2}$</tex> compound with an excess of Fe highlight the presence of a spin-polarized current in these compounds. The correlation between the electrical transport and X-ray diffraction results suggests changes in the Fermi surface induced by Fe excess.

articleTitle: Electrical Manipulation of Noncollinear Antiferromagnetic State via Orbital Hall Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Orbital Hall effect can induce spin-orbit torque in ferromagnetic heterostructures with similar symmetry as spin Hall effect. Due to its weak dependence on spin-orbit coupling, even light metals like Cr could exhibit robust orbital Hall conductivity and generate comparable spin-orbit torque as heavy metals. In view of this, we study the electrical control of antiferromagnetic state in Mn3Sn/Cr and ferromagnetic state in CoFeB/Cr. We find that Cr can induce efficient switching in both Mn3Sn and CoFeB despite its negligible spin Hall angle. However, from terahertz emission and magnetoresistance measurements, the inverse process - spin-to-charge conversion in Cr/CoFeB is much less efficient than the heavy metal-based structures. These results suggest that the observed switching in Mn3Sn/Cr and CoFeB/Cr is mainly contributed by orbital Hall effect rather than spin Hall effect.

articleTitle: Magneto-Structural Properties of Co2FeIn Heusler Nanowires for Spintronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Co}_{2}\text{FeIn}$</tex> Heusler alloy nanowires were synthesized through a pulsed electrodeposition process in the pores of alumina membranes. SEM and TEM analysis of nanowires display a diameter of around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$165\pm 11$</tex> nm, 12 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> in length and averaged composition of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">49</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</inf>In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</inf>. SAED analysis and X-ray diffraction patterns indicate the presence of a cubic L21 crystalline phase. VSM magnetic hysteresis loops of the as-synthesized nanowires array evidenced an easy magnetization axis lying along the nanowires length and showing a coercivity of around 70 Oe, which is of the same order than the switching field values measured in single isolated nanowires by NanoMOKE. FORC analysis revealed also high magnetostatic interaction among the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Co}_{2}\text{FeIn}$</tex> nanowires in the array, but with low coercive field distribution.

articleTitle: Efficient Grain Boundary Diffusion Technology in Sintered Nd-Fe-B Magnets: Nano-TbF3 Powders Electrophoretic Suspension Preparation via Sand-Milling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work proposed a sand-milling method to prepare nano diffusion sources and optimized the process of electrophoretic deposition and sintered Nd-Fe-B grain boundary diffusion. The optimal sand-milling process parameters were explored, the quality of electrophoretic coating was improved and high-performance magnets were obtained. By optimizing the entire process, the utilization of heavy rare earth resources has been achieved.

articleTitle: Magnetic Behavior of Nanoporous FeCo, Fully and Partially Dealloyed by Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Liquid Metal Dealloying (LMD) is recommended to enhance the near-surface ferromagnetic properties of Iron-Cobalt alloys. With a lower surface electrical conductivity, treated specimens are expected to accommodate the frequency effect better and exhibit a lower level of magnetic loss. This work focuses on the magnetic behavior of LMD-treated samples. The magnetic hysteresis cycles of a virgin, a fully, and a partially dealloyed specimens are plotted at different levels of frequencies of the magnetic excitation. Then, a model to simulate those cycles is described. The simulation parameters of the fully and virgin specimens can be leveraged to predict the behavior of the partially dealloyed specimen and estimate the thickness of the treated area accurately and non-destructively.

articleTitle: A Novel Electromagnetic Force Calculation Method for Homopolar Hybrid Magnetic Bearing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Electromagnetic force of homopolar hybrid magnetic bearings (HOHMB) is generally calculated by 3-D finite element method (FEM). However, 3-D FEM is time-consuming due to the large computational volume. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel electromagnetic force calculation method to reduce the computing time. The proposed method transforms 3-D finite element calculation to 2-D finite element calculation by establishing the 2-D equivalent model of the HOHMB. The leakage and fringing flux compensation are considered in the 2-D equivalent model. The experiments of the electromagnetic force measurement are conducted. The electromagnetic force calculated by the proposed method agrees with the experiment results. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Self-Induced Magnetic Anisotropy in 3D Printed Ferromagnetic Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: 3D printing of microwave absorbers gave rise to new shape optimization possibilities. However, new printable materials dedicated to this application have to be developed. In this study, an iron flake polymer composites was elaborated and characterized. Scanning Electron Microscopy observations demonstrated that iron flakes particles are naturally aligned along the extrusion flow direction without applied magnetic field during the 3D printing process. Magnetic anisotropy was demonstrated with both Vibrational Sample Magnetometer and microwave measurements. Indeed, at 5.4 GHz, a ratio of 1.71 between parallel and perpendicular susceptibility was demonstrated. These measurements demonstrated a self-induced magnetic anisotropy that can be used to control the angular robustness of free-space microwave absorbers.

articleTitle: Reluctance Network Model of V-Type IPMSM for Accurate and Practical Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a reluctance network analysis (RNA) model of a V-type interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) for accurate and practical design. As a result of the examination, it was verified that the proposed RNA model could accurately calculate the basic characteristics of the V-type IPMSM by comparing the calculation results with a finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: An aLternative Heat Treatment Recovery of the Magnetic Properties of a Non-Grain Oriented Fe-Si Steel After Cutting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work investigates the effects of an alternative heat treatment on magnetic losses and their components - hysteresis loss, excess loss and classic loss - in non-grain oriented (NGO) steel. The importance of this study lies in the search for strategies to optimize the magnetic performance of materials used in industrial applications. We carried out experiments using heat treatment at 700 ° C, 800 ° C and 900 ° C on NGO steel and evaluated its implications on magnetic losses. The results reveal that heat treatment at 700 ° C was highly effective and significantly influenced the different components of magnetic losses. We observed that excess and hysteric losses were the most impacted by heat treatment, demonstrating a particular sensitivity of these components to specific thermal conditions. In-depth analysis of these changes provides valuable insights for optimizing the magnetic behavior of NGO steel in practical applications. This study contributes to the understanding of the crucial role of heat treatment in modifying the magnetic properties in materials such as NGO steel and have important practical implications for the selection and development of magnetic materials in sectors that demand improved energy efficiency and magnetic performance.

articleTitle: MnGaGe Nanomagnets Epitaxially Grown on GaAs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Room temperature ferromagnetism and perpendicular magnetization are phenomena of great interest for spintronics applications. The intermetallic compound MnGaGe is a promising candidate because several of its magnetic properties meet desirable requirements for applications. MnGaGe nanoislands with perpendicular magnetization were grown by molecular beam epitaxy on commercial (001)oriented GaAs substrates. The formation of ferromagnet-semiconductor heterojunctions was analyzed by x-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, microscopies of atomic force, magnetic force and Kelvin probe.

articleTitle: Leveraging Spintronic Nonlinear Random Projections for Handwritten Digit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Nonlinear random projections are a powerful tool to efficiently classify real-life data while requiring much less computational resources than conventional artificial neural networks. We showcase the implementation of an echo-state network (ESN) based on a single spin-torque vortex oscillator (STVO) delayed in time. This network achieves accuracy of over 98% on the MNIST handwritten digit recognition task. Ultrafast data-driven simulations based on the Thiele equation approach are used to show that the performance of our STVO-based network is equivalent to that of conventional software implementations. We demonstrate how hardware neural networks based on STVOs can be studied for specific tasks through data-driven simulation, hence speeding up the development of such hardware intelligent systems.

articleTitle: Ferris-Wheel Magneto-Optic Kerr Effect and Optical Hall Effect Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: It is well known that the anomalous Hall effect displayed in ferromagnets is much stronger than the ordinary Hall effect. Similarly, the magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) is orders of magnitude stronger than the optical Hall effect taking place in normal metals. Here, we present a MOKE technique that we term the “Ferris” MOKE which is based on large-amplitude modulation of the externally applied magnetic field such that the sensitivity is enhanced by more than an order of magnitude. Consequently, the Ferris MOKE is found suitable for measurement of the optical Hall effect at visible light wavelengths where the effective electrical displacement is short. We derive a model that builds on the Lorentz-Drude formalism that accounts for the evanescent waves in the metal. By complementing the measurements with carrier density data extracted by DC Hall measurements, we show that the “Ferris MOKE” measurement can reproduce previously reported effective masses that is indicative of the effective band curvature. Since the optical cycle is much shorter than the Drude mean free path, the technique may prove useful for probing intrinsic properties of the band structure and topological states of matter in non-magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Dual Band Analysis of a Novel Rectenna for Wireless Power Transmission and Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This work presents a study of the wireless power transmission using a high-efficiency ISM band rectenna in a wide frequency band. A rectenna is a component of a Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) system used to convert radiofrequency energy into DC power. The study's rectenna includes a receiving antenna and a rectifying circuit, with simulations focusing on a circular antenna with a three-section feeding line. The rectifying circuit, featuring a L-shaped stub, aims for impedance matching. Simulations show promising results including a reflection coefficient below -10 dB, conversion efficiency greater than 50% and an output voltage of approximately 1.6 V. The substrates used for constructing the rectenna were FR4 and Rogers 5880, which were separately analyzed.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Bearingless Consequent-Pole Motor Using Combined Winding with Functions of Three-Phase Radial Suspension and Single-Phase Motor Driven by Zero-Sequence Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Conventional two-degree-of freedom (DOF) actively controlled bearingless motor has two kinds of three-phase radial suspension and three-phase motor windings and needs 2 three-phase inverters for the radial suspension and motor. To simplify the system, this paper proposes a two-DOF actively controlled bearingless consequent-pole permanent magnet (CPM) motor with combined winding, which integrates three-phase radial suspension and single-phase motor functions. The single-phase motor is driven by a zero-sequence current, which is superimposed onto three-phase suspension current in three-phase four-wire system. Therefore, the proposed system is operated with only one three-phase inverter for the radial suspension and motor. The FEA results indicate that the proposed bearingless CPM motor has superior suspension performance, compared to the bearingless surface permanent magnet (SPM).

articleTitle: Local magnetization processes at constricted regions in amorphous Fe80B20 stripes with nanometric thicknesses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Results are presented on the dependence of the coercivity and reduced remanence on the dimensions of constrictions engraved by UV lithography in long aspect ratio stripes having a few tens of microns widths and 20 nm thicknesses. Our data cover the hysteretic behavior both away and close to the constrictions and obtained by applying dc fields along the long stripe axis and perpendicularly to it. We conclude that it is possible obtain, at narrow constrictions involving large stripe width reductions and by applying transverse fields, local reduced remanences close to 1.0 associated to coercivities above 20 Oe, which is compatible with the stabilization, in the coercivity field range, of the local magnetization at the constriction in a direction close to perpendicular to the stripe long axis

articleTitle: Anisotropy dependent spin orbit torque switching in crystalline ferromagnetic semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We investigated spin-orbit-torque (SOT) magnetization switching phenomena in a single layer of crystalline dilute ferromagnetic semiconductor (DFMS) system by performing the micromagnetic simulation using MuMax<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The investigation was aimed to elucidate the influence of magnetic anisotropy on the SOT switching mechanism of the DFMS film. We discovered that the field-like torque (FLT) component of SOT dominates the field-free deterministic magnetization switching in an in-plane magnetized DFMS sample with biaxial anisotropy. Conversely, the damping-like torque (DLT) component plays a crucial role in the field-free deterministic magnetization switching in the DFMS film with uniaxial anisotropy. These findings deepen our understanding of the SOT switching mechanism for diverse anisotropic systems, paving the way for the development of SOT-based spintronics devices.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of Series Impedance for Deeply Buried Coaxial Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A formulation for the series impedance matrix is obtained for a deeply buried coaxial cable in terms of the Bessel functions from the electrodynamics scalar potential formula. The analytical formulations can model the proximity effect and skin effect in the series impedance calculations and easily solve problems where the Finite Element Analysis may fail, as in high-frequency eddy current problems, extensive domains, and thin semiconductor regions.

articleTitle: Availing Highly-saturable Advanced Soft Magnetic Materials for Rotating Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Electrical rotating machines are widely used for the large industrial applications for more than a century. Over last three decades power density, torque density and efficiency have been the optimizing design criteria for the EV applications and robotics. The current trend of electrical actuations on roads, over water, and in the air as UAVs are increasing for their continuous motions or servomechanism and have some specific needs for each of these applications. Most of these applications utilizes permanent magnet motors either PMSM or PM BLDCs. The advancements in permanent magnet materials both as rare earth (NdFeB and SmCo with and without Dysprosium) and ferrites are already avail by the designers to enhance their designs. This paper will discuss the limitations of the past motor grade steels, and how the advancement in soft magnetic material will support the design needs to meet the specification and performance requirements for today's rotating machine applications.

articleTitle: Development of Bonded $\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\prime \prime}-\mathbf{Fe}_{\mathbf{16}} \mathbf{N}_\mathbf{2}$ Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Because of their great technological impacts, permanent magnets play a crucial role in various aspects of modern life [1]–[2]. The problems generated by the availability and the resulting pollution to obtain the rare earths used in the preparation of the current permanent magnets stimulated intense research for the development of alternative materials. The iron nitride materials, especially <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}\text{-Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex>, are considered one of the most promising candidates for future rare earth free semi-hard magnetic materials [3] since they possess a giant saturation magnetization of ~2.9 T (~305 emu/g) [4]–[5] and the constituent materials Fe and N are abundant and environmentally friendly [6]. So far, many efforts have been made both on the fundamental [7]–[8] and experimental aspects of the preparation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}-\text{Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> material in various forms such as thin layers, strips, nanopowders [9]–[12]. However, the preparation of permanent magnets based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}\text{-Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> is still challenging. Current production of dense permanent magnets consists of powder production, pressing and magnetic field alignment, sintering, and post-processing. But the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}\text{-Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> powders are considered difficult to compact by sintering techniques that are commonly used for bulk magnets because the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}\text{-phase}$</tex> decomposes at temperatures higher than 200°C. In addition, it was reported that ultra-high pressure compaction above 5 GPa led to partial decomposition of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}$</tex> phase transition into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma^{\prime}\text{-Fe}_{4}\mathrm{N}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma^{\prime\prime}-\text{FeN}$</tex> phases [13]. Consequently, due to the critical thermo-mechanical instability of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}- \text{Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> phase, here we propose the preparation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime\prime}\text{-Fe}_{16}\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> magnets employing a bonding method at the expense of magnetic performance due the mixing with non-magnetic polymer.

articleTitle: Estimation of Core Loss in Fe-Ni Powder Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Ring-shaped Fe-Ni powder cores were prepared by cold pressing process using commercial powder with 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> size insulated with phenol resin. The investigation focused on understanding the impact of compaction pressure on the magnetic properties of the powder core, encompassing variations in density, saturation magnetization, real part of permeability, and core loss. Notably, core loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\text{cv}}$</tex> values consistently demonstrated a decrease for powder cores compacted at high pressures, particularly in the frequency range above 100 kHz. At a frequency of 200 kHz and a magnetic flux density of 50 mT, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\text{cv}}$</tex> value decreased from 1635 to 1500 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with an increase in compaction pressure increased from 980 to 1960 MPa. Consequently, these findings suggest that the core loss can be reduced by optimizing the compaction process and heat treatment.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Hydrogen-Induced Degradation of Steel Through Multispectral Analysis of Magnetic Barkhausen Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents the evaluation of hydrogen degradation in AISI 4340 steel based on the multispectral analysis of magnetic Barkhausen noise. Previous studies using acoustic and magnetic response of the Barkhausen effect have shown a large change in the course of the phenomenon as a result of the progression of hydrogen destruction of steel, and the applied time-frequency analysis has been limited to aggregated data in a few frequency bands. Thus, due to the complex nature of changes in the Barkhausen noise course, this study uses the analysis of the multi-domain representation of the measured signals, enabling a broad characterization of various aspect of obtained signal distributions by multiple feature assessment.

articleTitle: Magnetic Domain Walls in Rapidly Solidified Magnetostrictive and Non-Magnetostrictive Submicron Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Results on the magnetic domain walls in rapidly solidified magnetostrictive and non-magnetostrictive amorphous submicron wires are reported. Employing Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, we have observed the domain walls in such ultra-thin amorphous wires. All the investigated samples display vortex domain walls, irrespective of wire composition or diameter. In non-magnetostrictive wires, the domain walls maintain their structure and symmetry under various magnetic field conditions. In contrast, magnetostrictive wires show an elongation of their domain walls upon magnetic field application. The results are important for future developments in miniaturized magnetic devices.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Normal Magnetic Flux in Composite Materials Transformer Core
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: By altering the construction of the transformer core, the operational characteristics can be improved. A composite materials transformer core, consisting of amorphous alloys and silicon steel, has been developed to capitalize on the magnetic properties of both materials. Previous research on this composite materials has mainly focused on conceptualization and application, with limited understanding of the underlying mechanisms governing its magnetization characteristics. This paper presents a numerical analysis approach to investigate the magnetization behavior of the composite materials structure. The distribution of normal magnetic flux density within this structure under various saturation conditions is demonstrated, and the quantitative analysis of the variation in normal magnetic flux at different material interfaces due to differing permeabilities is conducted. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for the experimental design of magnetization characteristics and the design of magnetic cores in composite materials structures.

articleTitle: Bright Envelope Solitons in a Double Negative Medium Based on Nonlinear Ferromagnetic Metamaterial Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a normally magnetized nonlinear ferromagnetic metamaterial (FM MM) layer possessing simultaneously negative effective permittivity and magnetic permeability in some microwave frequency range, where a backward electromagnetic wave (BEMW) exists. The FM MM is a nonconductive FM host containing a square two-dimensional array of thin conductive wires cladded with a nonmagnetic dielectric layer. The nonlinearity of the FM MM is due to the dependence of magnetization on the amplitude of the high-frequency magnetic field. It is shown, that bright envelope solitons can be formed on the BEMW in relatively thick FM MM layers and at relatively small wave numbers.

articleTitle: Interlaminar faults in a GOFeSi laminated magnetic core: measurements and simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Grain-oriented silicon steel (GOFeSi) laminations are massively used as magnetic cores in electrical energy converters (motors and transformers). Edge burrs can appear during the manufacturing process and be at the origin of interlaminar faults (ILFs). In a recent paper, we described an efficient simulation method for GOFeSi laminations. This technique simultaneously solves the magnetic diffusion equation and a fractional differential equation for the material law. It produces excellent results across a large bandwidth of frequencies and is limited to only two parameters for the dynamic contribution. This study extends this method to predict the influence of interlaminar faults. We successfully reproduce experimental data for aligned ILFs and predict their impact in different working conditions. This work provides potential improvements in transformer reliability and defect detection.

articleTitle: Hybrid Three-Layer Sub-Harmonic Synchronous Machine using Consequent Pole Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A novel three-layer sub-harmonic synchronous machine is proposed, equipped with consequent permanent magnets and windings for superior torque generation and better overall performance. The consequent pole PM rotor design reduces the PM quantity by half versus conventional configurations without compromising performance. Finite element analysis of an 8-pole, 48-slot machine verifies a 6% increase in torque generation and 4 % lower torque ripple compared to a fully PM -assisted design. The proposed machine also outperforms alternatives on metrics, including torque density and efficiency. These favorable characteristics demonstrate the promise of the topology as a cost-effective, high-performing electric propulsion candidate. This work contributes to an innovative machine advancing progress toward affordable PM -assisted synchronous motors.

articleTitle: Magnetization dynamics in La0.7Sr0.3Mno3/LaTio3 (δ)/SrTio3 (00l) thin films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We have used ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) technique to study the magnetization dynamics and interfacial inhomogeneity in La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (15nm)/LaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (b)/SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(001) heterostructures. The variation of linewidth ΔH with polar angle (OH) is a very sensitive tool for quantitative analysis of magnetic inhomogeneity at the interface. We have considered the intrinsic Gilbert damping and extrinsic factors to quantify the magnetic inhomogeneity at the interface. The thickness variation of the interfacial LTO layer show changes in both intrinsic and extrinsic factors. The 2D electron gas (2DEG) at the LTO/STO interface and associated Rashba spin-orbit interaction is responsible for the change in magnetization dynamics of LSMO (l5nm) films.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Thermal Modelling of Hollow Conductors for Improved Cooling and Force Density of Coreless Linear Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The feasibility of using direct liquid cooled hollow conductors in coreless linear motors is evaluated in this paper. Hollow conductors with direct water cooling can significantly improve the heat dissipation inside electrical machines. Two different concepts for winding coils from hollow conductors are considered. A moving coil and moving magnet topology are analysed. The magnetic models, based on harmonic modelling or a surface charge model, and a 3D thermal equivalent circuit (TEC) model are used to model the coils. The model is validated via a FEM analysis. A coupled electromagnetic-thermal analysis is implemented. Further, the proposed motor with hollow conductors is compared to a state-of-the-art direct liquid cooled linear motor. The proposed topology with hollow conductors shows an improvement of the cooling performance, compared to the state-of-the-art motor. However, a much higher current is required to achieve a similar force profile.

articleTitle: Study on Using Magnetodielectric Ferrite for Impedance Matching to Improve the Transmission-Range of Implantable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Implantable electronic devices for wireless biotelemetry inevitably operate in the harsh electromagnetic environment within organisms. This study aims to explore the application of magnetodielectric ferrite for impedance matching at the skin–air interface to enhance the transmission range of implantable antennas. We delve into this field by establishing a connection between the electromagnetic parameters of the impedance matching layer and the human body. By analyzing data from human tissues, we successfully identified the parameter range of the ferrite impedance matching layer. Applying a Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>W-type ferrite to the body phantom and validating through simulation, it has been confirmed that loading this ferrite as an impedance matching layer (IML) can result in a 2 dB gain enhancement. The findings substantiate that the utilization of ferrite as a matching layer can effectively enhance the transmission range of implantable antennas. This discovery holds great significance for improving the performance of implantable electronic devices within the organism.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Single-Phase Inverter-Fed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Ladder-Connected Winding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a new permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with ladder-connected winding. The proposed PMSM is able to drive only by a single-phase H-bridge inverter thanks to an intrinsic wave propagation effect of the LC ladder circuit configuration. A mathematical modeling of the circuit is presented. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed PMSM, phase current and torque characteristics are calculated numerically from the derived circuit equations.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Magnetic Hardening of Nd-Fe-B Magnets after Grain Boundary Diffusion: A Layer by Layer Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study investigates the Grain Boundary Diffusion (GBD) of Dy-Cu in Nd-Fe-B magnets, focusing on understanding the GBD mechanism and its implications on magnetic properties. GBD operates by modifying the microstructure at the grain boundary surface to optimize magnetic performance, significantly enhancing the coercivity of these magnets. The experimental procedure involved the application of GBD of Dy-Cu elements to Nd-Fe-B magnets, and the subsequent characterization of these GBD magnets. The analysis focused on studying the shell formation via electron microscopy, and the diffusion depth via magnetometry. The diffusion depth was characterized by measuring the intrinsic coercivity (HcJ) at different depths using a destructive layer-by-layer analysis method. Preliminary results show notable improvements in the magnetic properties of magnets treated with GBD, with an increase in the magnet's HcJ by approximately 47%, without significant change in remanence. Particularly noteworthy is the identification of the almost linear dependence of HcJ on diffusion depth, providing valuable insights for future analyzes at the microstructural level of the alteration via GBD of ferromagnetic grains.

articleTitle: Progress in Nanofabrication of Superconducting Devices and Diverse Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Superconducting circuits have emerged as a highly promising platform for quantum computing, among other divices based on Josephson junctions. The fabrication and testing of these devices requires especiallized nanofabrication facilities and milikelvin range testing equipment. In the search for the fabrication of these devices we have ran into limitations which forced us into creative solutions for the fabrications of these superconducting circuits and Josephson Junctions. Furthermore the development of these technologies allows for application in a wide range of research fields such as quantum computing, magnonics, micro-electromechanical systems and more.

articleTitle: All-Optical Control and Ultrafast Spin Dynamics in Van Der Waals Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Despite tremendous interest in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets, little is known about how laser pulses can affect their magnetic properties. Here, we demonstrate laser-induced manipulation of magnetic domains within 2D ferromagnets CrI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. We show that depending on the initial state of remanent magnetization, pumping with laser pulses can lead to randomly oriented sub-domains, generate different type of topological spin textures, and even induce a reversible transformation between them. Furthermore, by fabricating CrI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> vdW heterostructures, we can achieve full all-optical switching (AOS). Finally, by using time-resolved beam-scanning magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy, we demonstrate how to modify the magnetization dynamics via thickness-dependent heat dissipation into the adjacent substrate.

articleTitle: Magnetic Hysteresis Models for 3D Printed Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work are presented magnetic hysteresis models for 3D printed composite materials. Fused Deposition Modeling 3D printing technology have been used. Composite material consists of polymer matrix with micro sized iron powder dispersed inside it. Composite samples are produced with variation of iron filled content and different micro fill patterns. The magnetization of these samples has been tested and single frequency hysteresis loops have been acquired. Measured magnetic hysteresis's data are used for parameter fitting for Jiles-Atherton and Stoner-Wohlfarth magnetic hysteresis models. The obtained results are useful for further modeling applications, implementation of 3D printed magnetic polymer composites and its predictive properties control.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Magnon-Based Radio Frequency Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A spin wave (SW) filter, consisting of a magnonic waveguide, a spacing layer, and an reconfigurable soft magnetic structure, is introduced. Micromagnetic simulations, along with preliminary experimental results, demonstrate the potential for a reconfigurable filtering action mediated by the dipolar coupling between the waveguide and the reconfigureble layer. This proof of concept lays the groundwork for a future device capable of serving as both a dedicated filter in radiofrequency signal processing and a tunable unit in computing applications.

articleTitle: Influence of Stator Core Manufacturing Displacement on the Electromagnetic Performance of Modular Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of various manufacturing tolerances of modular stator core, including radial, circumferential and axial displacements, on the electromagnetic performance of modular permanent magnet machine. The no-load back electromotive force, cogging torque and unbalanced magnetic force are calculated for a single module under the same displacement amplitude fault. The results reveal the influence of typical displacements on electromagnetic performance, which can provide a reference for motor design and analysis.

articleTitle: Decision-Feedback Single-Layer Read Reconstruction and Separation for Three-dimensional Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Three-dimensional magnetic recording (3DMR) based on energy-assisted recording techniques by either heat or microwave is a leading storage solution. Separation and detection are impeded by inter-symbol interference, inter-track interference, and inter-layer interference, especially when using traditional tunneling magnetoresistive (TMR) readers. To support a multi-layer magnetic recording system at an recording areal density of 4 Tbits/inch<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on a dual-layer recording medium, we propose a neural network estimator to reconstruct the top-layer read response signal from the decision feedback of a Viterbi detector. Then we separate the bottom-layer signal by subtracting the reconstructed top-layer signal from the mixed readback signal. For the critical bound of channel bit error rate (BER), our method gains over 7 dB than a multiple-output detecting system.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Tubular Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motors Considering Machining and Assembly Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimization design method for the tubular permanent magnet synchronous linear motor (TPMSLM) using Halbach array. For this TPMSLM, a subdomain model considering the longitudinal end effect is established by setting virtual permanent magnet (PM) regions at both ends of the Halbach array. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through a comparison with the finite element method (FEM). Subsequently, a surrogate model is developed using the proposed subdomain model, and an uncertain optimization model considering machining and assembly errors is developed based on the interval order and the possibility theory. Compared to its initial design, the average thrust of the optimized motor is increased by 12.7% and its PM material usage is reduced by 3.7%, significantly improving theoverall performance of the TPMSLM.

articleTitle: Tailoring the exchange bias by AFM interface patterned control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The interface exchange bias <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(H_{E})$</tex> in antiferromagnetic (AFM) / ferromagnetic (FM) layer systems is influenced by zero field cooling from specific ferromagnetic magnetization states, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, above the antiferromagnetic Neel temperature, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{N}$</tex> • The hypothesis posits that the AFM interface coupling depends on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_{0}$</tex>, and the treatment can induce a specific AFM interface coupling patterned zero field FM magnetization profile at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T=T_{N}$</tex> dependent. We investigated a system with two opposite interface coupling fractions at the F/AF interface, a function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>. Our results show a good correlation with experiment [1], providing ways to predict the magnetic domain geometry recorded during this thermal/field treatment and potentially tuning FM magnetization curves.

articleTitle: Energy of a Fully Spin-Polarized Two-Dimensional Electron Gas Separated from its Jellium Neutralizing Background
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We study a two-dimensional electron gas in which the electrons are separated from the corresponding jellium neturalizing background. For simplicity, we assume that the electrons are fully spin-polarized meaning that they are treated as spinless particles. The current setup implies that the overall energy of the system will depend on both density and separation distance of the electrons from the neutralizing background. The subtle interplay of these two parameters determines the stability of the system. Analytical results for the energy are obtained in the thermodynamic limit by using the Hartree–Fock approach. It is found that, within the framework of this approximation, the effect of separation manifests as an effective increase of kinetic energy.

articleTitle: Above Room Temperature Ferromagnetism in All-Epitaxial Fe5-xGeTe2/Graphene and Fe5-xGeTe2/WSe2 Van Der Waals Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic materials are promising building blocks for the realization of novel and ultra-compact devices for spintronics. Moreover, combining them with other 2D crystals to create van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is a very attractive route to realize hybrid 2D systems exhibiting integrated functionalities. In this contribution, we report recent achievements on scalable epitaxial growth of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-x</inf>GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on single crystalline graphene (on SiC) and WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (on Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) templates via molecular beam epitaxy (MBE). Structural studies show that epitaxial Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-x</inf>GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films with good crystalline quality and sharp vdW interfaces to graphene and WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> could be realized. Importantly, magneto-transport measurements and SQUID magnetometry reveal ferromagnetic order persisting above 350 K with a predominant out-of-plane anisotropy (for the case of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-x</inf>GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/graphene). These results represent an important advance beyond non-scalable flake exfoliation from bulk crystals, thus marking a crucial step towards the implementation of above room temperature ferromagnetic 2D materials in practical applications.

articleTitle: A Control Strategy Minimizing PM Loss of Phase-Shifted Dual-Winding PMSM for Aviation Electric Propulsion Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: High-efficiency constitutes a primary objective in the design and operation of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) in electric propulsion aircraft. The pursuit of high-power-density in PMSM design results in substantial harmonic components within the phase current when the machine is fed by voltage-source inverters, which contribute to additional permanent magnets (PM) loss. In this paper, a control strategy of phase-shifted dual-winding PMSM is proposed, which can effectively suppress PM loss. Analysis is carried out on the principles and outcomes of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Piezomagnetism in Cr Dopped Fe65Co35 Alloy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Fe-Co alloys have the highest magnetizations among all existing magnetic materials, 2.45 T for the alloy with 35% Co (% by mass). Regarding magnetostriction, the highest magnetostrictions occurs in Co rich Fe-Co alloys. The piezomagnetic behavior of Fe-Co alloys rich in Fe, that is, the variation of the material's magnetic induction as a function of applied force, was not found in the literature. In the present work, the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">65</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">35</inf> alloy (% by mass) was dopped with 0.5% Cr (% by mass) to inhibit the formation of the bcc cubic ordered phase with B2 structure. The purpose is to retain only the disordered bcc phase with A2 structure, as the ordered phase turn out the material brittle. The saturation magnetostriction was determined <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3/2}\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{s}}=\mathbf{61}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{6}}$</tex> for the dopped alloy and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3/2}\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{s}}=\mathbf{26}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{6}}$</tex> for the undoped. The enhancement of the magnetostriction imply in an improvement on the magneto mechanical coupling. The magnetic induction as a function of the applied magnetic field was determined for the doped alloy for tensile and compressive stresses <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\sigma})$</tex> in the range of - <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\mathbf{100}\ \mathbf{MPa} \leq\boldsymbol{\sigma}\leq \mathbf{100}\ \mathbf{MPa}$</tex> and magnetic fields (H) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0} < \mathbf{H}\leq \mathbf{5.5}\ \mathbf{kA}/\mathbf{m}$</tex>. From B vs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\sigma}$</tex> curves a sensitivity as high as 6 kA m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>/MPa was achieved for an applied field of only 3 kA/m.

articleTitle: Parallel Line Type Permeameter for Thick Magnetic Material to Reduce the Error of Demagnetizing Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We have developed a new high-frequency magnetic permeability evaluation method to suppress measurement errors due to demagnetizing fields of thick magnetic materials using parallel wires. The characteristic impedance of the parallel wires was designed to be around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{50}\ \mathbf{\Omega}$</tex>. The magnetic field inside the sample has almost in-plane components, and even in thick samples, the perpendicular component of the magnetic field was canceled, and measurement errors due to demagnetizing fields were suppressed. The thick noise suppression sheet (Tokin, EFS-02, 0.5 mm in thickness) was evaluated, and the results almost corresponded to that of the standard method (Nicolson-Ross-Wier method). The ferromagnetic resonance frequency was around 3.5 GHz, almost corresponding to the intrinsic value. There was a clear resonance around 12 GHz, caused by the impedance mismatch or the cutoff frequency of the Transverse ElectroMagnetic (TEM) mode.

articleTitle: Design and Quantitative Analysis of Asymmetric Flux Reversal Permanent Magnet Linear Machine with Reduced Leakage Flux
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes an asymmetric flux reversal permanent magnet linear machine (AFR-PMLM) with reduced leakage flux. By utilizing asymmetric permanent magnet excitation, the AFR-PMLM can effectively generate and fully exploit the second-order harmonic magnetomotive force (MMF), resulting in a substantial improvement in both thrust force density and power factor compared with conventional FR-PMLM. First, the machine topology and operation principle are introduced. Then, the thrust force generation mechanism under multi MMFs is analytically calculated based on MMF-permeance model. In addition, some electromagnetic performances, including open-circuit characteristics, thrust force performances and power factor are comparatively studied. It shows that the proposed AFR-PMLM with Halbach PM array can provide 7.2% higher average force than conventional AFR-PMLM under rated condition. Additionally, the power factor can be enhanced to more than 0.8 when the current density is 6 A/mm2.

articleTitle: A Comparative Performance Study of High-Speed SynRM and PMa-SynRM Rare-Earth and Rare-Earth-Less Permanent Magnets for Automotive Traction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper addresses a comparative analysis of high-speed Synchronous Reluctance Machines (SynRM) and Synchronous Reluctance Machines Assisted by Permanent Magnets (PMa-SynRM) of Ferrite and NdFeB magnets for automotive traction applications. The coils of these motors are subjected to high current densities, and liquid cooling is incorporated into their housing. Initially, a brief introduction to SynRM with and without permanent magnets is discussed. Subsequently, the paper presents the curves of the magnetic materials, which were characterized by the authors and utilized in the simulations. These motors are assessed through numerical simulations with a base speed of 6000 rpm and a maximum speed of 12000 rpm. At the end, electromagnetic results obtained through these simulations are presented, followed by their respective power and torque densities.

articleTitle: Analysis of Air-Gap Field Modulation Effect on Torque for 6-Slot 4-Pole High-Speed Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The air-gap field modulation (AGFM) effect on torque contributions for a 6-slot/4-pole high-speed permanent magnet (HSPM) machine is investigated and analyzed to illustrate its torque generation mechanism. Firstly, the permeance and magnetomotive force (MMF) model are deduced to analyze to identity the main-order working harmonics, and the Maxwell stress tensor (MST) method is employed to calculate the air-gap field harmonic electromagnetic torque and quantify the contribution of the main working field harmonics. Then, the influences of different stator parameters on the AGFM effect are studied and optimized to improve the torque density of HSPM machine. Finally, a 10kW 6-slot/4-pole HSPM machine prototype is fabricated and experimented to validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Efficient Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetization Switching with Low Current Density in Crystalline Ferromagnetic Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study explores spin-orbit torque (SOT)-induced magnetization switching in a ferromagnetic film of crystalline (Ga,Mn)(As,P) characterized by perpendicular anisotropy. The magnetization switching in the film is discerned through the hysteresis of Hall resistance (HR) during current scan measurements. The observed chirality in HR hysteresis aligns with the SOT generated by current-induced Rashba- and Dresselhaus-type spin orbit fields (SOFs) within the tensile strained (Ga,Mn)(As,P) film. As temperature increases, the critical current systematically diminishes, reaching a minimum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{J}\sim \mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{10}^{\mathbf{3}}\ \mathbf{A}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> at 65 K. This investigation reveals the feasibility of SOT-induced magnetization switching at remarkably low current densities in a single layer of ferromagnetic film, offering a novel avenue for the development of uncomplicated and energy-efficient spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Effect of Magnetostatic Interaction on the Single Domain Wall Propagation in Magnetic Microwires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We propose a novel method for effective control of the single DW propagation in a specially designed array consisting of two magnetic microwires by the stray field from magnetically softer microwires. We have experimentally demonstrated that the DW velocity of magnetically harder Fe-rich microwire in such linear array is affected by the stray field of magnetically softer Co-rich microwire. Additionally, the domain wall can be braked in the Fe-rich microwire by the stray field produced by Co-rich microwire in such linear array. Observed effect of magnetostatic interaction depends on position of Co-rich microwire in such linear array.

articleTitle: Investigation of Partially Oxidized Cu Capping Effect on CoFeB/Pt/CuOx Multilayers by Electrical and Optical Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Orbital Hall effect in light metals has attracted attentions recently, but research on the orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect and its inverse effect is relatively limited. In this study, we experimentally demonstrate the existence of both effects in CoFeB/Pt/CuOx multilayers. By conducting spin Hall magnetoresistance (SMR) and anisotropic magneto resistance (AMR) measurements simultaneously and calculating the ratio between them, we rule out the current shunt effect and conclude the surface oxidized Cu film contributes to the generation of orbital Hall currents, and these orbital Hall currents exhibit the same polarization as the spin currents generated by Pt. Our argument is further substantiated by the THz emission measurements which show that the effective spin diffusion length in Pt increases from 3.57 nm to 4.37 nm with the addition of CuOx. Our work provides further evidence to the hypothesis of interface related charge-orbital interconversion.

articleTitle: Conference Proceedings of the IEEE Magnetics Society Skyrmionic Synapse Implementation for Pattern Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Conventional neuromorphic computing faces the foreseeable limit of computational and power resources that can be mitigated by using spintronic-based devices. In this digest, we propose a 4-bit (16-state) skyrmion-based synaptic device for application in Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) consuming 0.971 fJ energy per weight update. Our proposed device offers compactness and scalability to higher bits. The skyrmionic synapse device is simulated using a micromagnetic simulation package(OOMMF) integrated with a software-based ReLU Max Pooled function to implement CNN for neuromorphic computing applications.
