We attained an accuracy of 98.15 % for pattern recognition on the MNIST handwritten data set.

articleTitle: Interface Phenomena and Magnetic Hyperthemia of Fe304 Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic hyperthermia studies were carried out on different sizes magnetic nanoparticles of iron oxide (7.3 nm (7IOMNp) and 9.5 nm (9IOMNp)). Heat properties were correlated with morphological, structural (Transmission Electron Microscopy and X-ray Diffraction) and DC magnetic (SQUID-Super Quantum Interference Device) by means of magnetization loops and magnetization curves as function of temperature measured in the protocol zero-field-cooling and field-cooling (ZFC and FC curves). Based on obtained, the linear response model validity was analyzed to better understand the effects of magnetic hyperthermia varing frequency and intensity of applied magnetic field.

articleTitle: Orbital Current Driven Magnetic Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Orbitronics is a newly developed field in spintronics with academic and industrial interests. Here, we for the first time demonstrate three-terminal magnetic tunnel junctions utilizing orbital Hall effect (OHE) as their main writing methods. The MTJ s were fabricated by a 200 mm spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory (SOT-MRAM) standard line. A critical switching current density of 0.61 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(10^{12} \mathrm{A}/\mathrm{m}^{2})$</tex>, or critical switching voltage of 0.37 V is realized. The effective charge-to-spin conversion efficiency of our Ru(12)/Pt(2) bottom electrode is determined to be 0.10 while its resistivity is as low as 32 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\Omega$</tex> ·cm, which is promising for integrating multiple MTJs on a same bottom electrode to optimize the footprint of SOT-MRAM. Our results pave the way for practical applications of orbitronics on magnetic memory.

articleTitle: Reducing Energy Waste by Tuning Martensite in Heusler Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Heusler alloys are widely studied due to their potential for practical applications, making use of their martensitic transformations. However, hysteresis is a long-standing drawback that reduces the chance of transferring these alloys from the laboratory to industry. In this work, we studied a Cr-doped Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa-based material designed by integrating data obtained from the previous phase and hysteresis diagrams taken from the literature, reaching Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.15</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.70</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Ga. The compound presents a magnetostructural transition at room temperature, with a ferromagnetic martensite phase, and moderate thermal hysteresis of approximately 4 K. The magnetocaloric effect was explored, showing a reversible entropy change higher than 8 Jkg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> under 0–5 T field change, an advance towards high reversibility for this family alloys.

articleTitle: Static and Dynamic Magnetic Properties in Layered Synthetic Antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Synthetic antiferromagnets (SAFs), consisting of antiparallelly coupled ferromagnets, are artificial layered magnetic structures that have been widely used in magnetic storage and sensing devices. In this work, we studied the static and dynamic magnetic properties of in-plane anisotropic SAFs with a repeated Py/Ru layers. It is found that both the magnetic hysteresis loop and ferromagnetic resonance spectra depend highly on the repeating period number. In particular, a plateau is observed in the hysteresis loop at small field region for even layer SAFs, which is resulted from the almost full cancellation of net moment. While a square shaped loop is obtained in the case of odd layer SAFs in the presence of structural asymmetry. More interestingly, the initially crossed acoustic and optical resonance modes in the bilayer SAF open up a gap in the spectra of trilayer case; and more resonance branches are observed with the increase of layer number due to the differences in static positions of the individual Py magnetizations.

articleTitle: A Novel Continuously Variable Magnetic Geared Dual Stator Hub-Motor for an E-Bike
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a continuously variable magnetic geared dual stator (CVMG DS) motor for a direct-drive electric vehicle (EV) hub-motor applications. The proposed design has combined advantages of the wide torque-speed characteristics of a synchronous motor and high torque density of a magnetic gear using a variable gear ratio. Further, design considerations, variable gearing effect, and preliminary results of the proposed motor obtained from 2-D finite element (FE) analysis are presented.

articleTitle: Ferromagnetic Behavior Induced bBy Structural Distortion in Pristine g-C3N4 Pellets Prepared via Isostatic Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is a two-dimensional (2D) material based on nonmagnetic atoms and shows many physical and chemical properties. In point of view of magnetic properties powder samples exhibits only a diamagnetic behavior. Otherwise, when we applied pressure on samples an intrinsic weak ferromagnetic behavior was observed at room temperature, where samples present coercive field and remanent magnetization. For understand this behavior we propose the coupling of the magnetic moments produced by pairs of spin ½ - spin ½ electrons located in a magnetic polarization plane due to an structural distortion observed through x-ray diffraction pattern. We assume that the magnetic moment comes from electrons in the π-bonding lattice, that, are affected by the deformation caused. The results found here are quite promising because of their advantages over materials that already have a magnetic moment at which lattice distortions control magnetic properties.

articleTitle: A New Radial Hybrid Consequent-Pole Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents a new permanent magnet vernier machine with radial hybrid consequent-pole (HCPMVM), which has the merits of high torque and low torque ripple. The PMVM is based on the theory of flux modulation effect, and the CP can effectively enhance the amplitudes of the modulation harmonics. Therefore, the utilization of the modulation harmonics can be maximized by selecting the appropriate the pole ratio and the torque can be effectively improved. However, CP tends to bring high torque ripple, which is caused by the different permeability characteristics of the PM pole and the iron pole. The HCP structure reduces the permeability difference by reducing the radial top height of the iron pole, and fills the PM to improve the air-gap flux density. Then, the geometrical configuration of HCPMVM is presented, together with electromagnetic performances are analyzed by finite element analysis. The analyzed results validate the employment of HCP can effectively improve steady torque and decrease torque ripple.

articleTitle: Development of a TR-MOKE Setup for the Investigation of Ultrafast Magnetization Dynamics in Magnetic Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Ultrafast magnetization dynamics study in nano-scale is nowadays an important field because of the increasing interest in magnetic storage systems, fast magnetic switching, and more over magnonic devices and spintronic devices. For this purpose, the study of spin wave dynamics along with ultrafast demagnetization is crucial. Time Resolved Magneto Optic Kerr Effect (TRMOKE) is a very efficient and non destructive experimental procedure to follow the study. Here in our work, we have established the microscopic TRMOKE setup in our lab with a dual-color pump-probe mechanism. We have experimental evidence of its success in producing magnetic Kerr signal with delay time. We used Ni thin film as ferromagnetic sample prepared in the EBV process.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Propagation in Multiconductor Submarine Power Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A comprehensive formulation for analyzing subsea cables in the frequency domain is introduced. This cable design encompasses multiple conductors, necessitating the resolution of a complex, coupled wave equation. To ensure accuracy and reliability, the derived results were rigorously validated against simulations conducted using PSCAD software.

articleTitle: Influence of Friction on High Speed Permanent Magnet Bearing Rings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: To build high speed magnetic bearings using sintered NdFeB magnets, it is necessary to assemble bandages with suitable interference by press-fitting. Here we investigate the joining process between titanium grade 5 bandages and sintered NdFeB magnets using finite element analysis (FEA) and experimental measurements with different friction. The coefficient of friction, µ is determined by measured and simulated force-displacement curves. Simulations show that the coefficient of friction between the joining parts strongly influences residual stresses in the magnet rings and subsequently the permissible speed of the magnetic bearings.

articleTitle: An Output-Fusion Fuzzy Logic Controller for Tumor Thermal Ablation Therapy System with Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Tumor thermal ablation therapy is a technology that uses high temperature to rupture tumor cells by the difference in heat resistance between normal cells and tumor cells. Among them, temperature control is particularly important for tumor thermal ablation therapy system with wireless power transfer. It will cause a lot of burden on the human body by exceeding the treatment temperature required for cautery, conversely, the purpose of cautery treatment cannot be effectively achieved. In this work, an output fusion fuzzy controller is designed. It includes a traditional fuzzy controller and two controllers which is also a fuzzy controller but be optimized for specific control performance indicators. According to temperature response changing, the output fusion fuzzy controller generates three output weights which correspond with three controllers for decision fusion, and then make the final output of controller include all advantages of three controllers at the same time. According to the experimental results, the output fusion fuzzy controller is significantly better than the traditional fuzzy controller in each control performance indicators.

articleTitle: Multiplanar Imaging with a Single-Sided MPI Scanner
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) is an emerging medical imaging modality with great potential for diagnostics and biopsy of cancer. Compared to the conventional closed bore scanners, single-sided device offers an open imaging volume, making it suitable for imaging larger subjects such as humans. Previously, we showed 1D and basic 2D imaging in a single plane with a manual rotation of rod phantoms. In this work we demonstrate multiplanar imaging capabilities of our scanner using filtered backprojection in the horizontal plane and the projection imaging in the vertical plane.

articleTitle: Thermal Spin-Current Generation in Bi-Substituted YIG Films with Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this study, we present a systematic investigation of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and spin dynamics in bismuth-substituted yttrium iron garnet (Bi:YIG) films grown on SGGG[111] substrates using pulsed laser deposition. The films' thickness ranges from 5 nm to 20 nm. Structural characterization, employing X-Ray Diffraction and High-Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy, shows that the film growth is epitaxial. All the films exhibit a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy component. Additionally, we analyzed the films by performing thermo-spin measurements in on-chip devices. Considering the device's geometry, we successfully quantified the spin Seebeck coefficient and the generated spin current within a Bi:YIG/Pt bilayer. The obtained value of the spin Seebeck coefficient is comparable to conventional YIG/Pt, affirming the potential of this material for efficient spin current generation as an insulating oxide with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Magnetic Ageing of Electrical Steel: Precipitates Impact on Magnetic Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this work, a high permeability grain-oriented electrical steel (HGO) was subjected to heat treatment to promote the magnetic ageing of the material. The magnetic properties, microstructure and precipitate formation of two samples, one with 38 ppm of C (sample 622A) and another with 18 ppm of C (256B), were investigate before and after of the heat treatment (ageing) at the temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{229}\pm \mathbf{3}\ {{}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}}$</tex>, which is approximately to that of power transformer operation. The magnetic loss of all samples in the frequency range from 10 to 60 Hz at 1.5 T was analyzed before and after annealing. It was found that there is an increase in magnetic loss in the heat treated samples, indicating the impactcof possible precipitates on the magnetization dynamics. Furthermore, the loss components (hysteresis, classical and excess) were determined as a function of frequency, and we observed that the hysteresis loss dominates at low frequencies (<50 Hz) and above this the excess loss becomes dominant, and this threshold is different for the two samples studied. This indicates that precipitates play a fundamental role in the movement of the material's domain walls, since excess loss is known to be associated with microcurrents induced by this physical mechanism.

articleTitle: Vortex Chaotic Dynamics in a Cross-Tie Domain Wall
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In high-sensitivity magnetic sensors, micro-sized magnetically-soft islands function as magnetic field detectors, featuring magnetic configurations composed of multiple domains, potentially containing cross-tie domain walls. Employing micromagnetics simulations, we examine the chaotic dynamics of a vortex within a cross-tie domain wall. We find that the vortex is confined within the domain wall, and it is continuously in core-reversal mode during relaxation or when driven by thermal excitation. This behavior contrasts with the 2D-free vortices which are more robust.

articleTitle: Variable Cross-Section End-transposed Rectangular Windings Based on Additive Manufacturing Technology for AC Loss Suppression in Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: High frequency AC loss in high-speed electrical machines reduces the efficiency, so it is necessary to study the AC loss in the windings. Additive manufacturing technology can realize high slot filling factor and design shaped profile windings. In this paper, a winding with variable cross-section and transposed structure based on additive manufacturing technology is proposed. By analyzing the distribution law of the magnetic density of the winding in the slot, an optimization method is designed to obtain the optimal cross-section parameters of the winding, thus effectively suppressing the AC loss of the winding.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Partitioned-Stator Hybrid Excited Permanent Magnet Arc Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: As a special motor, permanent magnet arc motor (PMAM) has a good application prospects in large telescopes and robot joints. In this paper, a partitioned-stator hybrid excited PMAM (PS-HE-PMAM) is proposed and investigated, which exhibits improved torque performances and good flux adjustment capability. The motor configuration and working principle of the investigated PS-HE-PMAM are firstly addressed. Then, the main structural parameters of the proposed motor are investigated and optimized for maximizing the torque and minimizing the torque ripple. Based on the optimal design, the electromagnetic performances of the four PS-HE-PMAMs with four different slot-pole combinations are fully investigated by using finite element (FE) method. Finally, the prototype of the proposed PS-HE-PMAM is built and experimentally tested to verify the effectiveness of the FE results.

articleTitle: Loss Analysis in Spoke Dual-Stator Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine Considering Stator Mutual Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The phase-shifted spoke array double-stator permanent magnet (DSPM) vernier machine has special merits for its high power factor, while the research on its loss influence principle is limited. In this paper, the mutual effect of stator phase shift on machine loss is revealed by the equivalent circuit based flux-pattern model. By the phase shift, both the ripple and average of the stator analytical air-gap length can be significantly reduced, which is the reason for the reduction of PM loss and rise of iron loss in the PSDSPM machine. And the proposed influence principle is verified by the comparison between PSDSPM and coincident DSPM (CDSPM) machine via finite element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: U-shape Magnetostrictive Harvester: Design and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Electromagnetic vibrational harvesters stand out due to their high-power density, long-life robust structure and low-cost design. Moreover, they can be designed using magnetostrictive materials. The mechanical vibrations cause stress on the magnetostrictive material, leading to variations in its magnetization. This, in turn, induces an electromotive force (EMF) in a well-designed pick-up coil system, thereby transforming mechanical energy into electrical energy. In spite of the potentiality of these electromagnetic harvesters, their practical implementation is limited due to the difficulties in the design optimization in terms of the device dimensions, effective stresses on the magnetostrive material, distribution and magnetic field strength of the permanent magnets and pick-up coil characteristics. Finite Element Methods (FEM) enable the estimation of the induced voltage and thus the output power as a function of harvester design parameters, allowing us to experiment with different configurations and identify optimal parameters.

articleTitle: Development of a Combined Maxwell's Equations and Magnetic Equivalent Circuit Solution for Induction Machines in Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study introduces a novel analytical technique for analyzing the magnetic field in induction motors (IM). This method combines Maxwell's equations with the magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) framework to determine flux densities in various regions of the motor. By integrating flux sources from Maxwell's equations into the MEC's network of reluctances, this method accurately considers the distribution of main and leakage magnetic fluxes within the motor. The approach significantly reduces analysis time while maintaining high accuracy and reliability when compared to numerical methods. Furthermore, it provides important motor features such as the radial and tangential components of the flux density in the air-gap, stator and rotor areas, as well as the induced voltage. Finally, to validate the accuracy of the proposed method, the analytical results are compared to the case that no leakage fluxes are included in the analytical model and to the finite-element method (FEM) in terms of computation time and accuracy. As such, this method is suggested to serve as a valuable analytical tool during the design process of IMs.

articleTitle: Tensile Stress Effect on Magnetic Barkhausen Noise of Silicon Steel Single Crystal (Measurements and Simulations)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: The Magnetic Barkhausen Noise (MBN) measurement can be used to evaluate non-destructively mechanical internal stress in electrical steel laminations. However such evaluation is complex as various factors can distort the MBN signal similarly. Internal stress is one of them, but an increase in dislocation density or other defects can be just as influential. This work focuses on single crystals with pre-determined crystallographic orientation to isolate basic mechanisms. The reconstructed MBN energy hysteresis cycles are compared to classical hysteresis loops, and to simulation obtained from a multiscale model. These comparisons provide new insights into the impact of tensile stress on the magnetization process and the magnetic domains kinetics and bring perspectives regarding the ideal way to perform MBN non-destructive evaluation of internal mechanical stress.

articleTitle: Microcoils for Magnetisation Reset in Stroboscopic Optical Pump-Probe Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Magneto-optical pump-probe techniques allow for the measurment of magnetic behaviours on femtosecond timescales. It is common in pump-probe setups for the sample magnetisation to be reset between pump-probe pairs using a continuously applied external magnetic field. Continuously applied reset fields can obscure aspects of the dynamics, particularly those relevant to the study of multiple pulse all-optical magnetisation switching. Here we introduce a pulsed microcoil device capable of magnetisation reset with tunable repetition rate. The pulsed-field induced switching is examined for magnetic multilayer and insulating magnetic garnet samples with out-of-plane anisotropy, and indicates the generation of fields up to 150 mT at frequencies up to 200 kHz.

articleTitle: Study of Disorientation in Polycrystalline Hexaferrites and Application to the Design of a Ka-Band Planar Self-Biased Isolator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Self-biased circulators and isolators require pre-oriented hexaferrites with a high degree of orientation in order to ensure a magnetization perpendicular to the plane of the hexaferrite sample. In this paper, a strontium hexaferrite is selected for this application. Angular Remanence Measurements and XRD are performed in order to quantify the distribution of magnetization directions in this polycrystalline hexaferrite. The extracted distribution law was used to develop a model to predict the evolution of remanent magnetization as a function of shape factor. This model is then used to design a self-biased isolator in Ka-band. Insertion loss of 0.85 dB at 38 GHz was demonstrated with a quite good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Using Nanocrystalline HDDR Powders in the Additive Manufacturing of Bonded Nd-Fe-B Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This study explored the application of high coercivity nanocrystalline powders in the additive manufacturing (AM) of bonded Nd-Fe-B magnets using two techniques: laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and stereolithography (SLA). The nanocrystalline powders were obtained through hydrogen decrepitation (HD) and hydrogenation disproportionation desorption recombination (HDDR) of Nd-Fe-B alloys. These high-quality powders were mixed with a binder and processed via LPBF and SLA to obtain bonded magnets. LPBF is a popular technique due to its design flexibility and reduced material waste. On the other hand, SLA also shows promise in producing bonded magnets, although there is limited literature on this topic. The impact of HDDR and AM processing parameters on the magnetic properties and microstructure of the powders and magnets was investigated. We were able to successfully produce isotropic HDDR powder with coercivity values up to 850 kA/m, and also bonded magnets via LPBF and SLA with various binder fractions, while maintaining the high coercivity of the HDDR particles. Exploring different AM techniques paves the way for the development of smart magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Losses in Composite Material Transformer Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: By altering the material of the transformer core, the operational characteristics can be improved. A composite material transformer core, composed of amorphous alloy and silicon steel, has been developed to harness the loss characteristics of these two materials. Previous research on this composite material has primarily focused on experimental results, with limited understanding of the mechanisms behind its composite loss characteristics. This study investigates the variations in losses of the composite material transformer core. Derivation of the calculation equations for hysteresis losses and eddy current losses in the core, which includes both materials, is presented. The changes in normal magnetic flux density at the interface of different materials are analyzed. The findings of this research provide valuable insights for experimental design of loss characteristics in composite material structures and core design.

articleTitle: Magnetotransport Properties and Spin Textures in Gd5Ge4
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We report on resistivity, magnetoresistance and Hall effect experiments in the magnetocaloric compound Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. Measurements were carried out in several temperatures in magnetically ordered state and in the paramagnetic phase. Attention is also given to the temperature domain where a Griffiths-type phase was identified. The resistivity versus temperature experiments are strongly dependent on thermal and magnetic cycling of the sample. These results indicate a polyfleration of microcracks in the sample under cycling or the occurrence of a phase separation phenomenon. At the low temperature limit the magnetoresistance is positive and dominated by the spin-mixing effect. In the intermediate temperature range the magnetoresistance is negative and reaches giant values. The Hall effect at low temperatures shows a peaked contribution that suggests the occurrence of a field-induced transition from the antiferromagnetic ground state to a ferromagnetic ordering. In the paramagnetic phase, the ordinary Hall effect is hole-like.

articleTitle: Effect of Synthesis Method and Calcination Temperature on the Physical Properties of Ni-NiO Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: We investigate the structural, morphological, chemical, and magnetic properties of Ni-NiO nanocomposites synthesized through two distinct routes, sol-gel and coprecipitation, followed by calcination. By considering several techniques we show that the resulting nanocomposites, as well as their properties, are strongly dependent on both, synthesis method and calcination temperature. Hence, we explore the possibility of tailoring the physical properties of the nanocomposite by modifying production parameters. The results place the employed routes as a simple, low-cost candidate to the production of Ni-NiO nanocomposites, especially nickel oxide.

articleTitle: Overload Capabilities of Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this contribution the overload capabilities of synchronous machines are analyzed. Overload operation has an important impact on different aspects of the design of electrical machines, and it is very important to identify electromagnetic designs helping an easier operation. The study is conducted based on a general equivalent electric circuits modeling, with normalized quantities and parameters, applicable to all types of synchronous machines (wound field synchronous machines, permanent magnet synchronous machines, hybrid excited synchronous machines, and synchronous reluctance machines). The tools developed for the study are provided. These analyses will help identify parameters sets allowing an easier overload operation of synchronous machines for variable speed applications, as electrical traction.

articleTitle: MTJ Based NV-SRAM Macro with Enhanced Read Margin and Low Static Power in FDSOI Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: This paper presents a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) based non-volatile static random access memory (nv-SRAM) macro with dual working modes, SRAM mode and magnetic random access memory (MRAM) mode. The self-body biasing scheme is proposed to improve the read margin in MRAM mode. By using 55-nm FDSOI process, simulation results show that the read margin in MRAM mode is increased to at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times$</tex> compared with the conventional MRAM, and the static power is decreased to about 30% of the conventional SRAM.

articleTitle: Disproportionation and Recombination Reactions - a Promising Technique for Producing Sintered Nanostructured Anisotropic SmCos Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A review of literature data on the features of hydrogenation, disproportionation, desorption, and recombination (HDDR) in the SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>-based ferromagnetic alloys is presented. It was found that the disproportionation reaction occurs at relatively low hydrogen pressures of 0.2-0.5 MPa during 2–5 h. The starting alloy decomposes into SmH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and Co in the case of conventional HDDR, and into SmH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, Co and Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf> phases in the case of solid HDDR. During the recombination reaction the SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> phase appears at a temperature of 700°C and reaches its maximum amount at 950 °C. The microstructures of materials after disproportionation and recombination reactions are nanoscale. The materials are anisotropic after HDDR treatment if they contain the ferromagnetic phase residues after the disproportionation reaction. For the first time, it has been demonstrated that SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>-type materials can be sintered using the HDDR method at temperatures as high as 950°C. Sintered materials have nanocrystalline microstructure with very low porosity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\leq \mathbf{0.8}\%)$</tex>. It was found that the after-sintering treatment of SmCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>-based magnets by the HDDR technique enables the achievement of high magnetic properties, namely coercivity.

articleTitle: Magnetism and Spin-Orbit Coupling in Iron Cbalcogenide Superconductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A prominent feature in iron-based superconductors is the strong interplay between superconductivity, magnetism, and spin-orbit coupling, which are key ingredients to promote topological states for fault-tolerant quantum computing, including Majorana zero modes (MZMs). While MZMs have been reported recently in FeTe0.55Se0.45, the topological features, magnetism, and superconductivity are found not uniformly across samples. Here, we discuss transport measurements and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to characterize the electronic states in a series of (Fe, Ni)Te0.55Se0.45, Substituting Ni on the Fe site modifies spin-orbit coupling. We found Ni substitution lowers the superconducting transition temperature and changes the electronic structure and related topological properties. Our investigations suggest the presence of superconductivity and other competing ground states in (Fe, Ni)Te0.55Se0.45 Thus, the ground state control appears to be a prerequisite for the use of MZMs in quantum applications.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Elasto Optic Dynamic on Co/Pt Multlayers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Thin Co/Pt multi-layers with a Pt cap-layer were grown with different capping layer thickness (3 nm< d <20 nm) over a Si02/Si substrate in order to stabilize the perpendicular anisotropy, as well as to control the spin pumping process. On the other hand, Pt layer enhance the damping factor for the magnetization relaxation. Also the Pt capping layer, form a cavity that may be used to generate coherent phonons wave. We show by time resolved spectroscopy, the magnetic relaxation damping rate and the phonon waves properties in these Co/Pt multi-layers.

articleTitle: Nanoribbon of Zigzag Silicene for Spin Field Effect Transistor with Low Voltage Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: A novel two-gate Spin-Field Effect Transistor (Spin-FET), employing Silicene nanoribbon with a mirror version z-shaped zigzag structure, as the channel material is modelled and assessed in this study. The proposed design of Spin-FET device is highly compatible with CMOS technology, enabling the creation of both n-type and p-type devices combining parallel and anti-parallel modes of Spin-FET. The device's feature size is in sub-4 nm range, making it suitable for cutting-edge integrated circuit technology. It offers enhanced “ON” current, reduced power consumption and parasitic capacitances, which are essential for high-frequency and low-power applications.

articleTitle: Electronic Structure and Magnetic Properties of the Full Heusler Alloys Mn2YAl (Y = Fe, Co, Ni)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: In this theoretical study, we investigate the electronic structure and magnetic properties of the full Heusler alloys Mn2YAI for late 3d transition metals, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Y}=\text{Fe}$</tex>, Co, Ni, in the framework of first-principles calculations. These alloys are crystallized in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> -Mn-type crystal structure. We investigated the electronic structure and magnetic properties within the DFT method with PBE pseudopotentials. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Mn}$</tex> -crystal structure was modeled with antiferromagnetic orderings of the Mn magnetic moments. Our calculations demonstrated that these alloys have metallic properties and a ferrimagnetic ordering with high values of the magnetic moments on Mn.

articleTitle: Fe2MnSn Heusler Alloy Based Rare-Earth-Free Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short papers (INTERMAG Short papers)
abstract: Considering the vast compositional space of Heusler alloys, first-principles-based calculations are ideally suitable for predicting the ground state structure and tailoring the magnetic properties of these alloys. We perform density-functional-theory-based calculations for step-by-step identification of the most stable phase of Fe2MnSn, followed by the calculations of magnetic properties. Ferromagnetic hexagonal phase is identified to be the stable structural phase of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnSn with a large magnetization <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{6.45}\ \mu_{B}/\mathbf{f}.\mathbf{u}.)$</tex>, high Curie temperature (729 K) but with an in-plane magnetic anisotropy. On doping with light interstitial atoms (B, C, H, N and O) an out-of-plane anisotropy can be engineered with enhanced magnetic properties, making this material suitable for permanent magnet applications.
